/
/
/We are the Waseda University Hawaiian Folk Dance Society, commonly known as Wasehula, the only officially recognized hula dance club at Waseda University!
/
/
/
/Celebrating our 20th anniversary this year, we’re a group of about 80 female Waseda students who practice in the Student Union Building during the 4th and 5th periods on Tuesdays and Fridays.
/
/
/
/In addition to our summer performances, Waseda Festival, and solo shows, Wasehula also participates in university-sponsored events, as well as performances at Spa Resort Hawaiians and in Hawaii!
/
/
/
/We warmly welcome anyone who wants to try hula dancing, loves Hawaii, loves dancing, enjoys being active, or wants to try something new!

/

/
/
/To all new students! Let’s bring a breath of Hawaii to Waseda together!!

名前: Waseda University Yosakoi Team Tokyo Hanabi
活動内容:
We are a Kochi-style Yosakoi team—a rarity among student teams!
/
/
/
/Kochi-style Yosakoi is characterized by dancing in a parade format while holding naruko clappers. We pride ourselves on our graceful performances, which blend powerful male movements, elegant female movements incorporating fans, and the interplay of the matoba (banners).
/
/
/
/Once a year, we create a performance where we handle everything ourselves—costumes, music, choreography, and MC—and participate in Yosakoi festivals across the country, including the Kochi Yosakoi Festival, to showcase our work.
/
/
/
/We get along very well regardless of grade level, and in a warm, friendly atmosphere, we practice diligently every day while taking our dancing seriously!
/
/
/
/If you want to try something new, are looking to commit to something wholeheartedly, want to meet wonderful friends, or simply love to dance… don’t worry—even if you’ve never danced before, you’re welcome! Most of our members started with no prior experience!
/
/
/
/Why not join us as a “Hanabi-ko” and bring smiles to audiences on stages across the country!! Let’s enjoy the final chapter of your college life together!!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday & Saturday / 7:00 PM / Student Union Building and surrounding university facilities

活動内容:
We perform at various events throughout the year, including freshman welcome shows, Waseda Festival, the Waseda-Keio Rivalry Match, and the JDC (Japan Dancer’s Championship). We also hold a large-scale solo performance every September.
/
/
/
/One of SesSion’s major attractions is our highly polished showcases. For each event, we create the choreography, staging, costumes, and music from scratch, and we practice daily to continuously improve together.

/
/
/At this year’s JDC, we advanced from the Kanto preliminaries in first place, and at ALL JAPAN (All Japan Street Dance Championship), we placed third nationally in the intercollegiate showcase contest.

/
/
/In recent years, more club members have been taking on dance battles. Whether you want to have fun dancing with everyone in a showcase or challenge yourself to improve your skills, SesSion is a great place where everyone can engage with dance in their own way.
/
/
/
/Another appealing aspect is our welcoming, family-like atmosphere where we maintain a serious attitude toward dance while cherishing the bonds with our fellow members! As an intercollegiate club, we have a diverse group of members—both Waseda students and students from other universities—who come together to have fun!

/
/
/If you’re serious about dance, join SesSion!

/If you’re serious about enjoying college life, join SesSion!
/

Please check our X and Instagram for information about TAP-LOVERS. If you have even the slightest interest in tap dance, please come check us out!! We’ll lend you shoes if you come for a trial session. Just bring comfortable clothes and come on over! Please contact us via email or similar before coming to practice.Please check the schedule for upcoming practice dates! TAP-LOVERS welcomes members from their second and third years of university. In fact, many students start with us in their second or third year. If you want to learn a new skill or make the most of your college life, feel free to join us anytime!

We practice three days a week—primarily Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays—at studios and cultural centers in Tokyo in preparation for our annual main performance, the new student welcome performance, Waseda Festival, and other events. We are also recruiting male students and students from other universities!If you’ve always wanted to try ballet, had to quit due to entrance exams, want to dance with peers, or are looking to take on a new challenge, now is your chance to start! Whether you love ballet or just want to dance, please join us! A performance created entirely by students is sure to be an unforgettable memory! Why not experience the thrill of a performance created by everyone together?

活動内容:
Good morning! We are "Gettapaz," Waseda University's dancing geta group!
/
/
/
/As the world's only "dancing team wearing geta," we perform not only at university events but also at major festivals across the country, including in Niigata and Kyoto. We also host our own unique solo performances every year at Okuma Auditorium, bringing smiles to many people every day!
/
/
/
/Although “Gettapaz” might appear to be part of the “Yosakoi” genre due to our dazzling traditional Japanese costumes, we set ourselves apart by wearing “geta” (wooden sandals) instead of “naruko” (clappers) and by not performing traditional chants.
/
/
/
/Furthermore, since many of our members are beginners and don’t specialize in any particular dance genre, we may be quite different from a typical “dance club.”
/
/
/
/But that is precisely what makes “Geta-Paz” so appealing!
/
/
/
/Our geta performances aren’t bound by “experience” or “genre”; we prioritize entertaining the audience by simply enjoying ourselves. “Geta-Paz” embodies the true spirit of Waseda’s “performance clubs.”
/
/
/
/Has anyone here ever danced in geta? That’s right—literally everyone starts as a beginner. Here, there’s definitely a chance for anyone who wants to take the stage.
/
/
/
/There are so many friends we’ve met because of geta, sights we’ve seen because of geta, and memories of our youth we’ve gained because of geta. College life only comes once. Why not put on your geta with us?

/
/
/In addition to our Wednesday group practices, we have lessons on Saturdays taught by a professional belly dance instructor. /

/
/If you want to learn to love yourself just as you are, try something new, find something to get passionate about, or improve yourself, we look forward to shining on stage with you!

名前: Waseda University Cheer Dance Team MYNX
活動内容:
Hello.
/
/
/
/We are MYNX, Waseda University’s only cheer dance club, celebrating our 12th anniversary this year! Our members are all Waseda students.
/
/
/
/“Become the best in the cheer dance world”
/
/“Dance cheer with mutual passion at our beloved Waseda”
/
/These are our two main goals, and we work toward them every day.
/
/
/
/We compete in tournaments like the JCDA and USA Championships about two or three times a year, seriously aiming for national dominance, while also performing in solo shows and at events both on and off campus!
/
/
/
/Sparkling cheerleaders, cheerleaders of sweat and tears. At MYNX, you can be both!
/
/Absolute beginners are more than welcome!
/
/
/
/Let’s enjoy a fulfilling college life together through cheer dance!
/
/
/
/If you’re even slightly interested, please check out our official social media accounts listed on this page.
活動日時・場所: 5 days a week (Mon, Tue, Wed, Fri, Sat) / 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM / Sports facilities near the university

活動内容: We are Waseda’s only flash mob club. A flash mob is a performance where performers, disguised as ordinary people, suddenly start dancing in the streets, surprising and moving those around them. It’s often used for proposals, birthday celebrations, and wedding surprises! No dance experience is necessary! Beyond dancing, you can showcase your “individuality” through instruments, singing, or anything else!We welcome passionate people who are motivated to make others smile, those who want to try something new at university, and creative individuals eager to build a performance from scratch! Be sure to search for “Waseda University Flash Mob Club” on YouTube. One look and you’ll be hooked on flash mobs! Why not join us in sweeping others up in a whirlwind of surprise and excitement?
活動日時・場所: When we have a project, we meet twice a week on Mondays, Wednesdays, or Fridays after the 5th period at facilities around Waseda (subject to change depending on the project)

活動内容: The Waseda Michael Jackson Research Society is an officially recognized Michael Jackson cover dance club at Waseda University. We typically practice for stage performances at events like the Waseda Festival and our own solo shows, as well as hold events related to Michael Jackson. Beginners and experienced dancers alike, Michael Jackson fans, fans of Western music, and even those who aren’t—everyone is welcome! Most of our members started dancing in college.Additionally, the M-Ken accepts new members year-round, regardless of year level. If you join the M-Ken, you’re guaranteed to master a special skill that will get you noticed by everyone! You’ll even be able to do the Moonwalk. If you’re even slightly interested, please check out the M-Ken’s official social media accounts (YouTube, Instagram, X, etc.) to see our performances. Whether you want to make the most of your college life or start learning a new skill now, everyone is welcome to come check us out! We look forward to your messages via DM.
活動日時・場所: At least twice a week (once on weekdays, once on weekends) / 5:00 PM – 6:40 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
We work hard every day with the goal of winning the UNIDOL idol cover dance competition.
/
/
/
/We perform cover dances of a wide range of idols, primarily from Hello! Project, as well as Cheeky Parade, Stardust, the 48 Groups, Heroines, and others.
/
/
/
/In addition to competitions, we also perform at Waseda Festival, our own concerts, and various events.
/
/
/
/We generally meet three times a week (two weekdays and one weekend day).
/
/
/
/Regardless of seniority, everyone gets along like family.
/
/
/
/Anyone with a passion for dancing is more than welcome. We recommend this club to those who can focus on a single goal and work hard together.
/
/
/
/As an officially recognized club, we can practice in the Student Union Building, which helps keep costs for studios and other facilities down.
/
/
/
/Also, since we’re an intercollegiate club, members come from a wide range of universities, allowing you to expand your social circle.
/
/
/
/We also engage in creative activities such as designing costumes and creating background videos.
/
/
/
/We’re recruiting not only dancers but also backstage staff.
活動日時・場所: Generally every Tuesday, Friday, and Saturday at 7:00 PM at the Student Union Building

活動内容: Hello! we are the Kpop perfect-cover dance team,Twinkle! Twinkle is a K-POP cover dance circle that values “perfectness”. We not only cover K-POP idol dance, but also strive to copy their outfits,facial expressions, and how they dance! Our main performances are the freshman welcoming event in April, in-circle performance in May and, independent show in August and February, and the Waseda Festival and farewell performance in November. We also upload videos on YouTube and TikTok! Announcements for our performances will be made via Twitter and Instagram, so make sure to follow us :) Apart from our independent performance, we also participate in events and competitions outside the University. In the past, our girls team and boys team won the 1st place in a K-POP cover dance competition on August 2022. We are a circle of diverse students with a common purpose. Let's dance Kpop! Our circle has not only Kpop groups' fans, but also people who love songs and want to start dancing. If you want to join the dancing, please come to the welcome practice (新歓, Shin-kan). If you want to enjoy watching our performance, please visit our Youtube channel, Twitter, Instagram, and Tiktok! Looking forward to seeing you soon!!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday日, Saturday日/19:00から22:00/Student Center, studios in Tokyo

名前: Waseda University Cheer Dance Team MYNX Tokorozawa Branch
活動内容: Hello! We are the Waseda University Cheer Dance Team MYNX! We are an all-female cheer dance team dedicated to two main goals: becoming the idols of Waseda University and reaching the top of the cheer dance world! Cheer dance is a competitive sport that combines four dance styles: pom dance (dancing with pom-poms), hip-hop, jazz dance, and line dance! We practice four times a week in the Takadanobaba area. In addition to participating in on-campus events, we also perform solo shows at the Okuma Memorial Hall and appear at the Waseda Festival. We compete in two annual competitions with the goal of winning the national championship. Our team consists of 20 Waseda women, regardless of experience level. If you’re looking to get involved at Waseda, this is the place to be! Why not start cheering—something you’ll love—right here at Waseda?
活動日時・場所: 4 days a week / 6:00 PM / Takadanobaba area

活動内容: Bankarism - Multicoloredism - is a Waseda University school uniform acrobatics troupe that operates under the philosophy of “igniting the ambition in everyone.” For those who are dissatisfied with their current situation, those harboring inner turmoil, or those living with a sense of unease.We want to be a source of inspiration that gives these smoldering individuals the push they need to take a new step forward. With this in mind, we perform unconventional acts that blend acrobatics and dance. By “acrobatics,” we mean performances that draw on each individual’s unique personality and flair. For example, at Bankarism, we consider not only nunchaku, batons, and acrobatics, but also video editing and calligraphy to be forms of acrobatics.We respect each member’s strengths and individuality, and to prove that anyone can shine, we perform on various stages both on and off campus. We hold recruitment events only in the fall, following the Waseda Festival. We’ll be posting updates on our official Instagram, so please check there. We hope you’ll come see us perform!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Thursday 7:00 PM–9:30 PM / Saturday 10:40 AM–1:30 PM

活動内容:
"Waseodo," the Waseda University Dance Circle, is an intercollegiate dance club that was officially recognized last year and is now entering its 12th year!
We meet twice a week, and our main events include stage performances at the Waseda Festival and two club-wide live shows held each year.
On a regular basis, we practice in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere while teaching each other dance techniques!
One of Waseodo’s biggest appeals is that you can freely choose any genre or song to dance to—whether it’s J-POP, K-POP, Vocaloid, or anime songs!
Whether you want to dance to existing choreography or create your own, what you dance is entirely up to you.
We also have many members who are beginners, students from other universities, and those joining in their second year or later, so everyone is welcome!
Whether you want to start dancing in college, love making “dance covers,” or are looking for friends who share your interests, why not join Waseodo and help create the best stage performances together?
活動日時・場所: Every Thursday and Saturday at 6:00 PM / Dance studio in Tokyo

活動内容: Hello, this is the Aikido Club! We are the only group at Waseda University affiliated with the Aikikai (the organization directly descended from Morihei Ueshiba, the founder of Aikido), and we are the oldest and largest Aikido club at Waseda University. While many people imagine intense competitions when they hear the word “martial arts,” Aikido does not determine superiority through competition! We practice techniques repeatedly, adjusting to each other’s skill levels, so even women who aren’t confident in their strength can feel free to join. (By the way, our gender ratio is 6:4.) Ninety percent of our members started practicing Aikido in college. Under the guidance of high-ranking instructors, we start with the basics, including proper falling techniques, so even beginners can participate safely and with peace of mind. You can join for as little as one day a week out of our six weekly practice sessions, and all our practice locations are within walking distance of the university.Since it’s easy to balance with classes, studying, and part-time jobs, students from a wide range of departments—regardless of whether they’re in the humanities or sciences—are members. Why not join us and train with the Aikido Club? You can join at any time, so please feel free to contact us!
活動日時・場所: Mon, Wed, Thu / 4:45 PM – 6:15 PM / Aikido Headquarters Dojo; Tue / 6:30 PM – 9:30 PM / Edogawabashi Gymnasium; Fri / 3:20 PM – 4:50 PM / Aikido Headquarters Dojo; Sat / 12:20 PM – 3:20 PM / Shinjuku Cosmic Center

活動内容: Our Kyudo Club practices once a week under the guidance of high-ranking instructors. Although there are two Kyudo clubs at Waseda University, we get along well and interact with each other. Club members are dedicated to their daily practice and have achieved excellent results in dan and kyo examinations as well as in shooting competitions against other university Kyudo clubs.On our days off, we go out to have fun or grab drinks; during free periods between classes, we hang out at our hangout spot, and afterward, we often eat "Wase-meshi" together—we see each other frequently even outside of practice. Why not join us and spend your college life with us?
活動日時・場所: Every Sunday / Hamadayama Archery Dojo

活動内容: We usually practice with instructors from the Shinjuku Kendo Federation. Our members range from beginners to experienced practitioners, and since participation in practice sessions is optional, everyone can train at a level and schedule that suits them. Senior members provide careful guidance to beginners, so even those starting kendo in college can feel at ease.We participate in about 10 tournaments a year, including friendly matches, and consistently achieve top finishes. Upon joining our club, you automatically become a member of the Shinjuku Ward Kendo Federation, allowing you to earn dan ranks through our club and compete in Shinjuku Ward tournaments. During the spring and summer breaks when there are no matches, we hold kendo training camps, spending a fulfilling off-season focused solely on practice.In addition to kendo, we frequently hold various fun events such as ski camps and social gatherings to strengthen the bond among members. On the other hand, we do not hold practice sessions during exam periods, making it possible to balance kendo with your studies, part-time jobs, and activities in other clubs. Let’s enjoy a fulfilling student life together in the Kendo Club!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday / 6:30 PM / Shinjuku Sports Center, 4th Floor, Second Dojo

活動内容: We, the Karate-do Seishinkai, are a traditional karate club celebrating our 54th anniversary this year.We are officially recognized by Waseda University as a "Student Club" and are classified as a Division II athletic club. Currently, we have about 30 members in their first through third years. Our members range from those with over 10 years of karate experience and those who have competed in the National High School Championships to those who started karate in college. Regardless of style, background, gender, or university, we all train together in a friendly and harmonious atmosphere.We belong to the “Wadokai” school, one of the four major traditional (light-contact) karate styles. Since we follow light-contact rules, women and beginners can participate with peace of mind (the gender ratio is roughly 1:1, and about half of our members are beginners). We hold practice three times a week at the Student Union Building on the Toyama Campus, and while we aim for participation at least once a week, members train at their own pace.During regular practice, everyone trains together on everything from basics to kata and kumite. Before tournaments, which are held once every one to two months, we focus our training on the specific events each member will compete in. Additionally, members who wish to do so can attend the Wadokai Arakawa Dojo—an All Japan Karate Federation-affiliated dojo—for free, and beginners can aim to earn a black belt while still in school.Centered around three regular practice sessions per week and three training camps per year, the club members get along very well and enjoy university life in a friendly, family-like atmosphere, organizing activities beyond karate such as summer festivals, trips, and snowboarding camps.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday / 5th period (Saturdays: 4th and 5th periods) / Student Union Building

活動内容: To everyone looking for a club: Why not join us and fill your days with karate!? Nice to meet you—we’re the Waseda Karate-do Shito-kai, an officially recognized Waseda University karate club! When you think of karate, you might picture “the quintessential Japanese martial art” divided into “kumite” (sparring) and “kata” (forms), where competitors showcase the beauty of their movements. However, karate was recognized as a new Olympic sport in 2016 and is now an incredibly popular “international sport” with over 100 million practitioners worldwide, particularly in Europe and the Middle East!! If you search for “karate” on YouTube, you’ll be amazed by its global popularity and just how cool it looks! Also, since we practice traditional karate with protective gear and use light contact, it’s very safe. Whether you’re an experienced practitioner from another style, a complete beginner, a student from another university, or an international student, we all have a great time together—practicing karate, hanging out in the club room, hosting events, and going out for fun! We practice every day after school from Monday to Saturday, and since you can train as much as you like in your free time, even beginners can become skilled enough to earn a black belt and place highly in tournaments! There are plenty of opportunities to interact with other universities and compete in tournaments, so it’s a great environment for experienced practitioners to improve their skills too! Plus, the gender ratio is 1:1, so female members can train with peace of mind! There are no annual fees, and the Shito-kai is always accepting new members, so if you’re interested in joining—whether you’re a freshman or not—please feel free to contact us!! Let’s practice karate together!!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday–Saturday / 4:30 PM–6:00 PM / Student Union Building, Club Room

名前: Waseda University School of Science and Engineering Judo Club
活動内容: The Waseda University School of Science and Engineering Judo Club brings together a diverse group of people, from beginners to elite judoka, who train diligently every day toward their individual goals. These goals vary widely, ranging from addressing a lack of exercise due to entrance exams to achieving higher dan ranks.The club’s overarching goal is to win the “Nine-School Tournament,” a competition held twice a year. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced practitioner, whether you have a specific goal or are just curious—anyone who wants to practice judo in college is welcome!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday and Saturday / 7:00 PM – 9:00 PM / Shinjuku Sports Center

活動内容: The Sagittarius Archery Club is an officially recognized club at Waseda University and Jissen Women’s University, celebrating its 45th anniversary this year. In addition to practicing once or twice a week at archery ranges such as the Shinjuku Sports Center, we participate in exchange matches with other universities and various events. Guided by the spirit of “enjoy, archery!”, we value a relaxed approach to archery and encourage open participation in the club.Most members of Sagittarius started archery in college. Upperclassmen, experienced archers, and instructors from the archery range will teach you from the very beginning, so even if you’re a complete beginner, you’ll be just fine! Of course, experienced archers are also very welcome! There is no obligation to attend practice. Furthermore, there is absolutely no pressure to go out drinking. We hope you’ll participate in the club however you like. But it’s more fun if you join in often! ☆
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday & Sunday / 4:30 PM / Shinjuku Sports Center

活動内容:
Welcome to the Protective Gear Karate Club! We’re a club that welcomes both beginners and experienced practitioners alike—even if you’ve never exercised before, you can earn a black belt in just two years. We know many of you are probably wondering, “What is protective gear karate?” so here’s a brief explanation.
/
/
/
/・It is a form of traditional karate with a long history.
/
/・Its defining feature is sparring while wearing protective gear, allowing you to fight with all your might without worrying about injuries.
/
/・The powerful and spectacular kata performed from a solid foundation are a must-see!
/
/
/
/The Appeal of the Protected Karate Club
/
/・Beginners are very welcome! We have many members who started with no prior experience.
/
/・Both men and women can thrive here. You can start competing in matches right after reaching green belt (the rank after white belt).
/
/・We’re always recruiting new members! We welcome students from all grades at any time of the year, so please feel free to contact us.
/
/・We’re a club with a 50-year tradition. You’ll receive careful guidance from alumni who hold black belts.
/
/・Our training focuses on building genuine strength. Without a strong foundation, a true karateka cannot be born.
/
/・International Students Welcome! Another feature of our club is that we have many international students!!
/
/
/
/Recommended for people like this!
/
/・Those who want to try karate but are intimidated by clubs with many experienced members.
/
/・Those who feel anxious about joining flashy or overly busy clubs.
/
/・Science and engineering students who want to meet people with similar interests.
/
/・Those who want to join a new club but aren’t sure where to start.
/
/・Those who want to try something different from what everyone else is doing.

名前: Waseda University Mind-Body Unification Aikido Club
活動内容: An intercollegiate Aikido club recognized by the Waseda University School of Science and Engineering. We hold practice sessions approximately twice a week at the Shinjuku Cosmic Center, located next to the Science and Engineering Campus. Members include not only students from the School of Science and Engineering, but also students from the humanities, graduate students, and students from other universities. Most members are beginners in Aikido, and we practice in a friendly and harmonious atmosphere with the goal of earning a black belt within two years.Our practice schedule is designed to accommodate the busy lives of science and engineering students, so it’s okay if you can’t make a session due to classes or other commitments. Training for promotion is tailored to each individual’s pace, so even if you have no prior athletic experience, there’s no need to worry. In addition to holding training camps in the spring and summer, we organize various social events and activities outside of Aikido practice. “Work hard when we work, and play hard when we play!”—this balance between dedication and fun is what defines our club!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday & Friday / 4:40 PM – 6:40 PM / Shinjuku Cosmic Center

活動内容:
The Sports Aikido Club is an officially recognized club with over 30 years of tradition. We meet 3 to 4 times a week in the basement of Building 17 at Waseda University.
We practice with the goal of participating in tournaments and promotion exams several times a year. One of our main selling points is that participation is voluntary—not just for tournaments and exams, but for regular practice as well—so there’s little pressure, and everyone can train at their own pace! Since almost everyone starts aikido in college, we believe it’s easier to get started here than in other sports clubs.
Everyone can enjoy it regardless of gender or athletic ability, and it’s possible to earn a black belt in as little as a year and a half.
We warmly welcome not only freshmen but also upperclassmen!
Many students start in their second or third year. The Sports Aikido Club also welcomes students from other universities, so please feel free to join us! If you’re even slightly interested in Aikido, please contact us via social media or stop by the dojo (B1 of Building 17)! All of us in the club look forward to seeing you!
活動日時・場所: Weekday schedules vary by semester; Saturdays 12:30 PM–2:40 PM / Building 17, Basement Level 1, Aikido Dojo

活動内容:
Honjin is an intercollegiate Kyudo club founded in 1984. Our members include not only Waseda University students but also students from various other universities. We enjoy a friendly, family-like atmosphere and have fun practicing together every week, teaching each other and striving to improve our skills. We welcome both experienced archers who want to continue practicing Kyudo in college and beginners who want to start.
/
/
/
/ We practice twice a week (three times a week only during university long breaks), renting out a dedicated archery hall for our sessions.During the university semester, practice is held on Fridays and Sundays; during long breaks, it is held on Wednesdays, Fridays, and Sundays. On Fridays, we practice at the Sumida Ward Kyudo Hall, and on Wednesdays and Sundays, we use the Koto Ward Sports Hall. In addition to regular practice, we regularly participate in shooting competitions organized by the “Kanto Kyudo Club Federation,” hold exchange matches with partner clubs, and conduct practice matches within the club.We are also affiliated with the Tokyo Kyudo Federation’s Second District, allowing us to take dan promotion exams and participate in adult archery competitions. Additionally, we hold intensive kyudo training camps twice a year in May and August. Beyond these camps, we organize various events such as skiing and snowboarding trips and BBQs, making this a club where you can make friends to enjoy university life with! Participation in practices, camps, and events is optional, so you can participate at your own pace.
活動日時・場所:
Every Friday / 5:30 PM – 9:00 PM / Sumida Ward Kyudo Hall
/
/Every Sunday / 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM / Koto Ward Sports Hall
/
/Every Wednesday / 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM / Koto Ward Sports Hall (Only during extended breaks in February, March, August, and September)

活動内容: The Doshikai is a Tomiki-ryu Aikido club based at Waseda University’s Tokorozawa Campus. Founded in the same year as the School of Human Sciences, we have shared a history with the school ever since. We’re not a large club, but that makes for a cozy, family-like atmosphere! Most members start Aikido in college! One of the attractions is that you can earn a black belt in as little as a year and a half.Furthermore, the Tomiki-ryu style features randori (sparring) similar to judo, allowing you to learn more practical techniques! You can join our practice sessions as little as once a week. In addition to practice, we hold various events and regular social gatherings. No forced drinking or chanting—none of that! We take practice seriously, but we know how to have fun when we’re out and about. Whether you’re serious about training, new to Aikido, or not very athletic, everyone is welcome—regardless of gender or athletic background! Please come check out the Doshikai!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Tuesday, and Friday / 4:30 PM – 7:00 PM / Tokorozawa Campus Second Sports Hall

活動内容: We are the only mixed martial arts club at Waseda. We practice a sport called "Kudo," which involves wearing protective gear during matches, allowing anyone to train safely and become stronger. We have a proven track record, including producing national championship winners, and we continue to train daily to achieve victory in competitions. Mixed martial arts can be broadly divided into striking, throwing, and ground techniques. By practicing each of these, we hone our skills so that we can use them exactly as intended in actual combat.Furthermore, since Kudo is a "martial art" derived from Kyokushin Karate, we place importance not only on physical conditioning but also on mental growth. This club is highly recommended for those who want to try something new at university or for those who wish to continue participating in sports. Additionally, many of our members belong to other clubs as well, allowing them to balance both social activities and sports. If you are interested, please visit our website.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday / Student Union Building, Shinjuku Sports Center, etc.

活動内容: We, the Waseda ITF Taekwondo Club, are the only officially recognized taekwondo club at Waseda. Most of our members had no experience with martial arts or combat sports before entering university. Beginners and those with no prior experience in combat sports are welcome.We hold practice twice a week, on Wednesdays and Saturdays. Additionally, about once a month, a black belt instructor comes to teach us. During these sessions, you can receive authentic, high-level instruction that’s a bit different from our regular practice. The club atmosphere is relaxed yet serious about training. Whether you want to get serious about martial arts, just want to get some light exercise, or are looking to lose weight, this club caters to all goals. Come join us and hone your elegant kicking techniques.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday & Saturday / 5:00 PM – 8:35 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: In a nutshell, "Taido" is a new martial art that blends karate and gymnastics! Since its founding in 1965, it has spread to dojos and universities across Japan. A distinctive feature of this martial art is the inclusion of acrobatic movements, such as backflips and somersaults, within its kata.In kumite (sparring) competitions, you can witness versatile kicking techniques executed from unique stances, as well as the mysterious footwork known as “Unsoku,” which allows for precise control of distance! Since most members start in college and are taught by instructors with over 20 years of Taido experience, beginners are more than welcome! Through tournaments held several times a year, we actively interact with Taido clubs from other universities, providing ample opportunities to make friends.Members balance practice with classes, studying, other clubs, and part-time jobs. They get along very well—organizing events like snowboarding retreats—and enjoy university life in a warm, welcoming atmosphere. We accept trial sessions and new members year-round, so please feel free to join us!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday / Wednesdays and Thursdays: 6:30 PM – 9:00 PM at a nearby junior high school / Saturdays and Sundays: Various times around the Waseda Campus

活動内容:
Hello! We are the Waseda University Iaido Club.
/
/
/
/The Iaido Club is a student group where members learn iaido techniques using Japanese swords and hone their skills individually. Although we use "Japanese swords," they are actually replica swords with blunted blades, so they are safe and secure. Once you decide to join, the first step is to order your own sword. You can customize and purchase a sword to your liking, including the scabbard, tsuba (guard), and blade pattern!
/
/
/
/We study "Musō Jikiden Eishin-ryū"—one of the largest schools within Iaido—and "All Japan Kendo Federation Iaido" under the guidance of Master Atsumi Hatanaka, a 8th-dan Kyoshi. We joined the East Japan Student Iaido Federation in 2010.There are few schools affiliated with the East Japan Student Iaido Federation that practice Eishin-ryu, making ours the first university in the East Japan region to adopt this style.
/
/
/
/Many students start practicing iaido in college; in fact, the majority of our club members began in college. Some students even start in their second year.
/
/
/
/Since there is generally no physical contact with opponents, even those with little athletic experience can get started. Furthermore, as it is an individual sport, you can practice at your own pace. If you have any questions or find something difficult, our upperclassmen, fellow members, and instructors will be happy to explain it to you in detail whenever needed.
/
/
/
/Please check out our Twitter and Instagram to get a feel for the club’s atmosphere! We welcome visitors, trial participants, and new members year-round, regardless of your year in school! We look forward to hearing from you anytime♪
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, Saturday, or Sunday… Yotsuya Hiroba (Yotsuya 3-chome) / Every Friday… Student Union Building
Every Monday & Wednesday / 7:00 PM – 9:30 PM / (Mon) Ikebukuro Daiichi Elementary School (Itabashi Station) / (Wed) Meihō Junior High School (Senkawa Station)

活動内容: We meet once a week on Sundays for horseback riding lessons or to ride horses in nature. Many members are complete beginners, though some have considerable experience. We operate on a flexible schedule where you can participate at your own pace whenever you want or have time, making it easy to continue without feeling pressured.The gender ratio is 2:8, with more women, but the members get along very well, and we often organize dinner parties and drinking gatherings. As a long-established club, we also value opportunities to interact with our alumni. Even members who previously had no interest in horses have come to discover the joy of riding after hearing stories and advice from our seniors. We also hold training camps three times a year, which are packed with activities aimed at improving riding skills and enjoying leisure time together.Recently, more members have been taking the initiative to plan activities outside of the club, motivated by a desire to improve their riding skills or get to know their peers better. As a club whose motto is “Everyone having fun,” we are truly delighted to see this.
活動日時・場所: Every Sunday / 2:00 PM / Sanyo Garden (Riding Arena)

活動内容: The Waseda Marine Yacht Club is a group that enjoys sailing in Enoshima every Sunday!Do you know what a yacht is? A yacht is a boat that sails using the power of the wind. Since you sail while feeling the breeze, you can experience a sense of oneness with the magnificent ocean off Enoshima! If the weather is nice, you can even see Mount Fuji while sailing! Furthermore, sailing isn’t just for fun—it also has a competitive side as a sport. Once you get used to handling the yacht, you can even compete in national tournaments!In fact, some of our club members have even placed in the top ranks at the All-Japan Championships. Some of you might be thinking, “I’ve never even seen a sailboat before, so I’m nervous,” or “I’m not a strong swimmer, so I’m hesitant about water sports…” But there’s absolutely no need to worry. First of all, almost all of our members are beginners who started sailing in college. You’ll practice under the guidance of our alumni, so you can learn to sail in a fun and supportive environment!Also, we always wear life jackets on the yacht, and there’s a rescue boat nearby just in case, so you can feel safe even if you’re not a strong swimmer. Besides sailing, we also go out on cruisers, have barbecues on board, and enjoy Enoshima—there are plenty of fun activities! Why not give sailing a try? We hold trial sessions, so please join us! We’re waiting for you at Enoshima Harbor!
活動日時・場所: Every Sunday / 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM / Enoshima Yacht Harbor

活動内容:
Windsurfing is a water sport where you glide across the water using the power of the wind. You ride on a board that resembles a surfboard with a sail attached.
/
/
/
/We compete for rankings by rounding two marks—one upwind and one downwind. Aiming to win the Intercollegiate Team Championship, we practice at Yuigahama on Saturdays and Sundays.
/
/
/
/We often hear people say, “I’m worried because I’m a beginner,” but nearly 100% of people who take up this sport start as beginners in college, so don’t worry. Also, even if you can’t swim, wearing a life jacket is mandatory, so you’ll be fine.
/
/
/
/We currently have a track record of winning the Intercollegiate Individual Championship and placing in the team competition. Even if you start in college, with enough effort, you can become the best in Japan!Furthermore, first-year students are treated as beginners and compete in races exclusively for beginners, so you can make an impact right from your first year!!
/
/
/
/The club has a great atmosphere, and you’ll get along well not only with your peers but also with the upperclassmen. During long holidays like summer and spring break, we go on training camps to places we wouldn’t normally visit, such as Lake Saiko, Lake Motosu, and Lake Hamana.Starting in your second year, you’ll also have the opportunity to go windsurfing in Okinawa. Furthermore, through races and practice sessions, you’ll make friends with athletes from other universities, allowing you to build a network of friends not just in the Kanto region, but across the entire country.
/
/
/
/If you’re looking to take on new challenges in college or are serious about sports, this is the perfect activity for you.
/
/
/
/Why not join the Waseda University Windsurfing Club and get fired up as we aim to become the best in Japan during your final years as a student?
活動日時・場所: Regular practice every Saturday and Sunday; voluntary practice on weekdays / 9:00 AM–4:00 PM / Sakashita, Kamakura; Yuigahama

活動内容: We are the oldest existing ski club at Waseda University. All members are Waseda students, and our membership is diverse, ranging from the School of Political Science and Economics to the School of Science and Engineering and the School of Sport Sciences, and even includes graduate students. We focus on the ski season during winter and spring breaks, training hard at training camps and participating in competitions.During the off-season, we hold training sessions twice a week to get in shape for the upcoming season. We also have plenty of events, such as trips to the beach, fireworks displays, and attending various Waseda-Keio rivalry matches. Many members balance their activities with their studies and part-time jobs, and some are also members of athletic clubs or multiple other clubs. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced skier, we all enjoy skiing together! Even if you’re trying skiing for the first time since entering university, you can improve, and those with prior experience can take their skills to the next level.
活動日時・場所: Twice a week / 5:00 PM / Toyama Park

活動内容: With a history spanning over 50 years since its founding, this ski club boasts one of the largest membership bases in the country. The club includes not only seasoned competitors who excel at national tournaments but also many beginners with no prior experience in snow sports. We train daily with the goal of winning championships. We are currently on a five-year winning streak in the men’s overall category at the All-Waseda Tournament! We are truly one of Waseda’s premier ski clubs in both name and reality.During the off-season, we strengthen both body and mind and deepen our bonds with teammates through weekly optional training sessions, special events, and summer training camps. We have no inactive members, and all 100 of us are able to participate in activities year-round without ever getting bored. In winter, we primarily hold training camps at ski resorts such as Oze Iwakura, Sugadaira, and Hakuba Iwatake, and compete in the National Championships and the All-Waseda Tournament in March. If you want to lead a passionate college life that beats anyone else’s, Suga is the place for you!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday–Friday / 4:50 PM / Toyama Park

活動内容:
During the off-season, we hold numerous events to strengthen bonds among members, such as BBQs, fireworks festivals, and camping trips. To improve skiing skills, we organize training camps, including inline skating camps and grass skiing camps. During the season, both groups receive instruction from professional coaches and can improve their skills by participating in the National Student Championships and the All-Waseda Championships.We have the opportunity to work as live-in staff at ski resorts across the country, and interacting with resort guests and instructors is a valuable experience you won’t find anywhere else. Even beginners can reach a level where they can take ski proficiency tests by the end of the season.
/
/Our clubroom is located in the Student Union Building, and it’s always bustling because you’re sure to run into someone whenever you stop by. Since training sessions are held daily, it’s possible to balance club activities with studies, part-time jobs, and other clubs. We value the close bonds among members as well as our connections with alumni.
/
/This is a club where everyone can have fun, regardless of their skiing experience.
活動日時・場所: Once a week / 4:30 PM / Toyama Park & Club Room (Student Union Building E301)

活動内容: Although 90% of Zermatt’s members are beginner skiers, we work hard every day to improve our skills by having fun exercising during weekday training sessions and receiving easy-to-understand instruction on basic skiing theory from our seniors. During winter training camps, we practice with full dedication while receiving instruction from coaches. As a result, both our men’s and women’s teams have grown to the point of winning the National Student Iwatake Ski Competition and the All-Waseda Ski Competition. Of course, the off-season isn’t just about practice.Every Sunday, we organize events like BBQs and bowling tournaments, and we always give our all to having fun too. Through these events and training sessions, you’ll get to know everyone and make lifelong friends. Zermatt’s strength lies in the bonds we build during the off-season, which become the driving force for the upcoming season.Play with all your might, train with all your might—and at the end of that journey lie the best memories you can only gain at Zermatt. To make the most of your one-and-only college life, Zermatt continues to give it our all today!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday–Friday / 5th period / Nishitoyama Park

活動内容: During the off-season in summer, we have fun training by playing various sports near the university. Participation is optional, so it’s easy to balance with your studies or join other clubs! We also have plenty of fun events, like group BBQs and road trips! In winter, we train hard at training camps held in Hokkaido and Nozawa Onsen in Nagano Prefecture, and compete in tournaments! Participation in training camps is generally optional, and you can choose your own schedule.You can practice at a pace that works for you, balancing your budget and other commitments! Springboard is open to beginners—we’d love to have you! Professional coaches and experienced upperclassmen will guide you from the very beginning, so you’ll improve quickly. Equipment is available for rent. Let’s enjoy college life together! We look forward to hearing from you anytime.
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday & Friday / 6:30 PM / Toyama Park

活動内容: We are affiliated with the All-Waseda Basic Ski Federation. We ski with all our might in the winter and host plenty of events in the summer! We are the only basic ski club that participates in all three of Waseda’s major events: the 100-Kilometer Hike, the Waseda-Keio Rivalry Match, and Waseda Festival. During the off-season, we hold twice-weekly training sessions to build stamina and practice off-piste training. We also host events twice a month, such as takoyaki parties and amusement park outings.In the winter, we hone our skills with the goal of competing in the Iwatake Student Tournament and the All-Waseda Tournament! Both beginners and experienced skiers are very welcome. We even have members who used to compete in alpine skiing. During training camps, we receive instruction from coaches, and even when we’re not at camp, our upperclassmen provide careful guidance. You can aim to place in tournaments even if you start in college! We’re known for our great club atmosphere, so please come check us out!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Friday (plus one Saturday per month) / 5:00 PM / Nishitoyama Park & Student Union Building Room E831

活動内容: We are a Waseda University-recognized ski club founded in 1978! We are affiliated with the All-Waseda Basic Ski Federation. The name “Belle” comes from the French word for “beautiful,” though French majors say it’s a bit odd or something… (lol).During the season, we hold three training camps in December, February, and March. We split into several training groups and learn to ski from upperclassmen and coaches. The December camp features ski proficiency tests (Levels 1–3), the February camp hosts an internal competition, and the March camp features the AW Tournament.Even outside of training camp periods, members can compete in national ski competitions held at Iwatake or work as instructors at ski schools. Rumor has it that some members, driven by their love of skiing, spend nearly two months holed up in the mountains…! During the off-season, we hold training sessions three times a week (Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Saturdays during 5th period) in front of the Shinjuku Sports Center. We generally build up our stamina through light activities like tag and long rope jumping.Also, once a month, the planning committee organizes an event for everyone to enjoy. In the past, we’ve had BBQs and road trips—we always have a lively, fun time together! During Golden Week, we hold a welcome retreat (at Shiga Kogen), and during summer break, we go to the beach or the mountains for a retreat. Beginners are more than welcome! You can enjoy skiing in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere! Please come check us out sometime!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday / 4:30 PM / In front of Shinjuku Sports Center

活動内容: During the off-season, we get pumped up with training, inline skating, and lots of events, and once the season starts, we dive into skiing in full-on serious mode! Basic is the only club where you can start from zero athletic experience or as a complete beginner and go on to compete nationwide.The bonds you forge with your teammates by overcoming long training camps and rigorous team practice are unique to Basic—something you can’t experience through any other part of college life. Of course, it’s not all hard work; we know how to have fun like college students should! Even though we’re serious about skiing, we go on road trips, visit islands, have social gatherings, and even celebrate Coming-of-Age Day. Enjoying college life is another hallmark of Basic. Whether you’ve worked hard before or not, everyone will experience the ultimate sense of accomplishment during their college years!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday & Saturday / 5:30 PM– (Saturdays start at 3:30 PM) / Toyama Park next to the Nishi-Waseda Campus

活動内容:
Why not make diving your lifelong hobby?
/
/
/
/The Underwater Club is a group centered around diving that operates in locations such as Okinawa, the Ogasawara Islands, and the Izu Peninsula. Our main events include biannual long-term training camps, short-term camps, and day trips for diving. The experience of spending extended time with friends on a tropical island, combined with the hobby of diving, is sure to become a lifelong treasure! Let’s go explore the remaining 70% of the world together.
/
/
/
/In addition to diving, we organize outdoor activities tailored to each member’s interests, making this a club that never gets boring all year round!
/
/
/
/★What Makes the Underwater Club Great★
/
/◎Passion
/
/Every member loves diving. We’re a club where diving is a regular part of our lives. With plenty of underwater cameras, you’ll end up with tons of Instagram-worthy photos! There are no mandatory events, and while we’re a small group, our participation rate is high—and we have zero “ghost members”! ?
/
/
/
/◎Peace of Mind
/
/The Underwater Club has been around for 55 years. We have long-standing relationships with numerous dive shops, accommodations, and dive service providers that have supported us for decades. Additionally, the club is sustained by members with extensive diving experience. Seniors provide solid support, so even beginners will be just fine!
/
/
/
/◎Variety
/
/Since we decide which island to visit together each time, the Underwater Club has a wide reach and offers the chance to experience various islands! We also hold training camps in the fall and spring, and day trips are organized regularly. Beyond diving, members enjoy traveling and going skiing together with their diving buddies. We even have a club room, so campus life is fulfilling too!?
活動日時・場所: Irregular / Okinawa, Izu, etc. / Clubroom available

活動内容:
We are an officially recognized swimming club with over 50 years of history, known as “Hayamizukai.”
/
/
/
/We practice three times a week at the Takaishi Memorial Pool on the Toyama Campus.
/
/
/
/Our members range from national competition veterans to complete beginners, so everyone is welcome.
/
/
/
/Whether you haven’t swum in a while or want to learn how to swim, please come check out Hayamizukai.
/
/
/
/We offer not only competitive swimming but also water polo, so if you’re interested in that, please come join us.
/
/
/
/We have many events planned, including BBQs, training camps, and open-water swimming competitions, so stay tuned.
/
/
/
/If you have any questions or concerns, please don’t hesitate to contact us.
/
/
/
/We look forward to meeting you all.
活動日時・場所: 3 times a week (days TBD) / 2nd period / Takaishi Memorial Pool (Toyama Campus)

名前: Waseda University Finswimming Team SIX BEAT
活動内容:
Finswimming is an aquatic sport where participants wear fins and compete for the best time. SIX BEAT has members ranging from beginners to members of the Japanese national team. We warmly welcome both those with competitive swimming experience and those who have never swum before. Our regular activities take place during the first period from Monday to Saturday at the Takaishi Memorial Pool on the Toyama Campus. Participation in practice is optional, so you can join in according to your own schedule.
/
/
/
/In addition to competing in finswimming competitions, we have plenty of fun events, such as summer training camps and Christmas parties!!
/
/
/
/Please check out SIXBEAT on Instagram. We’re also actively recruiting managers. You’re welcome to come watch a practice at the Takaishi Memorial Pool anytime!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday–Saturday, 1st period, Takaishi Memorial Pool

名前: Waseda Mountain Biking Club WFR (School of Science and Engineering Mountain Biking Club)
活動内容:
Activities:
/
/WFR is an officially recognized club that organizes activities such as mountain biking (MTB) and snowboarding. Currently, there are two divisions: the Mountain Biking Division and the Snowboarding Division. You can join both divisions or just one—it’s up to you. While MTB and snowboarding can seem intimidating on your own, joining WFR means you can enjoy them as much as you like, as long as your schedule allows!!
/
/
/
/・MTB Division
/
/MTB is a sport that uses bicycles specifically designed for riding on unpaved mountain trails. WFR is the only MTB club in Japan. We ride through mountain trails in the Kanto region and MTB courses set up at ski resorts during the green season. From off-road cycling to reach our destination to pulling off spectacular jumps on kickers, you can experience a wide range of fun!
/
/
/
/・Snowboarding Division
/
/WFR’s snowboarding division, “WGTA (Waseda University Grand Trick Association),” is a club dedicated to freestyle snowboarding. By the way, freestyle snowboarding is a riding style where you enjoy tricks like jumps and spins on ordinary slopes.Rather than renting out a house for days on end—what’s often called a “retreat”—we mainly go on short trips to hit the slopes. That’s why we recommend WGTA to busy people or those with unavoidable commitments during spring break.
/
/If you’re interested, please send us a message via the URL below.
活動日時・場所: Ski resorts (both winter and green season) and mountains near the Kanto region / Once a week

活動内容: What comes to mind when you hear “traveling by bicycle”? Some of you might think, “That sounds fun,” while others might think, “That sounds tough” or “It looks physically demanding.” It’s true that riding a bicycle for several days straight is no easy feat. Yet, we ride because the joy of finishing a ride together with our friends is simply irreplaceable.And every time we experience a training camp or a day trip, we find ourselves wanting to pedal toward a new destination. Why not join us on a cycling journey? If you’re interested, feel free to knock on the door of the E327 clubroom. We also share our activities on our website, blog, X, and Instagram, so please check them out. All of us in the club look forward to cycling with you.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday / 4:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: Our main activity is training camps. We take advantage of the long summer and spring breaks to go on cycling camping tours—to Hokkaido in the summer and to Shikoku and Kyushu in the spring. The camps last about a week. Since there are many members, we split into groups to travel and then meet up at the campsite. We change the group composition every day.We usually hold meetings every Wednesday during the 6th period in the Student Union Building or classrooms. At these meetings, we discuss training camps and various events. Events include sports activities, Christmas parties, monthly runs, and alumni gatherings. Additionally, starting in the 2014 academic year, we began operating a food stall at the Waseda Festival. As you can see, we engage in many activities beyond just cycling, and we constantly come up with new ideas to keep our members entertained.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday / 6:15 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Mountain Alkou Club is an officially recognized mountaineering club at Waseda University. We are active year-round, focusing on long-distance summer treks, winter mountaineering, and events at our club-owned mountain hut! During our main event, the summer training camp, we spend around 10 days climbing mountains in the Northern Alps, Southern Alps, Hokkaido, and Shikoku.The sense of accomplishment from completing the summer training camp is indescribable! Since 70–80% of our members started mountaineering in college, if you’re thinking about trying something new at university—or if you were in a high school mountaineering club—we look forward to welcoming you!
活動日時・場所: Anytime, Student Union Building E413

活動内容:
Our club is officially recognized by Waseda University and belongs to the "Student Association," a group reserved exclusively for clubs with a proven track record. There are no joining or annual fees! We also have our own dedicated clubroom in Room E306 of the Student Union Building. Founded in 1954, we boast one of the longest histories among Waseda’s many clubs.As we celebrate our 70th anniversary, we are continuing our activities to further explore the joy and depth of "fishing."
/
/
/
/We typically organize monthly outings on boats or from piers. We also set up a booth at the Waseda Festival and hold several retreats each year, including a club-wide orientation retreat (with a proven track record at locations such as Izu, remote islands, and managed fishing grounds). Please check our blog for more details on our activities.Furthermore, by making fishing buddies through spontaneous outings on weekends or after class, you’re sure to broaden your fishing horizons more than ever before!
/
/
/
/Even if you’re a complete beginner who’s never fished before, or if you’re interested but hesitant to start because it seems intimidating or you lack knowledge, our senior members will guide you through everything from buying gear to actually fishing, so please feel free to reach out.We also organize trips to offshore breakwaters, remote islands, and rocky shores, so even seasoned anglers with years of experience can enjoy themselves! In addition to fishing, we host events like drinking parties and BBQs. We accept new members year-round, so if you’re interested or would like to ask questions, please feel free to contact us via X (Twitter)! We look forward to hearing from you!
活動日時・場所: Anytime / Student Union Building E306, or anywhere there are fish

活動内容: The Mountain Club is an all-Waseda mountaineering club. In the summer, we go on tent treks in the Japanese Alps, do canyoning, and rock climbing; in the winter, we climb snow-covered mountains and go skiing. We engage in a variety of mountaineering activities throughout the year. Participation in each activity is not mandatory, so you can also join just for hiking or summer mountain treks.For activities involving risk, experienced upperclassmen and alumni provide guidance. Thanks to financial support from alumni, we have a well-stocked supply of high-cost mountaineering gear available for loan in our club room at the Student Union Building. Mountain activities are scheduled only on weekends or during long breaks, so even those busy with classes or part-time jobs can participate. Additionally, on weekdays, we hold seminars on mountaineering and training sessions at climbing gyms. Since many members started mountaineering while at university, both beginners and experienced climbers are very welcome.We welcome students in their second year and above. Since we don’t hold many drinking parties, those who don’t drink alcohol can join with peace of mind. If you’re interested in mountaineering, please join us!
活動日時・場所: Saturdays, Sundays, and as scheduled / Mountains & Student Union Building, 3rd Floor, Room E338

活動内容: We, the Waseda Rovers (Boy Scouts Shinjuku 2nd Troop), currently have 27 members (including those from other universities). Throughout the year, we engage in outdoor activities such as camping, overnight hikes, and ski camps, as well as community service projects centered around the Shinjuku area (including the Tokyo Marathon, Sumida River Fireworks Festival, and Meiji Shrine Bonfire Festival).As Waseda’s only Boy Scout club, we actively engage in exchanges with Scouts of the same age. Whether you’re experienced or a beginner, we warmly welcome anyone looking to start in college—including students from other universities! If you’re even slightly interested, please contact us via Instagram, Twitter, or other social media!
活動日時・場所: Varies by activity

活動内容: The Travel Club is an all-Waseda travel club celebrating its 64th year in 2023. With the goal of taking trips that can only be experienced as a college student, we travel to various locations throughout Japan. We form bonds with friends that can only be forged through repeated journeys together. We go on trips once every one to two months, but participation is generally optional! Don’t want to have regrets about your college life? Want to make true friends? We’re waiting for all of you who love travel and the outdoors!!
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule. We have a club room in Student Union Building E324.

活動内容: The Gakubun-kai is an outdoor club focused primarily on mountain climbing. Beginners and women who aren’t confident in their physical fitness are welcome! From spring through summer, we start with simple outdoor activities like BBQs and camping, then gradually work our way up from hiking low mountains around 1,000 meters to full-scale summer mountain climbs of around 2,000 meters to acclimate our bodies.Our main event is the summer training camp held every year in late August, where we traverse the Northern Alps—a range of mountains over 3,000 meters high. We also organize various other outdoor activities throughout the year, such as trips to Okinawa and ski camps. Gakubun-kai currently has over 100 members, but since we get to know each other through our monthly events, you’ll never find yourself not knowing a fellow member’s face or name! Our clubroom in Student Union Building E303 is always bustling with members, who often go out to eat or hang out together.Another key highlight is our weekly meeting held every Friday during 6th period (6:15 PM–) at the Student Union Building. Since all members gather there, it’s a great opportunity to get to know everyone on a deeper level! Despite our large membership, we have a close-knit, family-like atmosphere. We welcome students from other universities as well as Waseda students, so please feel free to drop by! Every Friday, 6th period (6:15 PM–)
活動日時・場所: Every Friday, 6th period (6:15 PM–)/Student Union Building

活動内容: The Walking Club organizes a variety of events, including mountain climbing, hiking along historic trails, casual strolls through Chinatown and Kamakura, and cycling trips. Most club members are beginners with no prior experience in activities like mountain climbing. The Walking Club offers a wonderful opportunity to travel to various parts of the country, enjoy local cuisine, and make friends with the locals. Members get along very well, and during the winter when outdoor activities aren’t possible, we hold drinking parties several times a week or hang out in the club room.
活動日時・場所: Weekends

活動内容:
The Historic Sites and Landmarks Research Society (Meiko-ken) is an officially recognized travel club with a history spanning over half a century since its founding. Meiko-ken’s activities can be broadly divided into three categories: training camps, regular meetings, and individual projects.
During training camps—Meiko-ken’s main events—we travel throughout Japan. There are up to six training camps per year, and participation is entirely voluntary.During summer break retreats, we travel on a rotating basis through Hokkaido, the Chugoku and Shikoku regions, and Kyushu, aiming to circle the entire country over a three-year period. During spring break retreats, we focus on Kyoto and tour the Kansai region. In addition, we hold short-term retreats, such as overnight trips, to visit areas near the Kanto region.
Regular meetings are held every Tuesday and Thursday during the academic term. We discuss topics of our choice or play games. The atmosphere is always relaxed and laid-back.Many members participate once a week, either on Tuesdays or Thursdays, and attendance is flexible. The more you participate, the better you get to know each other, which helps deepen our bonds.
Personal projects are events where members freely plan activities they want to do and enjoy them together. Many of these are day trips, such as mystery-solving, barbecues, and road trips, and they are an important part of Meikoken’s activities, second only to the retreats.
Meikoken has a long history, but its form continues to evolve, making it a very flexible club. Above all, it’s laid-back and relaxed. It’s also easy to join as a dual member. Whether you’re already a travel enthusiast or just want to start traveling more, please come join us! Let’s go on trips with the best friends!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday & Thursday / 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Nobu Club goes hiking mainly on weekends and during long breaks! We organize a wide range of trips, from day hikes to two-day tent camping trips and summer training camps. Many of our members started hiking in college, so beginners are more than welcome! We’ll work together to improve our skills with the goal of summiting the Northern Alps during our summer training camp. The sense of accomplishment from reaching the summit, the breathtaking views, cooking meals together… Let’s create lifelong memories with the Nobu Club!As an intercollegiate club, we have members from various universities. Unusually for a mountaineering club, we have a high percentage of female members, so please feel free to come check us out. We also have plenty of activities beyond hiking, such as island trips and ski camps. Joining Nobu is guaranteed to be the best part of your college years! Be sure to check out our social media to see what we’re up to. For our recruitment events, we’re planning a Zoom information session and a recruitment hike. Membership is limited to participants of these events, so we look forward to seeing you there!!!
活動日時・場所: Weekends and holidays (flexible schedule), optional participation, in the Kanto region and the Japanese Alps

活動内容: Hello!! We are the Waseda University Mountain Hut Research Society!! Commonly known as “Yamaken,” we are an outdoor club focused primarily on mountaineering. We are an officially recognized club at Waseda University and are celebrating our 57th anniversary this year since our founding in 1969. Most of our members are beginners!! Let’s enjoy mountaineering together with our diverse group of friends, each with unique backgrounds from completely different high school experiences!!We hold joint training camps in spring, summer, and fall, where the whole club goes hiking together. We also have a full lineup of events throughout the year! Additionally, the club owns a mountain lodge, and we visit it several times a year. We don’t climb in the winter because it’s too dangerous. Instead, we have plenty of recreational activities during the winter, such as ski camps!! We highly recommend this club for anyone looking to try something new in college! Of course, experienced hikers are also very welcome. Climb a little, play a little. We hope this club becomes your second home!
活動日時・場所: Every Friday / 6:00 PM / Plan-tan (a coffee shop near the main campus)

活動内容:
[Basic Activities]
We primarily go on day hikes, though we sometimes go on overnight hiking trips during our summer camps. We also organize other outdoor activities, such as barbecues and ski camps! Since we decide on our activities based on member suggestions, we can make your dreams come true—whether it’s the mountain you want to climb, the place you want to visit, or the activity you want to do!
[Frequency]
We aim for a schedule of three hikes per month and one event per month.There are no mandatory activities; you can participate freely by voting each month on the days you’d like to join!
【Members】
T.E.A. is composed of students primarily from Waseda University, Hosei University, and Japan Women’s University, so you’ll have the opportunity to interact with people from various universities.
Many of our current members started hiking in college, so if you love nature, you’re more than welcome—regardless of your experience level!
We also welcome students in their second year or higher to join.
【Activity History (2025 Academic Year)】
April: Mt. Takao, Mt. Jinba
May: Yamanote Line Loop Hike, Mt. Takao, Tomin no Mori, Mt. Otake
June: Chichibu Sightseeing, Nishizawa Valley Hike, General Meeting
July: Mt. Hyuga, BBQ
August: Summer Camp (Alpen Route), Watermelon-Splitting Contest, Mt. Nikko-Shirane, Hanno Hike
September: Tomin no Mori, Mt. Kagenobu, Sports Day
October: Mt. Jinba, Halloween Party
November: Mt. Tsukuba, Hakone Sightseeing
December: Christmas Party, Year-End Party
January: New Year’s Shrine Visit
February: Ski Camp, Ice Skating Competition

活動内容: Orienteering is a sport originating in Northern Europe that combines "mental agility" with "running ability." Participants read maps in the forest, filter information, navigate their way, and compete to see who can complete a set course in the shortest time. Simply being fast isn’t enough to reach the top; there is a depth to the sport that allows even those who aren’t fast to win.We, the Orienteering Club—commonly known as OC—take on this challenge together, bringing together everyone from those who simply enjoy the outdoors to those who compete internationally as members of the Japanese national team. Our regular activities include running and map-reading workshops, and on weekends we head out to participate in orienteering events.Due to the nature of the sport, we often hold events in forests and other natural settings, so our trips often double as excursions—making it perfect for those who love the outdoors and travel! Unfortunately, since it’s classified as a minor sport, we frequently collaborate with university students from all over Japan, not just Waseda, allowing us to make friends nationwide through orienteering. We welcome anyone with a spirit of adventure, curiosity, and a desire to take on new challenges—whether you want to start a new sport in college, love maps, travel, or the outdoors, or aspire to compete on the world stage!

Our members come from a variety of sports backgrounds, not just the swimming or track and field teams, but also soccer and baseball. Even students who were part of non-athletic or cultural clubs in high school have successfully completed triathlons! The sense of accomplishment after crossing the finish line is indescribable!
/
/Since North is an intercollegiate club, we also have members from universities other than Waseda! Managers are also very welcome!
/
/People often think of triathlons as grueling sports, but there are races that can be completed in about an hour. We also recommend enjoying triathlons by combining them with travel and sightseeing at races held in various regions! Plus, some students compete in events other than triathlons, such as swimming, road cycling, and marathons! How you enjoy it is entirely up to you!
/
/The best thing about North is that it’s a free-spirited and cheerful group!We have a diverse group of members, ranging from those competing in the Japanese National Championships and winning prizes at the Intercollegiate Championships to those whose goal is simply to finish the race. But everyone gets along great and trains together whenever you visit, united under the slogan, “It’s now or never!” During your four years of college, you can balance club activities with other priorities like studying, part-time jobs, and studying abroad! Since we’re a club, practice is optional! Why not choose North to make the most of your four years of college and enjoy a fulfilling student life? We look forward to hearing from you!

Founded in 1992 / Promoted to student club status in 2013
[Attractions of the Sport]
Ultimate is a competitive sport that demands both individual athletic ability and team tactics, allowing you to fully utilize the athletic experience you gained through high school. At the same time, a major attraction is that in Japan, most players start playing after entering university. Our club has produced numerous U24 national team players for both men and women, and it is not uncommon for members to continue playing after graduation in the senior national team, corporate leagues, or the U.S. professional league.
[The Appeal of Our Club]
The men’s team is a powerhouse, having won the All-Japan University Championship four years in a row, while the women’s team has placed third and fourth three times each. Through extensive discussions among members, students take the lead in deciding tactics and training methods; this organizational culture is what has built the “strong Waseda” of today.Many members study abroad, and in the past, some have even been selected for their host country’s national team, reflecting our commitment to valuing individuality and diversity. Additionally, since our alumni association is a general incorporated association, career guidance provided by alumni from various generations is both systematic and thorough. Every year, many graduates secure employment at major trading companies, real estate developers, megabanks, strategic consulting firms, TV stations, and advertising agencies.In addition, many alumni work in government agencies and public institutions, serve as university professors (including Professor Kenji Furuoi of the School of Advanced Science and Engineering, who is an alumnus of our club), or have passed the bar exam, CPA exam, and tax accountant exam. Our club provides an environment where members can focus on their sport while receiving a wide range of support.
You are guaranteed to have a fulfilling four years. Let’s aim to be number one in Japan together!

活動内容:
The Waseda University Yuben-kai is a political club established in 1902 (Meiji 35). At a time when the media was still in its infancy, the club was founded by Ono Azusa, the "Mother of Waseda University," together with students deeply moved by the tragedy of the Ashio Copper Mine Poisoning Incident. Lord Okuma Shigenobu served as the first president.For over 100 years since then, the Yuben-kai has remained true to its founding principles, consistently striving to cultivate “true orators who contribute to the progress of society.”
/
/
/
/ The main activities of Yuben-kai members are “Practice, Research, and Action,” based on the club’s mission. “Practice” focuses on crafting speeches and improving oratory skills.Members also participate in speech contests, where they express their own opinions from the podium. “Research” primarily involves study groups, where members can share their areas of interest with the association. “Practice” involves engaging in various initiatives in society; some members serve as legislative interns, while others participate in volunteer activities.
/
/
/
/The Yubenkai can be described as a gathering of students who possess a “pioneering spirit,” willing to take on any challenge that allows them to engage with politics and society from their perspective as students.Our numerous victories and awards in debate competitions, as well as the presence of alumni who are active in various fields—including five former prime ministers—truly reflect the unique character of our club.
/
/
/
/There are absolutely no restrictions regarding year, major, or prior experience for membership. If you’re even slightly interested, please don’t hesitate to contact us. We hold various welcome events, so we look forward to seeing you!

活動内容:
Founded in 1911, the Political Economy Research Society is one of Waseda University’s most prestigious academic clubs, renowned for its long tradition and high academic standards. Members can immerse themselves in their chosen fields of study within a relaxed and open atmosphere. Over the past 100 years since its founding, the society has produced many distinguished scholars, including two former presidents of Waseda University.Members’ career paths after graduation vary widely: while a few pursue graduate studies each year, others seek employment in the private sector or aim to become educators.
/
/
/
/ As part of our regular activities, we hold independent study groups (self-organized seminars) for each field on a weekly basis. Centered around book clubs featuring literature selected by members, these groups are run by students as spaces for collaborative learning. Currently, three courses are active: Political Thought, Economics, and Legal Philosophy.Each course is designed with beginners in mind, so little prior knowledge is required. With appropriate support from peers, the content is structured so that students can keep up by stretching themselves just a little. It is also possible to participate in multiple courses depending on your interests. Other activities include publishing our journals, *Mashira* and *Kōkyū*, and hosting events such as gatherings with alumni.
/
/
/
/There are no restrictions on your university, faculty, year of study, or background. The Kōkyūkai always welcomes anyone interested in learning—whether you’re simply “interested in academia,” “want to refine yourself through scholarship,” or “want to acquire a broad education or study seriously but aren’t sure where to start.” Whether you’re a beginner or feel that your university classes aren’t enough, why not join us in learning?
