活動内容:
We hold weekly study sessions every Tuesday where members give presentations. The topics covered range widely from political philosophy to history, economics, and national security, and members can deepen their understanding through the Q&A sessions held after each presentation. We also host lectures, inviting scholars and public figures we are eager to meet as speakers. Additionally, we interact with conservative political circles outside the university and participate in volunteer work at the Imperial Palace alongside those student groups.
/
/Finally, we define ourselves as a conservative political club and do not claim to be non-partisan. However, we have international students from South Korea among our members, so we do not hold exclusionary views, and we consistently find racist remarks and behavior offensive. If you respect the Imperial Family, we would be happy to welcome you.

活動内容: The Seiyukai is a university-recognized club founded in 1960 that operates under the principles of “impartiality and non-partisanship,” “a balance between theory and practice,” and “serving as a bridge between students and politics.” Our core activities consist of study sessions held two to three times a week, covering a wide range of topics including not only politics but also economics, journalism, and international relations.During these study sessions, members engage in mutual presentations, discussions, and book clubs. Since sessions are tailored to each member’s interests and viewpoints, participants are exposed to themes they may never have considered before and perspectives different from their own, providing opportunities for new learning. Furthermore, we value opportunities to engage with the outside world not only through classroom learning but also through lectures featuring politicians and experts, as well as the production of our club magazine, *BRIDGE*.Beyond academics, we offer abundant opportunities for social interaction, such as group viewings of the Big Six University Baseball League games and biannual retreats, which help deepen the bonds among members.
活動日時・場所: 2–3 times a week (irregular schedule) / 7:00 PM / Student Union Building Conference Room

活動内容: We place a strong emphasis on learning firsthand by directly engaging with the political arena, primarily through internships with members of the National Diet. You’ll gain invaluable experience that you won’t find elsewhere, such as assisting with the daily legislative work of Diet members, helping with national and local elections, participating in visa-free exchanges to the Northern Territories, and organizing biannual lectures featuring prominent politicians. Meeting people who are active on the front lines of society will surely become a treasure for life.
活動日時・場所: Internships at the Diet Members’ Office Building or local offices approximately once a week (days and times vary by individual) and monthly general meetings, etc.

活動内容: Founded in 1915 and soon to celebrate its 110th anniversary, the Economics Society operates daily under the motto, “Give your all to both study and fun!”As an officially recognized club at Waseda University, we are one of the largest academic clubs both on campus and in Japan. Academically, we focus on corporate analysis and marketing strategies, with activities centered around group work for problem-solving and business planning. We hold regular study sessions every Wednesday throughout the year. In addition, we enjoy a very fulfilling club life with events such as alumni gatherings held about four times a year and guest lectures by external speakers!We also host a wide variety of events, including summer and winter retreats, BBQs, and Christmas parties. One of the club’s biggest attractions is that [members from first-year to fourth-year students get along well regardless of their year] through these activities! Let’s spend your precious four years of college life together, enjoying fun and fulfilling days!!
活動日時・場所:
Regular Sessions: Every Wednesday / 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM / Waseda Campus
/
/
/
/Events are held mainly on weekends!

活動内容: The Waseda University Marketing Research Society, commonly known as “Ma-ken,” is a historic, officially recognized club celebrating its 68th anniversary this year. Under the slogan “‘Playing with Learning’ is here,” we aim to study and practice marketing. Our core activities consist of study sessions organized by club members, held twice a week on Mondays and Thursdays.Through these study sessions, we aim to acquire a wide range of business skills, from the basics to specialized fields. The knowledge gained here is put into practice through business competitions, lectures, and projects held in collaboration with companies. We also host plenty of fun events to deepen bonds among members, such as biannual retreats and seasonal activities. Come join Ma-ken and enjoy a fulfilling college life filled with both study and fun!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Thursday / 7:00 PM– (after the 5th period) / Waseda Campus, Rental Conference Room

名前: Waseda University Stock Investment Club Forward
活動内容: The Waseda University Stock Investment Club Forward is a club where members can study and practice a wide range of finance-related topics, with a focus on stock investment. In addition to weekly regular meetings, we deepen our learning through lectures featuring guest speakers, and we also enjoy plenty of social activities such as dinner parties, Shikiho study camps, and year-end parties!We keep things laid-back, so feel free to drop by whenever you feel like it! We’re a diverse club that welcomes everyone—undergraduates, graduate students, and postgrads alike—and we have lively daily discussions about economic news. Since 90% of our members are new to investing, if you have even a little interest in investing or building wealth, please come check us out! If you have any questions, feel free to contact us via Twitter DM. We welcome new members anytime during the semester!!
活動日時・場所: Every Saturday at 9:00 PM / Online

活動内容:
NEW (Next Entrepreneurs Waseda) is a club directly affiliated with the Venture Inmonkai.
/
/
/
/■Purpose
/
/Through interaction with Waseda University alumni who are business executives and peers interested in entrepreneurship, we aim to make entrepreneurship more accessible and contribute to fostering entrepreneurs from Waseda University.
/
/
/
/■Activities
/
/We host networking events featuring a variety of guests, primarily Waseda alumni who are business executives. We also organize gatherings for students aspiring to become entrepreneurs, serving as a community hub.
/
/In the past, we have organized events with executives from publicly listed companies, Waseda University professors, and board members of leading blockchain companies.
/
/Going forward, we plan to collaborate with the Venture Inmonkai to establish a system that provides multifaceted support for entrepreneurship.
/
/Venture Inmonkai……An association of venture entrepreneurs who are Waseda alumni　https://v-tomonkai.org
/
/
/
/■Activity Format
/
/We conduct activities in person or online, adhering to the university’s guidelines for infection prevention.
/
/
/
/■Notes
/
/This is a club open to all Waseda students!
活動日時・場所: Irregular / 1–2 times per month

活動内容:
The Waseda Career Research Society (commonly known as "Career Ken") is Waseda University’s first club dedicated to job hunting and career development. Advocating that students—who can often feel isolated from society—should “increase their career options by expanding their connections with the wider world,” the club conducts various activities such as business study sessions and event organization.
/
/
/
/Our main activities consist of three types: “Regular Courses,” which provide knowledge essential not only for job hunting but also as a foundation for professional life; “Internal Events,” which offer the kind of student-centered interaction that a typical job-hunting community simply cannot provide; and “External Events,” which offer opportunities to interact with professionals—including business executives—in a relaxed atmosphere, something rarely available to individual students.
/
/
/
/This academic year, our Regular Courses included a wide range of offerings such as Fermi Problem-Solving, Financial Statements, and Industry Research. For Internal Events, we organized numerous activities, including summer and winter retreats, road trips, and hot spring trips. As for External Events, we collaborated with external companies to host various events, such as networking sessions with business executives and internship events for first- and second-year students.
/
/
/
/We are always accepting new members, regardless of year or experience! If you’re a Waseda student with even the slightest concern about your future, please join the Career Research Society!
/
/
/
/For more detailed information about our activities, please check our Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), and website!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday / 5:30 PM – 8:00 PM / Waseda Campus

活動内容:
The History and Culture Research Society is an academic club established in 1950. While history is our core focus, we also have members interested in other humanities disciplines such as philosophy and religion. Students of any year and at any time of the academic year are welcome to join. We also welcome students from outside Waseda University.
/
/Activities
/
/1. Club Meetings
/
/　These are our core activities. We hold them once or twice a week. The schedule varies depending on the organizers, but we generally aim for 6:00 PM on weekdays and 3:00 PM on weekends. The format involves members researching topics of their interest and giving presentations. It’s perfectly fine to participate only when you have free time or are interested in a particular topic.
/
/2. Field Trips and Retreats
/
/　We organize one field trip and one retreat each semester. Field trips are day trips to locations near Tokyo. Last year, we visited Yokosuka and Odawara. Retreats are trips lasting about two nights and three days. While we haven’t been able to hold them for the past few years due to COVID-19, in the past we’ve visited Hiraizumi and Sado Island.
/
/3. Waseda Festival
/
/　We participate in the Waseda Festival every year. In the past, our booth featured a “History Quiz” where we posed questions for participants to answer. However, we are currently considering a different activity for next year.
/
/　If you’re interested, please feel free to visit our clubroom or attend a club meeting. We also regularly update information about orientation events and other activities on Twitter and our website, so please check there.
活動日時・場所: Irregular days / Weekdays at 6:00 PM, Holidays at 3:00 PM / Student Union Building
Every Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday / Times vary / Student Union Building, Room E910
1–2 days a week on days of your choice / 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM / Student Union Building E501

活動内容: The main activities of the History Society consist of weekly presentations held three times a week, known as “section meetings.” These are divided into Monday, Wednesday, and Friday sessions. During these meetings, members give presentations on historical topics of their interest. Participants ask questions and share their thoughts with the presenter to explore the topic in greater depth.We meet three times a week, and since attendance is flexible, it’s easy to find a time that works for you. Members belong to one of the three sessions, and most attend once a week. No prior notice is required to attend; simply come to Student Union Building E612 by 6:30 PM to join the session. The defining feature of the History Society is, quite simply, “diversity.”There are no barriers between Japanese and world history, and with themes ranging from biographical history to cultural history, you can broaden your horizons and rediscover history. Our membership is diverse, ranging from those studying history professionally to those who joined simply because they are interested in the subject. During study group sessions, presenters provide detailed explanations, so no prior knowledge is required.It’s a history club that’s open to everyone. After the meetings, we go out for dinner—participation is optional. In addition to regular meetings, we hold retreats twice a year (in spring and summer) to visit historical sites, as well as events to foster camaraderie. We also organize activities at the Waseda Festival. Whether you’re a history buff or a beginner, this is a history club where anyone can join with ease. Come experience the excitement of history with us at Shigakusha!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building E612

活動内容:
We study a wide range of topics, including the history of Egypt from ancient times to the present, as well as the culture and history of the Middle East and Islam. The Egyptology Research Group brings together people from all over the world who are interested in history and culture!
/
/
/
/〈Study Sessions〉
/
/Our main activity is study sessions held about once or twice a week. We use the Discord app and start at 9:00 PM. Since these are online, they’re easy to join at your own pace! (We also hold in-person study sessions at Waseda University’s Student Union Building from time to time.)
/
/At our regular “Free-Theme Study Sessions,” you can freely present on any topic that interests you. Many members choose topics other than Egypt. New students are welcome to present too!
/
/
/
/〈Other Events〉
/
/On holidays, we organize events such as visits to museums and exhibitions. We often go to see exhibits related to ancient Egypt and archaeology.
/
/We also hold occasional dinner gatherings at Middle Eastern restaurants!
/
/For the Waseda Festival, we create Egypt-themed projects! In 2023, we held a classroom exhibition recreating the world of Ancient Egypt, a mock mummy-making workshop, and created and sold pamphlets.
/
/We have a summer camp during summer break! We enjoy BBQs, fireworks, and boating.
/
/
/
/We are recruiting members year-round, regardless of university or year!
活動日時・場所: Student Union Club Room (E509), Discord (app) Wednesdays & Saturdays 9:00 PM – 10:00 PM (online)

名前: Waseda University Military History Research Society
活動内容: The Waseda University Military History Research Society is an officially recognized club established in 1994. Students interested in history, military affairs, and international politics gather primarily for research presentations held every Friday during the 6th period. In addition, the society is actively involved in publishing an annual newsletter, holding summer training camps, and participating in the Waseda Festival. Although the name includes “military history,” activities are not limited to military topics and cover a wide range of subjects.Furthermore, there are clubs with the same name—"War History Research Society"—at various universities across the country that study history and military affairs. We actively interact with these groups through joint research presentations and joint training camps. We welcome students from other universities and graduate students to join us. If you’d like to learn more about our activities, please check out our Twitter and website, as well as our newsletter *Hōka*, which we distribute at events like Comic Market. We look forward to the day we can work together with you!
活動日時・場所: Every Friday (during the academic term) / 6:15 PM / Student Union Building, Building 3, etc.

名前: Waseda University Three Kingdoms Research Society
活動内容:
The Waseda University Three Kingdoms Research Society is a history club that was revived in 2023 after a hiatus. We engage in a wide range of activities related to ancient China, including the Three Kingdoms period, the Han Dynasty, and the Sixteen Kingdoms period. Membership is open to all Waseda students; there are no restrictions based on year of study or length of membership.
/
/
/
/Activities
/
/ (1) Presentations
/
/Club members give presentations on topics of their interest. The subjects range from academic research to KOEI games—anything related to ancient China is welcome. Online participation is also available.
/
/
/
/ (2) Recreation
/
/Currently, we mainly play board games. Along with presentations, this is a core activity, and we aim to meet once or twice a week.
/
/
/
/ (3) Off-Campus Activities
/
/ In the 2023 academic year, we participated in the "Three Kingdoms Grand Cultural Festival" organized by the Three Kingdoms Society and held a discussion on Liu Bei. Plans for the coming academic year and beyond are still undecided, but we intend to continue engaging in off-campus activities.
/
/
/
/ We primarily post activity updates on X, so if you’re interested, please feel free to contact us via DM.
活動日時・場所: 1–2 times per week / 7:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
Our society is an academic club dedicated to studying Buddhist thought, regardless of nationality, sect, or school of thought. Founded in 1886 and tracing its origins to Azusa Ono, we boast the longest history at Waseda University.
/
/
/
/You often hear the phrase "Hara-so-gyā-te-bō-ji-sō-wa-ka" (Heart Sutra), but do you know what this passage actually means?
/
/We read sutras like this. By “reading,” we do not mean reciting them aloud as part of religious practice.
/
/We academically analyze Buddhist texts written in Classical Chinese over 1,000 years ago to correctly understand their meaning. We study the nature of Buddhist thought—which has had a profound influence on Japanese culture, art, and society from the Nara, Heian, and Kamakura periods onward—based strictly on the original sources.
/
/And even today, the Japanese language contains many Buddhist terms.
/
/Mahā-mysterious, a matter of great importance, karma, salvation through the power of the Buddha, the secular world, the true essence…
/
/Many words have flowed from the Buddhist philosophy that was once deeply rooted in the lives of the Japanese people. As you come to fully grasp the meanings of these words, you’ll also find it more interesting to read literature influenced by Buddhist thought.
/
/
/
/In addition, our other activities include holding zazen sessions, visiting art museums to view Buddhist art, and interacting with Buddhist youth groups from other schools… It’s a free-spirited club where you can fulfill your desires to “learn about this aspect of Buddhism!” or “try doing that!”
活動日時・場所: Every other Monday (dates vary), at the Student Union Building

活動内容:
Hello! We are the Waseda University Saiin-dan. You might find it hard to imagine what kind of club we are just from the name, but our activities are very simple. We practice zazen. That’s all. The group was founded in 1922 by Waseda University students who used to travel to Engaku-ji Temple in Kita-Kamakura to practice zazen.We have managed to continue to this day and celebrated our 100th anniversary in 2022. Our specific activities include holding zazen sessions at the university every Thursday and participating in various zazen sessions at Zen temples in Tokyo and Kitakamakura.
/
/
/
/*Starting in the 2024 academic year, we have also begun holding zazen sessions in Tokorozawa! Please see the link below for details.
/
/
/
/【About the Thursday Zazen Sessions】 These are weekly zazen sessions held during the academic term in a tea room rented at the Student Union Building. We conduct zazen practice as well as simple study sessions on Zen. Whether you’re interested in Eastern philosophy, meditation, or simply want to calm your mind—any interest is welcome. This is a zazen group with a fairly fluid membership rather than a fixed group of regulars.We welcome latecomers and those who need to leave early, so please feel free to drop by without prior notice. Due to the nature of the group, participants come from a wide range of academic years. We operate in a relaxed atmosphere with little hierarchy. If you’re interested, please come try out the Thursday Zazen Session.
/
/
/
/We do Zazen (Zen meditation)?no more, no less.
/
/
活動日時・場所: Every Thursday / 5th period / Student Union Building Tea Room 106; Every Tuesday / 5:30 PM – 7:10 PM / Kotesashi Community Center Branch

活動内容: The Waseda University Christian Students’ Association (WKGK) is the only officially recognized Christian student organization at Waseda University. Want to learn about Christianity? Did “Peter” come up in class and you’re wondering who he is? What are Christians like? The Bible seems hard, but you’re interested… If that sounds like you, we’d love for you to come! Come to our club room to read the Bible, pray, laugh, and just relax.Our club room is open every day. We have snacks and candy. We even have lollipops. We throw birthday parties, too. We have guitars and keyboards available. You’ll find friends here with whom you can have deep, meaningful conversations. Everyone is welcome anytime—freshmen, seniors, international students, everyone! *We’re active at both the Main Campus and the Science and Engineering Campus! Check our blog for details!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday–Friday / Drop-in / Student Union Building, 10th Floor, Room E1008

活動内容:
We are a club that explores contemporary thought, taking the social issues that arise daily as our starting point.
/
/
/
/  Putin’s invasion of Ukraine, the horrific genocide of the Palestinian people by Israel, and in Japan today, the Kishida administration is rapidly advancing plans to build a military power capable of launching preemptive strikes alongside the United States.This year, the Contemporary Thought Research Society will pursue research addressing this era of crisis under the theme “Resisting Fascism in the Age of War.”
/
/
/
/  Issues such as “the ongoing constitutional revision in Japan,” “state intervention in military research and academia at universities,” “the contradictions of capitalism,” and “the rampant rise of authoritarian figures like Trump”…Discussing these issues with fellow club members and forming your own view of society offers a different kind of excitement from studying for entrance exams.
/
/
/
/　Our regular activities consist of weekly meetings. We bring in news and newspaper articles to discuss, so no prior knowledge is required. We also plan to hold voluntary gatherings, research presentations, and fieldwork. We offer in-person club information sessions on an ongoing basis. If you’re even slightly interested, please don’t hesitate to contact us! We look forward to hearing from you.
活動日時・場所: Once a week / Student Union Building Conference Room

活動内容: The Philosophy and Criticism Research Society works to make progress through difficult philosophical texts by carefully reading literature selected by each study group, with a designated member giving a presentation once a week. Study groups are newly formed after the orientation period, where new members form groups, select the texts to be read, and decide on the schedule. We welcome new members at any time after the orientation period ends. In that case, please choose a study group to join from among the existing ones.Interaction among study groups primarily takes place at the four annual general meetings, the annual retreat, and through regular use of the club room. Our members come from a wide range of disciplines, including Political Science and Economics, Law, Education, Sociology, Literature, Cultural Studies, and Science and Engineering, and students from other universities tend to participate every year. One of our club’s strengths is that we provide a space for learning that transcends individual departments and universities. The requirements for membership are simple.Take responsibility for study sessions, participate in general meetings and orientation activities, and keep the club room clean after use. By adhering to these three principles, members can work together comfortably, and we can welcome new members the following year. There is no admission fee. This concludes our overview of the club. However, there is only so much we can convey here. Please do come visit our club room. We’ll have coffee and tea ready for you.
活動日時・場所: Weekly / As needed

活動内容:
Let’s start with a direct question: What exactly is “philosophy”? Many of you probably think of it as “a discipline housed in the Faculty of Letters where people spend their time endlessly pondering difficult and pointless things.”
/
/
/
/Admittedly, that perception isn’t entirely wrong. Over the 2,500-year history of philosophy, many ideas have been explored. In the process, some theories have “run away” to become part of the natural sciences, while others have migrated to the social sciences. Still others have simply faded into obscurity.Perhaps, in the modern era, the “significance of studying philosophy” isn’t all that great.
/
/
/
/But is that all there is to it? It seems to me that there is still a vast field of thought around us waiting to be explored. For example, what is “significance”? What exactly is “uselessness”? To take a more everyday theme, what is a “university”? What kind of people are “Waseda students”?
/
/
/
/With the goal of “philosophizing” about these “various aspects of daily life,” “Yururi! Tetsugaku!” was launched. Through philosophical dialogue and study, our group aims to help members construct their own perspectives on the world. Whether you’re interested in philosophy or just curious, please feel free to join us. We welcome you.
活動日時・場所:
Every Thursday & Friday / 9:00 PM / ZOOM
/
/We are also planning in-person events!

活動内容: Ryokuhokai is one of Japan’s largest law clubs. We are divided into 10 study groups and meet weekly. During the 5th and 6th periods, we hold lectures on legal subjects, followed by social events that everyone can enjoy. With plenty of activities throughout the year—such as cheering at the Waseda-Keio baseball game, two annual training camps, and running a booth at the Waseda Festival—you’ll never get bored. Please come to our study group information session.Each seminar group has its own unique character, so you’re sure to find one that suits you. During orientation week, we host events like cherry blossom viewing parties and social gatherings. Second- and third-year students will be there, so please feel free to join us. This year marks Ryokuhokai’s 80th anniversary, and we will be hosting a party in October featuring distinguished alumni. We look forward to celebrating this milestone with many of you new students. Joining Ryokuhokai is undoubtedly the best way to make the most of your student life in the Faculty of Law.We look forward to seeing you!
活動日時・場所: Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays

活動内容: Hello! We are Sohokai, one of Waseda University’s three officially recognized law clubs! Sohokai is a law club with a long history, now in its 68th year! Our club holds a wide variety of events, including high-quality legal lectures led by third-year students three times a week! We have three training camps a year (summer, winter, and welcome camps), on-campus legal debates and joint debates with other universities, alumni gatherings where we invite Sohokai seniors who are active in various fields, and farewell parties to send off graduating seniors… There are so many events that I can’t possibly list them all here!! And above all, Sōhōkai’s biggest selling point is that many members stay active long after joining! That’s how close-knit we are—both within our own class and across all generations! You only get one chance at college life—why not spend it with Sōhōkai???
活動日時・場所: Lectures: Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays / 4:30 PM – 6:00 PM (Spring Semester)

活動内容: The Civil Law Research Society provides solid academic support through easy-to-understand lectures and comprehensive exam preparation. Our lecture notes are widely regarded as the best in the Faculty of Law and are a must-have for every student. While people often assume we only study, we actually host plenty of fun events! In addition to spring and summer retreats, we go out together once a month for after-class get-togethers, as well as to places like aquariums, Disneyland, and animal cafes. We strive every day to be a cozy oasis within the Law School. Let’s enjoy the best college life together at the Civil Law Research Society! The Civil Law Research Society is a law club at Waseda University. Through exam preparation, weekly lectures, and support from upperclassmen, we help students in the Law School feel more comfortable with the law. After lectures, we often go out for meals or hang out together. We also have plenty of fun events, including training camps, Waseda Festival, and mock trials. While we take our studies seriously, we also know how to have a blast when it’s time to play! The Civil Law Research Society will enrich your life in the Faculty of Law.
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday / 4:30 PM / Buildings 3 & 11

活動内容:
The Criminal Law Research Society is a highly traditional law club that has been active since 1949. Our alumni are active in a wide range of fields, including judges, lawyers, and prosecutors, as well as national civil servants, university professors, and Tokyo Metropolitan Government employees. With this tradition in mind, our members enjoy their college life.
/
/We currently have about 40 members, with a large number of second-year students. The group is very lively, yet many members have a warm and laid-back vibe. If you’re worried that university clubs might be too frivolous or involve excessive drinking, this is exactly the club we’d recommend—we really hope you’ll come join us.
/
/As for our activities, we host weekly criminal law lectures led by graduate students, allowing us to receive high-quality instruction. The knowledge gained here will be put to use in the mock trial scheduled for 2017. Beyond academics, we have plenty of fun activities packed into our schedule, including biannual retreats, casual drinking parties, summer cruise outings, and courtroom observations. I believe this is a highly flexible club that will satisfy even those who haven’t quite found their place in other law clubs.
/
/Last year, the mock trial—which is held every other year in collaboration with the Civil Law Research Society (Minren)—took place at the Criminal Law Research Society. As a result, starting around the time of the summer retreat, we spent almost every week working on the script, assigning roles, and rehearsing for the mock trial, so we focused our efforts on those activities. Law students are always welcome to join us.
活動日時・場所: Every Friday, Saturday, and Sunday / Irregular / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Sociology of Law Research Society is a student organization aimed at fostering camaraderie among students studying law through the academic study of law. Although we are a relatively small law club—often referred to as a “small-to-medium-sized law club”—our appeal lies in the close-knit communication we offer, which is often lacking in larger clubs.The Sociology of Law Research Society actively engages not only in the study of sociology of law and foundational legal subjects, but also in the study of positive law. In particular, for first-year students who are new to the field of law, we hold study sessions focused on required courses such as Constitutional Law, Civil Law, and Administrative Law. These sessions support new students in their studies while also helping upperclassmen deepen their understanding of legal scholarship. We also organize activities such as study camps and court visits.Furthermore, our club room on the 8th floor of the Student Union Building is always open to members and serves as a space for daily activities, including legal studies. Our bookshelves feature a wide and extensive collection of materials, ranging from legal texts and specialized books to practical guides, as well as general literary works such as novels. We strive to make the club room not only a place for study but also a comfortable space where members can deepen their friendships.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday / 5th period / Student Union Building

活動内容:
The Public Law Research Society is a law club centered around students from the Faculty of Law. We welcome not only students from the Faculty of Law but also students from other faculties.
/
/The Public Law Research Society differs from many other law clubs in several ways. First, we primarily focus on constitutional issues. Additionally, while most law clubs conduct lectures that review course material, our sessions are held in a discussion format.
/
/The greatest appeal of the Public Law Research Society lies, without a doubt, in these discussions. When people think of studying, they typically imagine input-based activities like listening to a teacher or reading books. However, through discussion, we engage in a form of study that involves articulating our own thoughts and explaining them to others. This approach cultivates skills that are useful not only in legal studies but also in a wide variety of fields.
/
/Of course, engaging in discussions with one another naturally fosters closer bonds among members, making this a very welcoming and close-knit club. Why not take this opportunity to experience a truly university-style learning experience?
活動日時・場所: Every Friday / 6:30 PM / Building 3, Student Union

活動内容: The Hotaru Law Society, commonly known as “Hotaru,” offers three weekly lectures (Monday: Criminal Law, Wednesday: Constitutional Law, Friday: Civil Law) to help students navigate the challenging exams of the Law School, which are often considered difficult to pass.While we study law diligently during our regular activities, we also go out to eat together after meetings and have fun at events held about once a month. This balance between study and play is one of Hotaru’s greatest strengths. Additionally, with a membership size that’s neither too large nor too small, we’re a medium-sized club that combines the best of both worlds: the broad social network of a large club and the cozy, family-like atmosphere of a small one.Above all, for law students who spend most of their university life in Building 8, I believe the strength of our law club lies in providing a place to call home right there in Building 8. Let’s walk together toward a fulfilling “Hotaru Life”!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday / 6:00 PM / Student Union Building, Building 3, etc.

活動内容:
Crime is one of the keys to understanding society.
/
/  Every year, we select a topic related to crime or criminal policy and meet about once a week to study it. In the fall, we present the results of our research. Last year’s theme was “Employment Support for Delinquent Youth and Young Offenders: Toward Preventing Recidivism and Reoffending.” Detailed reports are posted on our blog, so please take a look if you are interested.
/
/　In addition to studying from books, we also visit relevant facilities and meet with professionals in the field. Last year, we visited a juvenile assessment center and companies that employ ex-offenders. While crime tends to be a topic of public interest, there are few opportunities to understand its reality, and it is often discussed based on impressions or imagination. To ensure we stay grounded in reality, it is important to visit actual sites. Such field research is one of the defining features of our club’s activities.
活動日時・場所: We meet once a week, and the day of the week is decided through group discussion. The location is primarily a meeting room in the Student Union Building.

活動内容: This club participates in international law moot court competitions held in Japan and around the world. For the past five consecutive years, we have represented Japan at the Jessup Cup, the most prestigious competition of its kind. First-year students attend weekly seminars where they receive lectures from third-year students, learning the basics of international law in a fun and engaging way.From the winter of their first year through their second year, members begin competing in tournaments in earnest. In February, they participate in a competition using international law related to space, where first-year students compete in their first official tournament against teams from other universities. In July, the Japan Cup—their second official tournament—takes place, where they face off against powerhouse universities such as Kyoto University, Tohoku University, and Sophia University.During summer break, the Asia Cup takes place, where students compete in English-language debates against teams from foreign universities. In the second semester, they participate in the domestic qualifiers for the aforementioned Jessup Cup, aiming to advance to the world competition. This competition serves as the culmination of all their previous activities.
活動日時・場所: Monday through Friday (one day per week) / 2:00 PM / Student Union Building, etc.

活動内容: The Contemporary Judicial Research Society (commonly known as Genshiken) is an officially recognized club at Waseda University. It is one of the law clubs within the Faculty of Law, and its members consist of students from the Waseda University Faculty of Law. The society’s activities include holding study sessions before exams, as well as daily interactions among members, visits to law firms, on-campus legal debates, and participating as executive committee members in the annual “Eradicate Pharmaceutical Harm Day” event held in front of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare alongside practicing attorneys.Although it is a small club with about 10 members per grade compared to other clubs, its activities extend far beyond the campus—including not only activities within Waseda University but also off-campus work conducted alongside lawyers through the "Eradicate Drug-Induced Harm Day" organizing committee.
活動日時・場所: No information

活動内容: Through the organization of welcome parties for new students and graduation celebrations for graduates of the Graduate School of Law, we provide opportunities for students to pass the bar exam and build meaningful connections for the future. These events are semi-official traditions, and each year we are joined by a large number of students, faculty members, and alumni who are active as legal professionals.In recent years, we have also strengthened our collaboration with the Law School Inmonkai to further deepen vertical connections within the community.While passing the bar exam is often seen as a long and arduous journey, we believe it can be overcome through the support of peers who encourage and challenge one another, as well as the encouragement of mentors and senior alumni. As fellow travelers on this thorny path, we continue our activities with the hope of helping to create an environment where we can support one another.
活動日時・場所: Irregular

活動内容: We edit and publish the legal journal (law review) "Law&Practice." Specifically, we invite faculty members from this graduate school and alumni who are practicing attorneys to write articles or participate in roundtable discussions, compile their contributions into the journal, and publish it as "Law&Practice." Students take the lead in soliciting contributions, editing, publishing, distributing the journal nationwide, and raising funds for these activities.You’ll have the opportunity to interact with professors, lawyers, judges, and prosecutors whom you might not otherwise have the chance to meet. The results of our work are preserved in the form of the journal, and it’s incredibly rewarding to come across references to *Law & Practice* while conducting research! If you’d like to receive a copy of *Law & Practice* or are interested in joining our club, please feel free to contact us!
活動日時・場所: Once a month (except July and January) / Building 27

活動内容:
Hello. We are the Law Classroom Street Law, an organization approved by the Graduate School of Law that conducts legal education classes for middle and high school students.
/
/Legal education involves classes that encourage students to think about topics such as “legal reasoning,” “the principles of the Constitution,” and “Are rules necessary?” Rather than one-way lectures, we strive to engage students in dialogue using language that resonates with middle and high school students.
/
/While the voting age has been lowered, debates surrounding the Constitution have intensified, and opportunities for the younger generation to make their voices heard have increased, the reality is that many young people remain indifferent to politics and the judicial system. We hope our classes will serve as a catalyst and provide the tools for students to think about the law.
/
/We are fully committed to preparing our classes through ongoing lesson planning, study sessions with guest lecturers, and frequent consultations with teachers at the schools where we teach.
/
/We look forward to working with you.
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Waseda Campus, Building 27

活動内容: An officially recognized club of the Graduate School of Law. We conduct research presentations and discussions on general gender issues.
活動日時・場所: Irregular

活動内容:
WLS Career Canvas is a law firm visit club officially recognized by Waseda University Law School. With over 150 members in total, we hold activities during the semester and long breaks. Our law firm visit programs are well-received because, compared to official events, they allow participants to see a more casual side of the firms and the attorneys.We actively visit not only law firms but also corporate legal departments and government agencies. Once you become a practicing lawyer, opportunities to visit such diverse organizations can be hard to come by. We invite you to join our club, explore what kind of legal professional you want to become and what kind of organization you want to join, and make the most of your time at Waseda Law School!
We hold career events for incoming students every year, so if you’re interested, please join us.
活動日時・場所: Irregular

活動内容: The Biology Club is divided into four groups—Aquatic, Insect, Bird, and Reptile/Amphibian—and each group goes out into the field to interact with the creatures they are interested in.For example, the Water Group engages in sea fishing and rock pool collecting; the Insect Group collects insects and creates specimens; the Bird Group goes birdwatching; and the Reptile and Amphibian Group conducts field observations and keeps live animals at home. That said, we don’t operate as completely separate groups within the club; we actively participate in group activities such as a welcome retreat in the spring, a summer camp, an exhibition at the Waseda Festival in the fall, and a Christmas party in the winter.We also hold monthly meetings where each group shares updates on their activities. For more details, please check our club’s website, Twitter, and Facebook. Whether you’re a beginner thinking, “I love animals, but I’ve never done fieldwork before…” or an expert saying, “I was in the biology club in high school, and this year I want to go insect collecting all the way to the Boso Peninsula!”—let’s go out together and experience the grandeur and charm of nature!
活動日時・場所:
Activity Dates: Irregular

/
/
/Location: Outdoors, Student Union Building Club Room (Room E723)
Every Wednesday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building, 11th Floor

名前: Fossil and Mineral Research Society (Fossil & Mineral Research Society)
活動内容:
The Fossil and Mineral Research Society (Fossil & Mineral Research Society) is a club dedicated to exploring the history of the Earth through the collection and observation of fossils and minerals!
/
/
/
/Main Activities
/
/・Collecting Trips: Held once a month. We visit sites in the Kanto region for day trips to collect fossils and minerals. We select safe locations, and with support from experienced upperclassmen, even those with no prior experience can participate with confidence.
/
/・Retreats: Scheduled mainly during summer break. We travel to distant sites that are inaccessible during regular collecting trips to gather specimens.The appeal lies in enjoying the local atmosphere, which differs from the Kanto region, and being able to take our time collecting to our heart’s content.
/
/・Waseda Festival: We display and sell fossils and minerals.
/
/・Visits to Mineral Shows and Museums: We visit events where fossils and minerals are displayed and sold, such as the Tokyo International Mineral Fair (Shinjuku), the Tokyo Mineral Show (Ikebukuro), and special exhibitions at the National Museum of Nature and Science.
/
/・Clubroom Activities: We used to hold these before the COVID-19 pandemic and are currently considering bringing them back. We are taking steps to create a relaxed and enjoyable space where we can observe and critique our collected and purchased items together, as well as study fossils and minerals.
/
/
/
/This is perfect not only for those experienced in collecting, but also for anyone who is interested in fossils and minerals but feels nervous about going out to collect them on their own, or who isn’t very familiar with collection sites! Many of our current members collected fossils and minerals for the first time after joining the club.
/
/If you love fossils and minerals, you’re more than welcome to join, regardless of your grade level or experience. Please feel free to stop by!
活動日時・場所:
About once a month / Fossil and mineral sites throughout the Kanto region
/
/
/
/Activities in the club room are currently under consideration

活動内容:
We are conducting research and promoting synthetic biology in order to participate in the iGEM (International Genetically Engineered Machine competition), an international synthetic biology competition.

We are conducting research and promoting synthetic biology in order to participate in the iGEM (International Genetically Engineered Machine competition), an international synthetic biology competition. Synthetic biology is a discipline that seeks to deepen our understanding of biological systems through the approach of “creating life? in which genetic recombination technology is used to give organisms the desired functions. A typical example is the creation of E. coli bacteria that flash fluorescent colors and emit fruit smells. In addition to conducting experiments, iGEM students are also expected to contribute to society through synthetic biology. We give lectures on synthetic biology to the high school students, and we also work on entrepreneur projects that use synthetic biology technology. Through these activities, you can learn the importance of conducting research in a team and, as well as the relationship between science and technology and society. You do not need to have a deep knowledge of biology to participate in these activities. All that is important is enthusiasm and responsibility. We are looking forward to your participation, regardless of whether you are a humanities or science major.

We hold practices and even organize tournaments! There are 4 camps and other fun events throughout the year! / /Want to have a blast? Come to WESA!

活動内容: The Spanish Language Society is one of Waseda University’s oldest clubs, established in 1960. Most people don’t start learning a second foreign language until they enter college. You probably have many concerns, such as “How should I study?” or “What dictionaries and reference books do you recommend?” Joining the Spanish Language Society will solve all those worries in one fell swoop! Work through what you don’t understand with our self-proclaimed “expert seniors” and make friends to learn with.Our activities go beyond just language study and include a wide range of events, such as volunteering at festivals and cooking Spanish cuisine. Recently, we welcomed Professor Goto from the Department of Intercultural Studies in the School of Education as our president. He is incredibly passionate about Spanish, so he might even be able to offer you some advice! If you’re even slightly interested, please feel free to stop by our clubroom.
活動日時・場所: Dates and times are decided each semester after consulting with members about their schedules. We meet in the club room, E536, in the Student Union Building.

名前: Waseda University School of Science and Engineering English Club
活動内容:
The two main strengths of our club are “the ability to conduct activities in English” and “the opportunity to interact with students from other universities”!
/
/
/
/〇 English Activities: We mainly have four types of activities!
/
/1. Value Discussion
/
/In these discussions, we talk in English about a wide range of topics, from simple self-introductions to philosophical topics and social issues. Not only does this improve your English conversation skills, but it also helps you develop the ability to think logically.It’s really interesting to debate a single topic with your peers.
/
/
/
/2. Guide
/
/As the name suggests, this activity involves guiding international visitors around famous Japanese tourist spots like the Imperial Palace, Asakusa, and Meiji Shrine. By conversing with native speakers, you’ll not only be exposed to authentic English but also gain insight into their culture through conversation!
/
/
/
/3. Speech
/
/In speech contests, participants are evaluated on various factors—including fluency, content, and delivery—so if you take your speech seriously, not only will your English skills improve dramatically, but you’ll also hone a variety of other abilities, such as presentation skills and logical thinking!
/
/
/
/4. PDD Discussion
/
/Participants exchange opinions in English on predetermined social or other themes. A distinctive feature is the use of chart paper, which significantly improves not only your English skills but also your presentation abilities. You can even win awards known as “ranks”!
/
/
/
/〇Inter-University Exchange
/
/The biggest appeal of this club is, quite simply, the chance to interact with students from other universities!
/
/Other universities also have ESS (English Speaking Society) groups, and through discussion competitions and serving as guides, you can build friendships with members of other universities’ ESS groups.
/
/
/
/You’re sure to have a great time in this club!
活動日時・場所: Twice a week (Monday, Wednesday, or Friday)

活動内容:
We learn Chinese by communicating with students from China and other Chinese-speaking countries.

We have a fun conversation and play games in both Chinese and Japanese in a relaxed atmosphere. We also offer training for Chinese qualification exams such as HSK. We also sometimes go to the cinema, hang out or have a cooking party!

Our members come from a variety of backgrounds. Some are beginners and some are advanced. We also have members from Chinese-speaking countries or Chinese families in Japan.

We meet twice a week and have events during the holidays. You are welcome to join the activities only when you are free.

Our club is for those who want to learn languages and make friends at the same time. Anyway, come and try our activities.
活動日時・場所: twice a week（曜日varies）/16:30-19:00/Student Center

活動内容: Waseda University Sign Language Saakuru is an officially recognized Waseda University club established in 1982. Our clubroom is located in the Student Union Building (E203) on the Toyama Campus. Our "project planning" sessions, which form the core of our spring semester activities, are held every Monday and Friday during the 6th period (6:55 PM – 8:35 PM) in the Student Union Building. Rather than inviting guest instructors, senior students teach the classes.Since we participate in intercollegiate activities, students from other universities, not just Waseda students, can enjoy participating in our activities. In the fall semester, our main activity is practicing for events that incorporate sign language. During the spring semester sessions, first-year students learn sign language alongside upperclassmen, and in the fall semester, they use what they learned in the spring to perform at events, allowing them to improve their sign language skills over the course of the year. Although most members started learning sign language in college, they have become able to enjoy conversing in sign language.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Friday / 6th period (6:55 PM – 8:35 PM) / Student Union Building

活動内容:
Paddy is an intercollegiate club for people who want to improve their English skills right here in Japan! So, what can you gain from joining Paddy?
/
/
/
/1. Practical English Skills
/
/Some members have seen their TOEFL and TOEIC scores improve, and some have even scored near perfect! Since the focus is on conversational English, you’ll end up being able to speak English with people from other countries (lol).
/
/
/
/2. Friends Among International Students
/
/We recruit international students every fall. Since you can speak English with native speakers who teach you practical English, your skills will naturally improve—and you’ll make friends with them too! Even though they return home after a year, they’ll guide you on trips or let you stay at their homes, making for a lot of fun!
/
/
/
/3. Friends from Other Universities
/
/Paddy is an intercollegiate club that brings together people from various universities (Rikkyo, Meiji, Japan Women’s, Home Economics, St. Luke’s Nursing, Tokyo Women’s Medical, etc.)! There are many people here you wouldn’t normally meet just by being at Waseda.
/
/
/
/4. Unforgettable Memories
/
/An English conversation club… you might think it sounds really serious, right? We do take our activities seriously.Let’s practice English during our meetings! (lol) But the rest of the time, we have tons of fun! On weekends, someone organizes a drive or we gather at someone’s place to hang out. Last month, we even went paragliding! (lol)
/
/
/
/5. Plenty of Events
/
/In addition to personal plans, Paddy’s planning team organizes various events, including four annual retreats (spring, summer, fall, and winter), a summer cruise, a Halloween party, a Christmas party, and cherry blossom viewing!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday and Friday / 6:30 PM – 8:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
We are an English Debating Circle specializing in Parliamentary debate!

WAD is a circle for Parliamentary debates in English. Debate topics range from familiar social issues to international political issues. The appeal of debate is that we can express our paradigm (worldview) in the language during our speech time. You do not need to be an experienced debater or a fluent speaker of English to join WAD. WAD is a strong institution in the English debate world and has achieved excellent results in national and international competitions, despite the fact that many of our members are relatively pure Japanese (*no long-term overseas experience) and beginners. As you continue to debate, you will naturally acquire critical thinking, presentation, and logic skills. You will also have many chances to interact with seniors who have a lot of knowledge about international relations and with your classmates from other universities at tournaments, and you will also be able to lead a stimulating university life. If you want to try something new in university, why don't you start debating?
活動日時・場所: Every 火, 木, Friday日/17:0000分-(5period-)/Waseda Campus10号館もしくは7号館

活動内容:
The Waseda Literary Society, known as "Wasebun" for short, was founded in 1911
/
/ and claims to be Waseda’s oldest literary club! Wasebun focuses primarily on creating literary works and conducting group critiques. We offer many opportunities to write and are actively involved in producing the booklet *Naked Women and Hungry Ghosts* for sale at the cultural festival, as well as participating in the spring and fall literary flea markets.We hold monthly critique sessions within the club. In addition to creating our own literary works, we also host book clubs and study groups to explore existing literary works. We cover a wide range of genres, including novels, manga, poetry, and film—any cultural work involving written media. Our scope of novels is broad, encompassing various fields such as serious literature, popular literature, Japanese literature, foreign literature, philosophy, and contemporary criticism.Whether you want to write or not, everyone is welcome! Since each member focuses on their own areas of interest, the club has a very relaxed atmosphere. We also hold retreats and recreational activities. “Wasebun is a great place—come check it out!”
活動日時・場所: Anytime / Student Union Building E728

活動内容:
The Tanka Club (commonly known as "Wase-tan") holds weekly "uta-kai"—tanka critique sessions and study groups—every Tuesday or Friday starting at 6:30 PM in a conference room at the Student Union Building on Waseda University’s Toyama Campus. Once a year, we publish a journal titled *Waseda Tanka*, where members can submit series of tanka poems, critical essays, and individual poem reviews.In addition, we hold joint training camps with student tanka clubs from across the country in the spring and summer. Wase-tan is in charge of organizing the summer camp and works to make it a lively and enjoyable event!
/
/Many of our alumni have won newcomer awards such as the Kadokawa Tanka Award, so both experienced members and beginners can deepen their interest in tanka. Students from other universities are also very welcome, so please feel free to drop by and check us out.
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday or Friday / Student Union Building Conference Room

活動内容: Centered on the production (creation, criticism, and editing) of our club magazine *Mare* for sale at the twice-yearly (spring and fall) Tokyo Literary Flea Market, we hold study sessions covering a wide range of fields—including general literature, critical theory, philosophy, film, music, and theater—as well as book clubs where we thoroughly analyze literary works, and lectures featuring guest speakers invited based on members’ interests. We also hold a summer retreat.We assume everyone has favorite authors or works. This is a place where you can reflect on what you like about them and why. While we certainly can’t claim to be a large organization, we are a club that supports what each member wants to do or study most right now—whether by receiving tremendous inspiration from people pursuing completely different interests or by organizing study groups with those who share similar goals. Students from other universities and international students are also very welcome.
活動日時・場所: Flexible based on members’ schedules / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are a comprehensive literary club that welcomes all genres, including mystery, science fiction, fantasy, and light novels. Our first advisor was the renowned Edogawa Ranpo. Among our alumni are Kaoru Kitamura and Yusuke Miyauchi, who are now active as professional writers. Both avid readers and aspiring writers participate in our laid-back activities.
活動日時・場所: Irregular / 1:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We hold monthly critique sessions (1-2 times a month) where members bring their own works to discuss and critique. We also organize occasional roundtable discussions where interested members read poetry together. We publish and distribute our club magazine at the Tokyo Literature Flea Market. Beyond that, we just lounge on the sofas on the 11th floor of the Student Union Building, gazing at the Skytree while relaxing and doing whatever we please.Our motto is to be active only when it comes to writing and reading, while keeping other obligations and constraints loose enough to avoid burnout. Joining multiple clubs is, of course, welcome. Whether you’re fully committed to writing, just come to read and go home, or simply drift in and zone out, it’s all fine. While modern poetry and its creation form the core of our activities, we also welcome members with a focus on novels, plays, music, or criticism, and we are always looking for people who can help edit our club magazine.
活動日時・場所: Irregular / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Children's Literature Research Society is a comprehensive literary club consisting of five sections: creative writing, picture books and crafts, poetry, literary criticism, and storytime.Activities vary by day of the week: the Creative Writing section focuses on writing and critiquing novels; the Picture Books and Crafts section involves drawing and arts and crafts; the Poetry section involves writing and critiquing poetry, tanka, haiku, and other forms in a free style based on a given theme; and the Criticism section involves a "reporter" selecting a literary work for the group to discuss their impressions andcriticisms, and interpretations of literary works selected by a “reporter.” The storytime section holds paper theater and picture book readings for children visiting the Shinjuku City Tsurumaki Library. We also organize storytime events for children and produce booklets for the Waseda Festival. People interested in creative writing, those who want to play with children, and those who want to talk about the things they love come together to participate in a free and fun atmosphere.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday at 6:30 PM / Student Union Building; Every Saturday at 2:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Shubun-kai is a club whose main activities involve writing short stories of 2,000 to 5,000 characters—known as “competitive writing”—based on a given theme, sharing them among members, and holding discussion sessions. Competitive writing sessions are held once or twice a month, and past themes have included “Order,” “Re-[something],” and “Education,” among others. Additionally, we publish our club magazine, *Hakushi*, twice a year.We plan to distribute *Shirashi* at the Waseda Festival and the Literature Flea Market. In addition to our regular writing contests, we also hold “unlimited-word-count contests” about twice a year, where members can write as much as they like without any word limit.Attendance at every writing competition submission or feedback session is not mandatory; members tend to drop in casually whenever it suits their schedule. People interested in writing—whether it’s creative writing or editing—work together in a friendly atmosphere, regardless of their level of creative or reading experience!
活動日時・場所: As needed / Online or at the Student Union Building

活動内容: The Kyokuchukai is a Kinko-ryu shakuhachi club. Our appeal lies in our ability to perform a wide variety of songs, ranging from J-POP to classical honkyoku! Every Monday, we offer professional instruction at no annual membership fee. We are a traditional club with a history spanning over 100 years. You can join at any time, and it’s perfectly fine to be a member of other clubs as well.As an intercollegiate club, students from other universities are also welcome to join. The shakuhachi is a simple instrument made from bamboo with five holes. Because of its simple structure, it can produce a wide variety of tones, and since the sound changes depending on the player, the appeal lies in the fact that everyone can develop their own unique sound. It may be a little difficult to produce a sound at first, but our master instructors and upperclassmen teach with great care, so you’ll be able to play in no time. Why not start a hobby at university that you can enjoy for a lifetime?
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Friday / 1:00 PM – 6:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
The Waseda University Taketomo-kai is an organization dedicated to traditional Japanese classical music, founded in 1920 (Taisho 9). When you hear “traditional performing arts,” you might imagine something “stiff,” “dreary,” or “austere,” but all of our past members were people who had never had any exposure to traditional performing arts before!Beginners are more than welcome!! Plus, we’ve been collaborating with various groups recently, so there are plenty of performance opportunities for those eager to play! (However, the club’s official performances are limited to the study session in the first semester and the concert in the second semester, so it’s fine if you only want to participate in those or if you’re busy. In fact, that’s the case for most of us.)
/
/ We are the only group at Waseda University that performs koto, shakuhachi, and shamisen all under one umbrella.The Taketomo-kai practices with the goal of holding a study session in the spring semester and a solo Taketomo-kai concert in the fall semester. We also have training camps twice a year, in the spring and summer. We even get to go to places you wouldn’t typically visit on a regular club retreat!
/
/ The Taketomo-kai is a member of the “Waseda University Classical Performing Arts Federation” and the “Kanto Student Sankyoku Federation.”The Waseda University Classical Performing Arts Federation holds joint concerts twice a year: a spring concert and a performance at the Waseda Festival. We collaborate on welcoming events and social gatherings to foster active exchange among classical performing arts clubs within Waseda University. The Kanto Student Sankyoku Federation hosts various events, centered around two concerts and two training camps each year. With over 25 participating universities, you’ll have the chance to interact with students from other schools.
/
/  Takuyukai is a club with a 96-year history, so we have strong bonds across all generations. Above all, we have a warm, welcoming atmosphere where everyone is welcome!! We also have a spacious clubroom! If you have even the slightest interest in classical performing arts, please come try a practice session! We generally hold practice sessions every Saturday. Since we have an environment where you can practice anytime, even those busy with studies, part-time jobs, or other clubs can balance it all! We look forward to performing with you all!!!
活動日時・場所: Every Saturday afternoon (flexible) / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are the Waseda University Hōshō-kai, a Noh theater club! We practice the dance and chanting of "Noh," a traditional Japanese performing art passed down from the Muromachi period to the present, at a relaxed pace. Why not experience the charm of Noh, a tradition spanning 600 years, here at Waseda University?With instruction from professional Noh performers, you’ll soon be able to dance beautifully on the Noh stage. And when we all sing the soothing Noh chants together, even hearts weary from busy college life will gradually find peace... New members get free monthly fees! We don’t charge annual dues either. All you need is a pair of tabi socks! We provide the kimono used for performances.Please stop by the Student Union Noh Stage during your free time to enjoy a fun part of your college life! “Takasago, or raising sails on the Kono-ura boat, setting out with the moon and the sea…” All of us in the club look forward to seeing you!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday at 3:00 PM – Student Union Building Noh Stage B107, Kasai Noh Master’s Practice Stage (irregular schedule)

活動内容:
We conduct practice, research, and outreach activities, centered around twice-weekly independent practice sessions and twice-monthly sessions with a master instructor.
/
/
/
/We hold a performance once a month, but participation is optional. The pace of practice is also flexible. You can begin practicing dance accompaniment in as little as six months and Noh in about a year and a half.
/
/
/
/Since our founding, we have published the research journal "Kiridoguchi." Our alumni include numerous researchers and theater professionals, and Noh performers who started with us continue to be active in the field.
/
/
/
/We share the stage with 12 other university Noh clubs, allowing you to make friends with whom you can connect even if you’re not very talkative.
活動日時・場所:
Mondays: Room 110 Itanoma / Thursdays: B107 Noh Stage
/
/
/
/Master Classes: Tetsusen-kai Noh Training Institute (Omotesando)

活動内容:
At the Kanharu-kai, we practice Noh dance (known as “shimai”) and chanting! We also receive instruction from professional teachers on an irregular basis.
/
/Being able to practice Noh at university is very rare, and it will undoubtedly be a truly valuable experience in your life!
/
/We meet three times a week! However, you can participate whenever you have free time, depending on your classes or part-time jobs, and in fact, very few members are able to come all three times a week. (Many members are also active in other clubs!)
/
/We hold training camps in the summer and spring, and every fall, we put on regular performances at Okuma Auditorium and host Noh workshops, so it’s very rewarding and will surely become a great memory of your college life!
/
/On a regular basis, members often go out to eat together or just hang out and relax!
/
/Many people worry, “What is Noh? I’ve never done it before—will I be okay?” But all of our current members are people who tried Noh for the very first time after entering university!
/
/Why not experience “Noh,” a form of art that packs Japanese culture into a concentrated form?
/
/We welcome visitors and new members at any time. Please feel free to ask us!
活動日時・場所: Tuesdays & Wednesdays, 2nd–3rd periods; Fridays, 6th–7th periods at Waseda University Student Union Building, B107 (Noh Stage)

活動内容:
A club to enjoy Nagauta ; Japanese traditional music performance

Nagauta is Japanese traditional music performance, originally played for Kabuki.

We plactice Nagauta together with a teacher from a Yoshizumi-ryu school on every Thursday evening.

You can make great experiences throughout many events including regular concert (twice a year), training camp in every summer and winter, and gathering of Nagauta club in other universities.

Come and be a member to enjoy singing and playing shamisen with us!
活動日時・場所: Every Thursday日/16:30-21:00/Student CenterJapanese-style room

活動内容: Hello! We are the Waseda University Rakugo Club, commonly known as "Rakken." Rakken is a club with a history spanning over 70 years, and we have organized the major "Waseda Yose" rakugo performance series approximately 90 times! This "Waseda Yose" is famous among rakugo enthusiasts because it has featured numerous renowned rakugo masters...! Currently, our activities are centered around two main pillars: "appreciation" and "performance"! For appreciation, we hold "viewing sessions" about once every two months and the annual "Waseda Yose," where we invite professional rakugo performers so members can watch rakugo up close—activities designed to help us "deeply enjoy" rakugo.On the performance side, we hold “Club Member Live” events about once every two months, where we showcase the results of our daily practice in front of an audience—an activity designed to help us hone our skills. Whether you want to watch or perform rakugo, let’s come together, inspire each other, and learn more about rakugo! Knowledge comes naturally when you’re having fun. Rakugo is a form of popular entertainment, so don’t overthink it—just dive right in! Beginners and those with no prior knowledge are more than welcome!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday & Saturday / 2:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are the "Shimokake Hōshō-kai," a club dedicated to the Waki role! The Waki is a specialized role in Noh theater. So, what exactly is this character? If the Shite represents the spirit world, the Waki portrays a character from this world (a human). As such, the Waki plays a storytelling role. Now, while there are many Waki roles, the "Shimokake Hōshō-kai" is the only university club in all of Japan where you can practice the Waki role.What’s more, we receive free lessons from professional instructors every week. During our regular practice sessions, we focus on practicing “utai,” the choral singing portion of Noh. We also practice for actual performances on the Noh stage as Waki. Practice is held every Monday at 6:00 PM in Room 110 of the Student Union Building. You’re welcome to observe or try it out anytime!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday / 6:00 PM / Student Union Building, Itanoma Room 110

活動内容: "Kyogen" is a form of Japanese comedy with a history of over 600 years. We study and practice Kyogen, performing in our own productions twice a year as well as on many other stages. This club was founded by Mr. Mansaku Nomura, the father of the renowned Mr. Mansai Nomura. We continue to receive instruction from the teachers of the Mansaku-kai, maintaining an active relationship with them.Our goal is to enjoy the humor of Kyogen and use our expressive skills as students to spread it in the modern world. Although we are a small group, most of our members participate in multiple clubs, and our high level of flexibility is one of our attractions. We actively interact with various Kyogen and Noh clubs from within Waseda to across the country, expanding our network of connections. Rehearsals are completely open, so please feel free to drop by anytime!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday: Student Union Building B107 Noh Stage / Every Friday: Student Union Building 110 Itanoma / 6:00 PM – 10:00 PM (Open to all)
