活動内容:
Hello! Ininkai is a traditional performing arts club that practices and performs shigin (poetry recitation), kenbu (sword dance), and senbu (fan dance). If you’re wondering, “What is shigin?”, look it up online! In kenbu, we swing swords in time with the shigin—it’s so cool! In senbu, we dance gracefully with fans—it’s beautiful! Current members and alumni are happy to teach you.Beginners are more than welcome! Most of our members started with no prior experience! Twice a year, we hold training camps where we visit our master instructor’s dojo in Kobe. Even outside of these camps, our master instructor sometimes comes to the university to teach us.
Additionally, Ininkai is unique among university clubs in that we have four partner clubs: the Mori no Kai, the Waseda-Keio Rivalry Support Club, the Hoshi-kai, and the Waseda Spirit Uplifting Society (all officially recognized clubs). We actively interact with members of these groups.That’s why Iningikai lets you experience the full range of Waseda events! From the Waseda-Keio Rivalry Match and the Hyakuhai to Waseda Festival and more—fun events are galore. Of course, we also have plenty of opportunities to interact with shigin clubs from other universities, ranging from Keio University, Meiji University, and the University of Tokyo in the east to Kansai University, Ryukoku University, and Okayama University in the west!
Plus, we have a spacious clubroom! Please make it your hub for campus life. It’s so comfortable, there are even rumors that some members have practically moved in…
You might think traditional performing arts sound stuffy, but our daily activities are laid-back! Come experience a club life that suits you, free from any “obligations,” at the Inaginkai!
活動日時・場所: Every Friday / Periods 3–5 (1:10 PM – 6:40 PM) / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Ikebana Club holds ikebana (Ikenobo) lessons every Tuesday. The sessions run from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM, and we invite an Ikenobo instructor to teach us each time. Lessons take place in the tea room of the Student Union Building, where we practice in a calm atmosphere within a tatami-mat room. With fewer than 20 members, the club is relatively small, so everyone gets along well, and during lessons, the instructor is able to provide thorough guidance to each student.Anyone can join our club regardless of year, college, or prior experience, and in recent years, we’ve welcomed many international students. Therefore, we highly recommend this club to international students who want to learn about Japanese culture, as well as to students who wish to deepen their connections with international students! In addition to our regular practice sessions, we display our work at various events such as the Waseda Festival and major flower exhibitions. We also hold regular dinner gatherings to provide opportunities for members to bond.We welcome trial sessions and visits at any time, so if you’re interested, please feel free to contact us via email ([email protected]), X (@ikeken_waseda), or Instagram (@ikeken_waseda) DM! All of our members look forward to meeting you.
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday / 5:00 PM – 8:00 PM / Student Union Building, Tea Room 106

活動内容: The Koto Music Society is a traditional Ikuta-ryu koto club with a history spanning over 60 years since its founding. In this club, you can engage with a wide variety of pieces, ranging from classical koto music to contemporary compositions. Experienced players are welcome, of course, but beginners are also very welcome. We also actively welcome international students, students in their second year or higher, and students from other universities. Joining multiple clubs is also allowed. Our regular activities mainly consist of weekly lessons or practice sessions.During lessons, you will receive careful instruction from professional instructors. On weeks without scheduled lessons, we hold practice sessions. Regardless of seniority, everyone practices together in a friendly and harmonious atmosphere. By practicing together, even beginners can improve quickly. In addition to holding an annual concert, we have a full schedule of events, including summer training camps and performances at the Waseda Festival.Furthermore, our club is a member of the “Waseda University Classical Performing Arts Federation” and the “Kanto Student Sankyoku Federation,” so we actively engage in exchanges with clubs at Waseda University and other universities. Through these exchanges, you can meet fellow students who are passionate about classical performing arts and traditional Japanese instruments. If you have even the slightest interest in the koto, joining our club is a great way to get started. The koto is also a hobby you can enjoy for a lifetime.Come join the Koto Music Research Society and enjoy a fulfilling student life! We look forward to hearing from you. (Email: [email protected])
活動日時・場所: Every Friday / 3:00 PM – 7:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We, the Waseda Yose Performing Arts Research Society, primarily organize comedy live shows featuring manzai and skits. We hold regular live shows 4–5 times a year at venues near the university, each lasting two days. We also occasionally hold joint live shows with other comedy clubs. All the material performed at our shows is original work created by our members. While we are keenly aware of the challenges of writing comedy material, we strive every day to make our audience laugh as much as possible.In addition to our live shows, during summer break we visit several hospitals across Japan to perform comedy shows as volunteers. At the Waseda Festival held in November, we rent a classroom and hold a “7-Hour Non-Stop Live Show,” where club members take turns performing non-stop.
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday & Friday / 4:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
We are an original creation club, commonly known as "Ijiman"!
No experience or confidence? You’re more than welcome! We create original manga, illustrations, novels, and more, and publish them as a book!
● Activities
Production and publication of the club magazine "Solange" 9–10 times a year
We publish "Solange," a club magazine compiling members’ original works.Anything that can be expressed on paper—manga, illustrations, novels, and more—is welcome!
〇 Exhibiting at and distributing "Solange" at Summer and Winter Comiket, COMITIA, and Waseda Festival
We distribute the completed issues of "Solange" at various doujinshi conventions! Since we participate in two types of conventions in both summer and winter, we attend a total of four times a year!
At Waseda Festival, we take over an entire classroom to host a variety of events! We work together as a club to prepare and run everything, including exhibitions of original works, distribution of "Solange" and merchandise, and live drawing sessions!
〇 Summer and Winter Retreats
We hold two 2-night, 3-day retreats each year—one in summer and one in winter! Summer retreats are usually held in coastal areas, while winter retreats are often at hot spring resorts!
We go sightseeing, relax, create art, and just take it easy—everyone spends their time however they like!
〇 In addition to that, we have plenty of other events, such as live drawing sessions, clubroom art sessions, and dinner parties!
All activities are optional, so you can enjoy creating art at your own pace!!
● Membership Fees
New Members: Annual fee 5,000 yen + enrollment fee 1,000 yen
The fee is a bit higher because we publish a club magazine… we appreciate your understanding!
活動日時・場所: Irregular (days vary) / Club Room (Student Union Building E827) · Discord

活動内容: We enjoy a wide range of media, including shōjo manga, manga, anime, and 2.5-dimensional musicals. We do not have regular scheduled activities; instead, members gather in the club room at their convenience to socialize. The club room is equipped with manga, a TV, and computers, making it a relaxing place to spend free periods.Our annual events include orientation for new members, watching the Waseda-Keio rivalry game, end-of-first-semester and end-of-second-semester parties, a special exhibition at Waseda Festival, a Christmas party, and the publication of our club magazine. We sell our published magazines at events like the Summer and Winter Comic Markets. Participation in all events is optional, so members who belong to other clubs are more than welcome! We also welcome beginners to contribute to our club magazine! We accept applications from students in their second year or higher, as well as those joining after the orientation period, so please feel free to contact us if you’re interested!
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Student Union Building E531

名前: Waseda University Takarazuka Revue Lovers' Club (Saho-kai)
活動内容: Three times a year, we handle everything from planning to production of the magazine "Yume no Hanataba" (Bouquet of Dreams). In the summer, we go on a retreat to the Takarazuka Grand Theater. Whether you’re already a fan, have never seen a performance before, or are a man, please feel free to come join us!
活動日時・場所: Irregular / Student Union Building, Hibiya

活動内容: With the motto "Spreading the joy of Tsugaru shamisen," we are a club that performs ensemble music exclusively on the Tsugaru shamisen—a rarity even nationwide. While most members started playing the shamisen in college, we have a club room where you can practice on your own whenever you like, allowing everyone to progress at their own pace. We receive technical guidance from upperclassmen and alumni who have won awards at national competitions, and there’s a welcoming atmosphere where underclassmen feel comfortable asking questions!Since we practice together all the time, the members get along very well, and as an intercollegiate club, we have members from a variety of universities! We have won numerous awards at competitions, and at the Tsugaru Shamisen World Championship held annually in Hirosaki City, Aomori Prefecture, we achieved four consecutive victories in the Group A category from 2016 to 2019. Looking at our track record, you might think our practice sessions are intense, but usually, we just relax and enjoy playing the Tsugaru shamisen together.We are actively involved both domestically and internationally, performing not only at university events like the Waseda Festival but also at welfare facilities such as day care centers, local festivals, and corporate events. We even travel abroad several times a year to perform upon request.At Mitsuba, we welcome anyone who shares our spirit of “enjoying the Tsugaru shamisen together.” We’ve also posted videos on YouTube, so please check them out. We’re sure you’ll fall in love with the charm of this instrument.
活動日時・場所: Every Friday / 5:30 PM – 7:30 PM / Nearby facilities

活動内容: We are Japan’s premier student biwa club. We specialize in the Tsuruta-ryu Satsuma biwa, known for its powerful tone. Under the guidance of a professional instructor, you can enjoy playing the biwa at your own pace. All members are beginners who started in college, so you can feel at ease.In addition to classical pieces based on Japanese history—such as "Gion Seisha," "Honnoji," "Atsumori," and "Nasu no Yoichi"—you can challenge yourself with a variety of genres, including modern pieces, ensemble performances, and original compositions. Beyond our regular activities, we hold three concerts a year in March, June, and November, and we also perform at the Classical Performing Arts Federation’s joint concert "Wagaku" and library concerts. Furthermore, in the summer, we go on retreats to places like Lake Kawaguchi.We also have a comfortable club room fully equipped with amenities like a refrigerator and microwave! Plus, you don’t need to buy your own instruments! Whether you’re looking for a laid-back club experience, interested in traditional Japanese instruments or music, or simply love music… everyone is welcome, regardless of grade or school!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday / Periods 4–6 / Japanese-style room on the 1st floor of the Student Union Building

活動内容: We usually enjoy reading manga and watching anime featuring Doraemon and other works by Fujiko. In April and May, we hold a welcome party for new students, where we watch Doraemon movies. In June, we visit the Fujiko F. Fujio Museum in Kawasaki City.During summer break, we go on a summer camp. In past years, we’ve visited a variety of locations. These range from places associated with Doraemon—such as Toyama Prefecture, the birthplace of the series’ creator Fujiko F. Fujio; Hokkaido, home to the Doraemon Waku Waku Sky Park; and Hakone, where we participated in a Doraemon stamp rally—to places unrelated to Doraemon, such as Aichi Prefecture.We also celebrate Doraemon’s birthday on September 3rd. For the past few years, we have visited the Fujiko F. Fujio Museum on that day. Once summer vacation ends, preparations begin for the Waseda Festival, held in early November. Every year at the Waseda Festival, we host the “Doraemon Quiz,” where visitors can test their knowledge of Doraemon.After the Waseda Festival, we return to our regular activities. In December, we hold a reunion where we can interact with our alumni. Then, around Christmas, we visit the Fujiko F. Fujio Museum. Once spring break begins, we go to see the new Doraemon movie, which is released every March. If you love Doraemon, we look forward to seeing you!
活動日時・場所: Irregularly every Monday / 6:15 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Young People’s Kimono Club holds kimono and yukata dressing practice sessions once or twice a month in the Japanese-style room at the Student Union Building! We also go on leisurely strolls in kimono to places like Asakusa, Kamakura, and Kawagoe, and participate in kimono-related events—our activities are laid-back and relaxed! Even if it’s your first time wearing a kimono, you’ll be able to put it on easily after just two or three practice sessions, so it’s a lot of fun! ♪ Men and international students are, of course, more than welcome! Our activities include: April: A welcome event featuring a kimono-wearing experience and a dinner party; around May: Participating in the ICC Japanese Culture Event to let international students try on yukata; around June: A stroll through Kamakura when the hydrangeas are in full bloom; August: Summer festivals and fireworks displays in yukata; September:retreats to places like Kyoto, Nikko, and Chichibu; sessions to learn kimono dressing from a professional instructor; the wind chime event in Kawagoe; November: letting visitors try on kimonos at the Waseda Festival… and much more!
活動日時・場所: No specific days/Starting at 4:30 PM/Japanese-style room in the Student Union Building

活動内容: As Waseda University’s first graduate-level cultural club dedicated to the tea ceremony, we practice daily alongside international students from more than seven countries.Team Tea Ceremony brings together Japanese and international students from the three universities in the Science City, working as a single team regardless of nationality, age, or university affiliation. Every year, we host a large tea ceremony called the “International Student Men’s Tea Gathering,” which has become a local specialty of Kitakyushu. Recently, we also went on an overseas tour. Through traditional Japanese culture, we can connect people across national borders.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday–Friday / 11:00 AM–4:00 PM / Inside the FORSNET Office (Kyoto Science City International Student Support Network)

名前: Waseda Branch of the Pokémon Lovers Club
活動内容: We are the only officially recognized Pokémon club at Waseda University! During our weekly regular meetings, we not only play Pokémon games and cards but also engage in various Pokémon-related activities. At the end of every month, we hold a tournament for all club members using Pokémon games. We also host exchange events with Pokémon clubs from other universities, so you can make lots of friends who love Pokémon! In addition to Pokémon-related activities, we hold events such as dinner parties, karaoke contests, and barbecues, as well as training camps during summer and spring breaks.This year, our club members advanced through the national qualifiers in both the video game and card game categories and made it to the World Championships! This is a fun club for everyone, whether you’re someone who wants to “dive deep into Pokémon” or simply “loves Pokémon”! If you’re interested, please feel free to contact us!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday / 4:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: While many people know how to put on a yukata or kimono, very few can properly don a kariginu or ikkan. A kariginu is a relatively active style of clothing worn for activities such as falconry and kemari, while an ikkan is a simplified version of the attire worn when attending court.Our Costume Research Society is a club where members can actually dress others in—and wear—Heian-period attire that is rarely encountered in everyday life. We start with basic tying techniques, so no prior knowledge is required; with practice, anyone can learn to dress others in these garments. Since we use costumes owned by the club, there is no need for members to provide their own. Our main activity is practicing dressing techniques, and during the Waseda Festival, we also have opportunities to dress visitors. Come join us and enjoy the elegant world of traditional Japanese attire!
活動日時・場所: Once a week (irregular schedule) / (On weekdays) 6:00 PM / Japanese-style room in the Student Union Building

活動内容:
This year’s research theme is “Russia’s Invasion of Ukraine, Israel’s Invasion of Gaza, and Tensions in East Asia—Examining a World of Conflict Where the U.S., China, and Russia Collide.”
/
/
/
/ Two years after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the world is becoming increasingly turbulent, intertwined with the deepening conflict between the U.S. and China.Since Israel’s invasion of Gaza began last October, the risk of nuclear war has surged rapidly in East Asia, with the focus on Taiwan and the Korean Peninsula.
/
/
/
/　There has never been a more critical time to confront the modern world, where so many people suffer from war, division, poverty, and oppression. Let’s study together how to resolve these issues while resisting the rising tide of nationalism.
/
/
/
/　Our regular activities consist of weekly club meetings. We collaboratively research the latest international issues using newspapers and news reports as our source material. The results of our research are presented at the Waseda Festival. The true appeal of the International Studies Research Club lies in the opportunity to shape your own worldview through collaborative research. No prior knowledge is required. If you are interested, please start by registering for our official LINE account.
活動日時・場所: Once a week / Student Union Building

名前: Group for Reflecting on War, Poverty, and the Environment
活動内容:
We are a club that addresses current issues in Japan and around the world, delving deeper into them through discussion. Through this process, we aim to cultivate the ability to gain deep insight into the crises facing the modern world and to form our own well-grounded views on society. Our club offers the unique rewards and enjoyment of collaborative research. We also plan to participate in fieldwork and organize exhibits for the Waseda Festival.
/
/
/
/〔Here is the research we will be conducting in the 2024 academic year↓〕
/
/　More than two years have passed since Russia’s military invasion of Ukraine—a barbaric act of the century. Following Israel’s massacre of the Palestinian people, here in East Asia, the United States, Japan, and China are intensifying their military standoff over Taiwan. Japan’s Kishida administration has now completely abandoned the principle of “exclusive defense” and is pushing forward with the creation of a “war-capable nation” capable of launching preemptive strikes alongside the United States.
/
/
/
/　This year, we will explore paths to transcend the modern world that has entered an “era of war and massive military expansion.” What are the aims of the constitutional revision plotted by the government and the Liberal Democratic Party? What is the reality of this unprecedented military buildup? What is the reality of military research mobilizing universities?
/
/
/
/　What is “Putin’s War”? What drives the Ukrainian people to resist so tenaciously? What was the collapse of the self-proclaimed “socialist” Soviet Union? — We will research these issues under the annual theme “Resisting New Fascism.”
/
/
/
/　We hold information sessions on an ongoing basis, so please come and hear what we have to say! We look forward to hearing from you.
活動日時・場所: 1–2 times a week / Clubroom E530, Student Union Building

名前: Waseda Social and Environmental Engineering Research Society
活動内容:
The Waseda Society for Social and Environmental Engineering (Shakanken) is a club dedicated to deepening interest in social and environmental engineering. It is composed of students studying social and environmental engineering—a field that supports cities and the nation through structures such as bridges, tunnels, rivers, and roads.
In addition to exchanging information on civil engineering, our main activities include organizing project site visits 2–3 times a year, social gatherings, and trips to view outstanding civil engineering structures.During site visits, we tour the sites of the latest construction projects both within and outside the Tokyo metropolitan area, allowing us to experience firsthand the large-scale nature of civil engineering work. These visits also provide a valuable opportunity to hear about practical aspects of the field, such as construction processes.
Members also occasionally organize walking tours of the city or short trips together. With background knowledge in fields like geography or folklore, the streets, roads, and bridges you’ve walked past without a second thought might just reveal a whole new side to you!
Another advantage is that our base of operations is located on the Nishi-Waseda Campus. As a historic club founded in 1974 and originating from the River Engineering Seminar, we welcome not only those interested in civil engineering but also anyone who loves—or hopes to come to love—urban planning, transportation, and community development.
[2025 Activities]
・Walking tour of the Shibuya area (June)
・Visit to a highway construction site (July)
・Visit to an underground airport station construction site (July)
・Site visits and urban structure analysis activities in the Republic of Indonesia (August)
・Port tour (scheduled for January 2026)
活動日時・場所: Almost every day / Nishi-Waseda Campus

活動内容: Our club aims to help members obtain a wide variety of certifications, ranging from those useful for job hunting—such as TOEIC and bookkeeping—to national certifications like Real Estate Transaction Manager and Financial Planning Specialist, as well as novelty certifications like the Ninja Certification and Okonomiyaki Certification.We are an intercollegiate club with approximately 150 members. Our regular activities take place every Tuesday and Thursday during the 3rd, 4th, and 5th periods, when we open our club room in the Student Union Building to study for certifications and exchange information. On weekends, we organize group exam sessions, and we hold monthly general meetings.We also participate in events such as 100-kilometer hikes and the Waseda Festival. During the long summer and spring breaks, we hold training camps where all participants take certification exams together. At the 2016 summer camp, we earned Barbecue Instructor certifications, and at the 2017 winter camp, we took the Ski and Snowboard Certification exams. We enjoy our activities while encouraging and competing with one another.
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday and Thursday / 1:00 PM – 6:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are the Education and Teaching Career Club T-team, the only Waseda University-recognized club focused on education. While we may seem serious at first glance, we actually have a friendly atmosphere where members from various departments work together! We meet twice a week on Tuesdays and Thursdays during the 6th and 7th periods. Our activities center around mock lessons, where we actually teach classes and discuss what went well and what could be improved.We also hold events where we work together to help with essential procedures for pursuing a teaching career, such as course registration and completing the teaching career portfolio. We organize field trips and trips, making this a great club for making friends who share your goal of becoming teachers. Sometimes we even have fun playing card games like poker after class…! We post specific activity dates and details on X (formerly Twitter) and Instagram. All of us in the club look forward to welcoming you, new students!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday & Thursday / 6:55 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We hold study sessions on clinical psychology and engage in volunteer activities at sites related to psychology. Our main activities include assisting with SST (Social Skills Training) sessions at rehabilitation facilities, taking notes during sessions, chatting with participants at tea parties, and conducting debriefings with facility staff and SST instructors. Since these activities do not require any special skills, you are welcome to participate with the mindset of a field trip.We also hold study sessions to prepare for graduate school entrance exams in clinical psychology, including summarizing key terms and practicing past exam questions. These sessions are held at locations such as the Tokorozawa Campus to accommodate participants’ schedules. Additionally, as volunteers supporting individuals with social withdrawal, we participate in the monthly meetings of the self-help group “KHJ West Tokyo ‘Moe no Kai’ Gathering Place Cosmos” and engage in school student volunteer activities.
活動日時・場所: First and third Sundays of every month / 8:30 AM – approx. 11:00 AM / 15-minute walk from Takadanobaba Station

名前: Science and Engineering Academic Club Wathematica
活動内容:
Wathematica is a science and engineering academic club that is mainly active on the Nishi-Waseda Campus! Students interested in fields such as mathematics, physics, and computer science gather here to conduct independent study groups.
/
/
/
/At Wathematica, members are free to choose the topics they want to study and explore them in depth through seminar-style sessions. While studying at university can sometimes be discouraging when done alone, learning collaboratively with peers helps maintain motivation and deepen understanding. Additionally, members can strengthen their bonds through regular social gatherings, as well as annual events such as presentations and retreats.
/
/
/
/While many of our members are science and engineering students, the number of members from a wide range of other departments is growing every year. Students from the humanities who are interested in science and engineering are also very welcome!
/
/
/
/Wathematica is a place to share a passion for learning, think independently, and deepen your understanding. If you’re interested, please join us. Let’s deepen our knowledge together and enjoy new discoveries and interactions.
活動日時・場所: Weekdays (irregular schedule) / Free periods or 5th and 6th periods / Building 61 Learning Commons, etc.

活動内容:
[Activities]
The Waseda University Exam Question Creation Club (hereinafter "Sakusar") creates exam questions for a wide variety of subjects! From science subjects like math, physics, chemistry, and biology to humanities subjects like English, Japanese history, world history, and modern Japanese literature—some members even create questions for niche subjects like home economics and information technology! Of course, we don’t limit ourselves to high school level; we’re happy to create questions for middle school or even elementary school levels too! Let’s create your very own original questions!
[How to Enjoy]
We have a track record of establishing the "National Problem-Setting Circle Federation"! There is a Discord server where problem-setting circles from all over the country gather. It’s a chance to hear from all kinds of people!!
We hold retreats twice a year. In addition to problem-setting activities, you can bond with members regardless of grade level through recreational activities!
We sell original problem books created by our members at the Waseda Festival and the Science and Engineering Expo. Why not include your favorite problem in the book!?
We also actively interact with students from other universities! In the past, we’ve held events like collaborative mock exams and the Waseda-Keio Showdown!!
[Features of Our Club]
Creating problems for any subject is welcome!
Since we’re an inter-university club, students from other universities are welcome too!
We’re not big on drinking parties!
活動日時・場所:
Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays, 5th and 6th periods
We usually use classrooms in Building 3!

活動内容: The Waseda University Railway Research Club (WRC) is one of the largest university railway clubs in Japan. From monthly meetings to summer camps and booths at the Waseda Festival, we hold various events throughout the year where railway enthusiasts gather to deepen their connections. Our diverse membership ranges from casual enthusiasts to hardcore fans, and each member deepens their knowledge of railways in their own unique way.While the term “railway hobby” may seem broad, it encompasses a wide range of interests, including photography, model railroading, and rolling stock research. To accommodate these diverse interests, we have established “special interest groups” where members can engage in activities tailored to their specific passions, allowing for deeper exploration of particular fields. Our main events include welcoming new students during orientation week with cherry blossom viewing parties, model train operating sessions, chartered train rides, and training camps.During our summer retreat, members travel on their own routes, meeting and dispersing at their destinations, and we always include a tour of a rolling stock depot. We exhibit at the Waseda Festival every year, showcasing a massive model railway layout, railway photographs, parts, and other displays that bring together the collective expertise of our various sub-committees.We also publish our club magazine, “Switcher,” to share our members’ research findings with the public. Additionally, we receive media coverage from magazines and TV stations, as well as requests for railway-related work. One of our club’s defining features is the many unique experiences available only through WRC. If you’re even slightly interested, please feel free to drop by our clubroom in the Student Union Building!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday through Saturday / Student Union Building, Club Room E516 (Open to all)

活動内容: Founded in 1999, this is Japan’s oldest university cafeteria research club. We evaluate cafeterias using our own proprietary survey forms and compile a cafeteria ranking every six months. These rankings have garnered significant attention, and we have collaborated with numerous media outlets in the past, including Mezamashi TV, World Business Satellite, Weekly Asahi, and J-WAVE! Throughout the year, we visit cafeterias at various universities, not just Waseda.Furthermore, we hold retreats twice a year, in August/September and March. We travel to distant cafeterias that we wouldn’t normally visit, enjoying a different kind of fun together that sets us apart from our regular study group activities. About two or three times a week, all members casually participate in our regular activities at their own pace. Since attending three of our regular cafeteria study sessions is one of the requirements for joining, please feel free to come check us out first!
活動日時・場所: Irregular / Cafeterias in Tokyo

活動内容: As a group dedicated solely to "viewing" tokusatsu works, we are a club that watches a wide range of films and videos utilizing tokusatsu techniques. Our objectives are, first, to enjoy watching these works while sharing our appreciation with others; second, to rediscover the value of tokusatsu as a traditional Japanese art form; and third, to analytically evaluate the artistic and representational qualities of these works to uncover new value within them.As a result of these efforts, we self-publish collections of essays based on various themes and distribute them twice a year at Comic Market. Our activities are divided into regular and special events. During regular activities, we watch 3–4 seasons of shows on a regular basis, while special activities involve participating in various special effects-related events as needed.Additionally, we organize a large-scale tour in the spring and hold a summer retreat. We are a club that not only fulfills our hobbies and strengthens our knowledge but also fosters active interaction among members. Depending on the activity, we engage with visual media beyond tokusatsu—such as anime and films—to broaden each member’s horizons and cultivate their aesthetic sensibilities.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday from 4:30 PM / Every Saturday from 1:00 PM at the Student Union Building

We are the Waseda University Touhou Club, the "Gensokyo Research Society," commonly known as Geso-ken!
/
/
/
/・Activities?〈In-Person Activities〉
/
/During our regular in-person meetings, we play the original Touhou Project shooting games and fan-made Touhou board games!
/
/In addition to the activities mentioned above, we also hold small-scale gatherings on an irregular basis after school on class days!
/
/
/
/・Activities? <Online>
/
/We mainly use Discord for communication, where we stream the original games via voice chat and play Touhou TRPGs with multiple people!
/
/
/
/・Activities?〈Event Participation〉
/
/Every May and November, we participate as a circle in the "Hakurei Shrine Grand Festival" held at Tokyo Big Sight!
/
/At the Grand Festival, we create and distribute our circle’s anthology, "Gensou Nenpo"!
/
/We also participate in the Waseda Festival every year, where we prepare various events such as demo play sessions for the original games!

活動内容: The Waseda University Vocaloid Fan Club is a student group where students who love synthetic voices, particularly VOCALOID, gather to enjoy their shared interests. Our regular activities include introducing each other to our favorite Vocaloid songs, holding Vocaloid-themed quiz nights, and going to karaoke together to foster camaraderie among members. In addition, we organize Vocaloid DJ events and participate in the university festival.When these events are approaching, preparations for them become part of our regular activities. We welcome new members regardless of their level of knowledge about VOCALOID. As we are an intercollegiate club, we also accept students who do not belong to Waseda University.

活動内容:
We are Waseda’s only officially recognized VTuber club!
/
/
/
/■VTuber Planning & Management (VTuber Bureau)
/
/We are currently managing our second-generation official VTuber, “Satsuki Hayayumi.”
/
/We are also planning for our third-generation official VTuber!
/
/We handle everything in-house, including planning, model creation, video editing, and PR.
/
/
/
/■Publishing Activities (Editorial Bureau)
/
/We participate in events like Comic Market and Bungaku Flea Market to distribute our club magazine *VTrue* and research journal *Waseda V-Gaku*!
/
/We allow interested members to enter as vendors, so aside from their approximately 2-hour shifts, they can enjoy the event with the club covering their admission fees!
/
/
/
/■Exchanges with Other Universities
/
/We are a founding member of the Kanto VTuber Federation (V-Uni) and participate in joint activities and exchange events.
/
/You’ll also expand your circle of fellow fans with students from other universities!
/
/
/
/■Other Activities
/
/Any member can propose and carry out new activities related to the club’s objectives, such as VTubers or VR!
/
/We provide funding for each activity (project) as needed.
/
/
/
/■Membership Fees
/
/Membership is free for your first semester!
/
/Starting the following semester, we charge a fee of 1,000 yen per semester (2,000 yen per academic year).
/
/Membership fees are used for club operations, producing publications, and purchasing books and supplies.
/
/
/

活動内容:
The Waseda University Divination Research Society is the only officially recognized divination club at Waseda University.
/
/
/
/You can learn a wide range of divination techniques, including palmistry, tarot, Western astrology, Four Pillars of Destiny, Zi Wei Dou Shu, runes, and Mayan calendar divination.
/
/
/
/We meet every Tuesday for relaxed get-togethers. Our main activities include reading each other’s fortunes, discussing tarot interpretations, and studying together using books and videos. After our meetings, we often go out for a meal.
/
/
/
/In addition, we have plenty of fun events, such as our hugely popular fortune-telling sessions at the Waseda Festival, lectures by professional guests, retreats, and participation in external events!
/
/
/
/Participation in our regular activities is optional. You’re welcome to join just for weekend events or retreats. It’s a club where you can enjoy yourself at your own pace!
/
/
/
/Beginners, students from other universities, sophomores and juniors, and international students are all very welcome.
/
/
/
/We accept visitors and new members year-round. If you’re interested, please contact us via DM on Instagram or X (formerly Twitter)!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday / 5:30 PM to 8:00 PM / Takadanobaba area

活動内容:
The Waseda Drama Research Society is an all-Waseda club established in 2022.
For our regular activities, we gather every Monday in Building 3 or a rental space to watch Japanese TV dramas and participate in drama-related recreational activities. We relax and enjoy watching dramas selected by vote.
In addition to our regular activities, we occasionally organize special events such as location tours and pilgrimages to "holy sites" from the dramas. We generally visit filming locations in the Tokyo area, but we also go on longer pilgrimages to sites further afield! You might even get to visit the filming location of your favorite drama.
We also engage in a wide range of drama-related activities, including producing our own dramas, sharing drama news, and participating as extras in TV dramas.
We hold retreats twice a year and host numerous events, so whether you’re a drama fan or not, you’re sure to have a great time!
We accept trial members and new members at any time. We look forward to hearing from you!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday / 7:00 PM / Building 3, Rental Space

活動内容:
We are Waseda University’s only LEGO club and meet approximately once a week (day varies). While our activities are centered on the Nishi-Waseda Campus, we have many members from faculties other than Science and Engineering, as well as students from other universities!
In addition to basic LEGO creations, we build a wide range of projects, including moving LEGO creations like those seen on “Pythagoras Switch.”We exhibit our creations at campus festivals and external exhibitions. In addition to building, we organize various events such as visits to LEGO stores and overnight retreats.
We share photos of our creations and club activities on social media, so please check them out if you’re interested!
Whether you’re a LEGO enthusiast or just looking to relive childhood memories, everyone is welcome—beginners are especially encouraged to join!
We accept new members year-round, so feel free to contact us via social media DM!
活動日時・場所:
Once a week (day varies)
Weekdays: 5:00 PM – 7:00 PM / Nishi-Waseda Campus
Weekends: 2:00 PM – 5:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Waseda University Aerospace Research Society (WASA) is the largest officially recognized hands-on engineering club in the School of Science and Engineering.The club is divided into four projects: the "Birdman Project," which designs, builds, and operates human-powered aircraft with the goal of competing in the Birdman Contest; the "Astronomy Project," which organizes observation sessions, study groups, and builds planetariums; the "Electronics Project," which aims to consolidate and advance WASA's electrical engineering expertise through the construction of aircraft robots and the development of autonomous control systems for radio-controlled vehicles; and the "Rocket Project," which builds model rockets and can satellites.The club has a long history. It was established at Waseda University in the 1960s—a time when there were no departments dedicated to aerospace studies—with the goal of “conducting research in the fields of space and aviation without being confined by academic departments.” To date, the club has produced many notable alumni, including employees of the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), and we hold regular alumni gatherings. Currently, we participate in intercollegiate programs with other universities, collaborating with students from various institutions, including those from Japan Women’s University, which has officially recognized our partnership.No experience necessary! Members who belong to other clubs are welcome! Activities can be tailored to individual needs!
活動日時・場所: Daily / Rental property, Student Union Building, Makerspace

活動内容:
At the Waseda University MicroMouse Club (WMMC), even beginners can easily build robots under the guidance of senior members!
/
/  The "MicroMouse" in our club name refers to a small, autonomous maze-exploring robot. At the Waseda University MicroMouse Club, each member builds their own MicroMouse. This allows you to be involved in the entire robot-building process and work on your project at your own pace.Additionally, we provide standard MicroMouse kits with pre-designed and pre-programmed components, making it easy even for beginners to build.
/
/  Through the process of building a MicroMouse, you’ll learn various robotics-related skills, including mechanical design and fabrication, electronic circuit design and soldering, and programming in C and C++. We also aim to compete in the MicroMouse competitions held three times a year.
/
/　In addition to MicroMouse, we also aim to participate in the “Tsukuba Challenge,” a competition where robots autonomously navigate the streets of Tsukuba City. For this event, volunteers from the club come together to build a single robot as a team.
/
/　The only cost is for robot materials; there are no joining fees or annual dues. We also hold training camps in the summer and winter. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced robot builder, if you’re interested, please come check us out!
活動日時・場所:
・Every Saturday / 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM / Makerspace
・Occasional activities organized by volunteers at the Student Union Building

活動内容: Our "Student Formula" project involves students developing Formula cars (single-seater, open-wheel racing cars similar to F1) with their own hands. As a student racing team, we compete against other universities to see who can build the best car.Under globally standardized rules, we plan one car per year. We use 3D CAD software for design and analysis, then manufacture the vehicle through machining and welding based on those plans. We evaluate and refine the car through extensive test drives, aiming to build the fastest machine at the Student Formula Japan Championship.The competition evaluates not only vehicle performance but also driving technique, fuel efficiency, cost planning, and business plans, allowing us to cultivate comprehensive “manufacturing” skills. Project management—including securing funds to operate the team, procuring parts and materials, negotiating with sponsors, and managing goals and schedules—is also a crucial part of our activities.Building a real car and building a team with our own hands is no easy feat, but the thrill of seeing the car we built as a team actually race right before our eyes—and beat every other team—is truly special. For more detailed information and updates on our daily activities, please visit our team website. We would greatly appreciate your support and encouragement. We are also always looking for new team members!
活動日時・場所: Daily / 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM / Manufacturing Workshop, Nishi-Waseda Campus (We often have away events on Saturdays and Sundays!)

活動内容: Waseda Computer Entertainment, commonly known as WCE, is a community where members learn programming, illustration, 3DCG, DTM, and game design through the creation of computer-based works. We began our activities at Waseda University in 2011 and have exhibited at the Science and Engineering Exhibition (university festival), Comic Market, as well as other events such as Comitia and M3.In June 2014, we were officially recognized as an approved organization by the School of Science and Engineering. We believe there are many people who want to try programming, illustration, or music production but don’t know where to start, or who feel lonely working on their own. WCE is a club designed for such people—a place where like-minded individuals can gather, learn how to get started, and take that first step into the world of creation, which is actually right at our fingertips but can sometimes feel a bit out of reach.Experienced members will patiently guide beginners, and since our activities are open to any form of creative expression, you’ll surely be able to create whatever you want. Additionally, as a club, we develop completely original games for people to play at the Science and Engineering Fair (our university festival), and we create illustration books and music CDs to exhibit at external events. So even if you want to create something but don’t have a specific goal in mind, you can still enjoy the creative process. Why not take that first step into the world of creators with us?
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday and Friday / 6:00 PM / Nishi-Waseda Campus

活動内容: You only get one shot at college life—why not throw yourself into something? ROBOSTEP is an officially recognized university robotics club that works daily toward winning the NHK Student Robot Contest. We won the NHK Student Robot Contest in 2015, placed second in 2019, and have been competing for five consecutive years.Since the rules of the NHK Student Robot Contest change every year, we develop a robot from scratch each year to meet those new requirements. We split into a "Design Team" and an "Electronics Team" to share responsibilities for mechanical design, machining and assembly, circuit design, and control systems, working together as a team to build a large competition robot. We participate in rookie tournaments and internal club competitions from the very first year to hone our skills from the ground up, so even if you have no prior experience, there’s no need to worry.We are actively recruiting motivated students regardless of year, major, or prior experience. If you’re serious about making things, want to compete in Robocon, or simply want to build a robot, please come visit us!
活動日時・場所: Regular meetings every Wednesday starting at 6:00 PM / Activities during free periods / Manufacturing Workshop

活動内容: Our club focuses on two main activities. The first is creating and distributing a free English-language newspaper. Club members propose projects they are interested in, conduct interviews with prominent figures, and organize roundtable discussions to produce in-depth articles.The second is the production and sale of “Waseda Spirit,” a magazine supporting college entrance exam candidates. Centered on the theme of “the true face of Waseda that only current Waseda students can convey,” club members plan and execute projects themselves to create a magazine that readers will enjoy. We then sell the magazine nationwide, from Hokkaido to Kyushu. A key feature of these activities is that, depending on the content, we can interview various famous people when writing articles, and we can plan and execute innovative projects that only students can pull off!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building

名前: Waseda University Mass Media Research Society
活動内容:
The Media Studies Club is divided into four subcommittees—Planning, Reporting, Design, and Literature—and is involved in producing the free magazine "Wase-kichi" and publishing articles online.
/
/
/
/  The Planning Subcommittee develops ideas for features to be published in "Wase-kichi" based on members' interests and turns them into articles.Additionally, the Reporting Subcommittee conducts interviews from perspectives unique to college students, while the Creative Writing Subcommittee engages in various activities, such as writing original novels and essays. Finally, the Design Subcommittee creates the layout for *Wase-kichi* based on the articles and texts produced by the other subcommittees. While many members are beginners when it comes to article production and design, we learn the ropes from scratch and hone our skills by collaborating with other members!
/
/
/
/  Furthermore, during the Waseda Festival, we invite prominent figures every year to give lectures and participate in interviews. In the past, we’ve welcomed guests from a wide range of genres, including authors Natsuhiko Kyogoku and Kaoru Hayamine, as well as lyricist and composer Katsuhiko Sugiyama.
/
/
/
/　Of course, it’s not all serious work—we also hold plenty of events to help members bond, such as overnight retreats and day trips! Since you can adjust your participation frequency among our four weekly sessions, it’s possible to join this club while participating in others. Whether you’re interested in publishing and design or not, you’re more than welcome. Let’s turn your “likes” and “interests” into reality with the Media Studies Club!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday / 5th or 6th period / Toyama Campus Student Union Building (We plan to adjust the schedule due to extended class hours. Details will be posted on our official Twitter account.)

活動内容:
We are Waseda Links, an officially recognized student organization. In addition to publishing a free newspaper twice a year (in spring and fall), we also operate a web media platform, publish other materials, and organize events.
/
/
/
/For each issue of our free paper, we set a different theme (such as “Choosing,” “Reflecting on Binary Oppositions,” “Morning,” or “Loss”) and attempt a multifaceted approach to the theme through interviews, columns, and articles featuring design and photography. Since we distribute it for free without charging a price, we can create a magazine that distills the unique frustrations of student life from a perspective slightly removed from the commercial market—this is one of our key attractions.
/
/
/
/One of our key features is the wide range of activities available, including writing and editing articles, design, photography, and video production.
/
/
/
/We provide an environment where you can acquire the necessary skills after joining, so anyone interested—whether a beginner or an experienced member—can play an active role.
/
/
/
/If you’ve entered college and want to put your interests to use or try something new, please come check us out.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday, 6th period / Student Union Building

活動内容:
With the vision of “Bringing Commercial Publishing to Students,” Publishing Koshien works to connect students with unique ideas to publishers.
Our main activities include soliciting proposals from students nationwide. After several rounds of screening by our committee members, we hold a final competition judged by active editors. Outstanding proposals are commercially published, and over the past 20 years, we have published 43 books.
We, the executive committee members, review proposals and support participants in preparation for the competition. We also interact frequently with professionals, such as celebrity guests and professional editors at the final competition. …While this might sound like a lot of work, there’s no need to worry. Our upperclassmen are all kind and fun people who respect individual schedules, and we warmly welcome students who are involved in other clubs as well!
Why not experience something unique—connecting students who want to publish books with publishers—that you can only do here?
活動日時・場所:
Monthly general meetings.
Frequency varies by individual but is generally once a week. Meetings are held at the Toyama Campus, the University of Tokyo Komaba Campus, or online.

活動内容:
The publishing group ENJI is a student organization founded in October 2009 with the concept of “Changing Waseda’s Fashion.”
/
/  Our main activity is the publication of a free magazine three times a year (Spring/Summer, Fall, and Winter issues).The models featured in the free magazine are Waseda students. We handle everything ourselves: finding the models, putting together outfits, dressing them, photographing them, and using editing software to design the layout and visuals. We also raise our own funds through outreach efforts, securing sponsorships from companies and restaurants.
/
/ The club has a consistently friendly atmosphere, and everyone gets along very well regardless of seniority. We’re a fun group of people who love all kinds of fashion and culture!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
The Perspective Research Group is a club focused on architectural tours, primarily centered around Waseda University. Composed of members from various universities—including Japan Women’s University, Yokohama National University, Meiji University, and the University of Tokyo—we visit various buildings designed by famous architects, mainly in Tokyo, once a month. During spring and summer breaks, we hold two 4- or 5-night retreats to visit architectural sites not only in and around Tokyo but also in regional areas.
/
/
/
/By listening to explanations from senior members, you can experience architecture in a way that magazines and photos cannot convey. Through interaction and information exchange with students from other universities, you can gain a wealth of knowledge essential for thinking about architecture.
/
/
/
/Whether you want to study architecture, deepen your knowledge, are not in an architecture program, or are an international student, everyone is welcome to join!
活動日時・場所: Once a month (mainly Saturdays and Sundays) / Tokyo metropolitan area and surrounding areas (depending on the site visited)

名前: アニメーション同好会 (WALT)
活動内容:
We watch anime, read manga, play games, attend comic markets, and do many other things./

Waseda Animation Lovers Team (WALT) is a so-called ?consumption-oriented? circle that focuses on watching anime. The club is officially recognized by Waseda University and is provided with a club room. The club room is equipped with a computer where we can watch almost all kinds of anime, both past and current. WALT has no fixed activity days or hours, and members are free to come to the club room whenever they feel like it, allowing them to do circle activities according to their own schedule. One of the most important activities of this circle is ?participation in the Comic Market?. Members work together to produce and sell booklets at Comiket, which is also known as Comic Market.

名前: Waseda Model United Nations Research Group
活動内容: In a nutshell, Model United Nations is an activity that simulates international conferences. While Model UN events are held all over the world, the Waseda Model United Nations Society holds regular meetings every Tuesday during the 6th period at Waseda University. You can also participate in conference retreats, national tournaments, and international conferences held overseas! We’re just as dedicated to having fun as we are to the conferences, so we have plenty of fun events like recreational retreats. If you have any questions, please contact us via social media or email!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday / 6th & 7th periods / Student Union Building or nearby university facilities

活動内容: In addition to monthly events, we hold a monthly general meeting as well as volunteer-organized events such as lunch gatherings and study sessions. In recent years, we have also taken on new challenges, such as staging plays and producing films at the Waseda Festival. We also have our own club room where members can spend enjoyable time together between classes. Through these diverse activities, GLOW serves as a place where students from sexual minority backgrounds can form strong bonds with one another.
活動日時・場所: Daily, as needed. Not disclosed due to the nature of the club.

活動内容: This club consists of students from the Faculty of Human Sciences e-School, where e-learning is the primary method of study. Therefore, we recognize the need for a space for peer communication. Every year, we plan and execute numerous events to provide opportunities for members to share information and build camaraderie.Our main activities include the Spring Welcome Party, cheering at the Waseda-Keio game, study sessions during summer camp, and seminar review meetings. At the March Graduation Celebration, faculty and students come together to honor graduating seniors, sharing a meaningful time that serves as an opportunity to boost the academic motivation of current students. Moving forward, we will continue to strive for active engagement through these activities, serving as a “bridge of friendship and passion” among fellow distance learners.
活動日時・場所: Irregular / Student Union Building, Faculty of Human Sciences classrooms

活動内容: Under the vision of “Making sustainable fashion a lifestyle,” Rethink Fashion Waseda (ReF) shares information on sustainable fashion that is easy for students to incorporate into their daily lives via social media. By doing so, we aim to increase the number of people who think about and take action on fashion sustainability.On Instagram, our primary platform, we currently reach over 3,000 followers as of 2024. We also organize events (such as vintage clothing flea markets and beach cleanups) and collaborate with companies (including fashion magazine WWD, JanSport, and the Nikkei) to broaden our scope of learning and action, working to contribute to the creation of a sustainable society that is kinder to both the environment and people.
活動日時・場所: Last Sunday of the month / 9:00 PM / Online (Zoom)

活動内容:
We, the Advertising Research Society, view advertising as “something that moves people,” and we conduct daily research on how advertising can transform everyday life. The breadth of this definition directly translates to the breadth of our activities and the diversity of our members. As a result, there is certainly an activity within the Advertising Research Society that everyone will find appealing. Furthermore, because we bring together a diverse group of members from both cultural and athletic backgrounds, we can say that we are a group with a very strong sense of individuality.
/
/Furthermore, our history spanning over 100 years has fostered this diversity of people and activities. With a legacy dating back to 1913, we enjoy strong external trust, and our alumni are all individuals with impressive achievements. In this fertile environment, we not only create advertisements based on challenges provided by companies but also approach advertising from multiple angles, collaborating with university clubs, local shopping districts, and events.
/
/Advertising is meant to “move people”; it must not remain mere theoretical knowledge. Our work extends from creating content to sharing it with the outside world and ultimately inspiring action. Through communication with a wide range of people, we strive daily to share our advertising with Japan and use it to energize the nation. 　There is no such thing as “experience” in advertising production. What matters most are your individuality, your genuine passion, and the courage to take the plunge. There may be times when you find it tough. However, we take advertising seriously, seek out new possibilities, and continue to take on challenges. It is these daily experiences that create our irreplaceable memories.
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday and Friday / 6:30 PM – 9:00 PM / Classrooms and Student Union Building on the Waseda University campus

活動内容: The Broadcasting Research Society is the largest of Waseda University’s over 1,000 student clubs. Our main activities fall into two broad categories. The first involves utilizing video, audio, and lighting equipment, as well as announcing skills. We accept requests from various organizations both within and outside Waseda, providing equipment operation and MC services tailored to their specific needs.Notable examples include providing sound and serving as MCs for the Waseda-Keio baseball game, and operating the special stage at the Waseda Festival. The second area is content production and planning. We not only support performances and events organized by other groups but also develop our own plans and produce original content. Additionally, we hold an event called the “Program Presentation” every June and December to showcase the programs we have produced.Specifically, we plan comedy segments featuring guest comedians—such as manzai and ogiri—as well as performance segments like dance routines, and we handle the operations for these events ourselves. The Waseda University Broadcasting Research Society marks its 76th anniversary this year. The knowledge of equipment, production skills, and announcing techniques cultivated over our long history continue to be passed down without waning, even as our membership has grown. To further the development of the Broadcasting Research Society, each member actively participates in our activities.
活動日時・場所: Varies by day and time / Student Union Building

活動内容: We explore every aspect of broadcasting, ranging from basic exercises like articulation and vocal projection to free-talk practice, all the way to practical training in news reading, recitation, script reading, radio commercials, play-by-play commentary, MC work, reporting, and radio hosting. You can also practice using equipment for program production! The club has about 180 members, all of whom are Waseda University students, with a male-to-female ratio of roughly 1:1.We hold activities every day, and participation is open to all, making it easy to join while being part of other clubs. We also warmly welcome those who want to come every day and practice as much as possible! Our members have diverse interests: some are interested in voice acting, while others say, “No, I want to be an announcer,” “I just love talking,” or “I want to get better at speaking!”We also have quintessentially college-like activities that foster a sense of unity among all members, such as summer and spring training camps, production showcases, a satellite studio at Waseda Festival, and our own club graduation ceremony. You’ll find friends who share your goals and discover worlds you never knew existed! College life is a precious time, and experiencing a variety of things is incredibly important. Why not join the Announcing Research Club to develop the ability to share those experiences in a compelling way? More than any other experience, your voice will be your most powerful asset.
活動日時・場所: Every day (open to all!) / Student Union Building

活動内容: "Shining a light on every athletic club." The Waseda Sports Newspaper Club (Waseda Sports) covers all 44 athletic clubs affiliated with Waseda University, conveying the appeal of Waseda sports through our newspaper, website, and various social media platforms! From interviewing athletes and writing match reports to photographing games in action and producing a professional-quality newspaper, we offer a wealth of experiences unique to Waseda Sports.Through on-site newspaper distribution and social media, our articles and photos are widely viewed by people outside the university as well. Having been published continuously since our founding and long beloved by the community, our newspaper will reach its milestone 600th issue with this year’s Waseda-Keio Baseball (Spring) edition! We also hold many fun events beyond reporting, such as training camps and sports tournaments. This is a club where everyone can thrive—not just sports enthusiasts, but also those interested in media, image production, or photography. We warmly welcome new members at any time.We look forward to seeing you at our casual welcome events and welcome your inquiries!
活動日時・場所: (Times vary by activity) Various tournament venues / Student Union Building / To-Nichi Printing

活動内容: FM Waseda is an officially recognized Waseda University club focused on radio program production! We broadcast programs created in a variety of formats. From radio hosts to mixers (sound engineers), directors, scriptwriters, and voice actors for radio dramas, all production activities are handled entirely by students.Our activities are diverse, including broadcasting radio programs at restaurants and online, participating in broadcasting contests, and hosting events at the Waseda Festival. We also hold club retreats about twice a year. Since we teach how to use recording equipment from the very beginning, even beginners can get involved right away. As long as you have the motivation to “create something interesting,” anyone can join in immediately. That’s FM Waseda.
活動日時・場所: Activities held as needed / Monthly regular meetings / Student Union Building

名前: Science and Engineering Exhibition Liaison Committee
活動内容: We, the Rikou-ten Liaison Committee, are a festival planning club responsible for organizing and running "Rikou-ten," the annual Waseda University School of Science and Engineering festival held in early November. We meet every Saturday to prepare for the event. We are one of the largest clubs exclusively for students in the School of Science and Engineering.Since members come from all faculties and departments within the School of Science and Engineering, we provide a very welcoming environment for students in the school. We also organize activities outside of regular meetings, such as going out to eat after practice, three annual trips, and club events, allowing you to build a wide network of friendships. The highlight of the Rikou-ten Liaison Committee is the “breadth of our activities.” Compared to high school festivals, university festivals involve a much wider scope of work, and we build everything from scratch ourselves.You’ll be involved not only in planning for the day of the festival but also in fundraising, event promotion, equipment setup, and staffing—aspects you likely never encountered at high school festivals. Of course, building everything from the ground up isn’t easy, but the sense of accomplishment when you pull it off is beyond what you can imagine. We’re looking for teammates to join us in working toward the goal of “making the festival a success.” If you’re interested in the Science and Engineering Festival Liaison Committee, check out our website and social media for details on our various recruitment events. We look forward to seeing you there!
活動日時・場所: Every Saturday / 1:00 PM – 5:00 PM / Classrooms on the Nishi-Waseda Campus

活動内容: The Waseda University People Research Society aims to interview prominent figures active in various fields. By conducting these interviews ourselves, we seek to cover our subjects from a perspective different from that of the mass media, bringing out a side of them that has never been seen before.Our specific activities include selecting interviewees, scheduling appointments, conducting interviews, and writing reports. Members provide friendly and thorough support regarding how to carry out these activities, so anyone can feel confident about getting started. It is a vibrant environment where we respect each other’s opinions while striving to improve together. In addition to our regular interview activities, we organize an annual lecture series during the Waseda Festival. Here, all members work together as one to create a single event, so I believe there is a great sense of accomplishment once it is over.
活動日時・場所: Irregular

活動内容: We are Benrisha, an officially recognized planning club at Waseda University!We invite celebrities and notable figures to host talk shows and events about five times a year—in April, July, and during the Waseda Festival. We handle everything ourselves, from planning and conceptualization to actual event management. Here’s how it works: First, we hold a competition where members present the projects they want to organize. There are no restrictions on these proposals—you can present any idea you like, whether it’s based on your hobbies or features a celebrity you’d like to invite.Once a project is selected, we handle everything from booking the guest to coordinating meetings ourselves. While this keeps us busy, it provides invaluable experience. During our regular meetings, all club members brainstorm ideas for the event’s content and work together to refine them through hands-on testing. As the event date approaches, we spend entire days preparing, creating slides and videos for the event. Since we operate the video and sound equipment ourselves, we also practice during rehearsals.During the actual event, you might even get to chat with guests backstage or get their autographs! Seniors will teach you everything about production and operation, so beginners need not worry. We also host the “Waseda King Championship” every year, which sends Waseda Festival into a frenzy. This competition to determine who is the most “Waseda-like” is the highlight of Waseda Festival. Information about our events is updated regularly on our official social media accounts.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday & Friday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building Conference Room

名前: Waseda University Anime Voice Actor Club
活動内容: In the past, we have organized events for titles such as *Mahou Sensei Negima!*, *Sayonara Zetsubou-sensei*, and *Invasion! Ika Musume*, as well as the "Ayana Taketatsu & Yuiko Tatsumi Talk Event in Waseda," attracting around 600 attendees annually.Furthermore, since the 2007 academic year, we have organized unique events that set us apart from other anime-related clubs, such as hosting free lectures featuring industry professionals involved in anime and anime song production, including Shinichi Watanabe, Junichi Sato, Aki Hata, and Hikaru Kondo.These activities are not just about hosting events related to the anime you all love; they also allow us to leverage our status as a university club to experience new worlds, savor the sense of accomplishment and camaraderie that comes from achieving something together with friends, and create fulfilling memories. Planning and managing an event involves handling a wide range of tasks, from negotiating with companies and public relations to managing finances, as well as organizing guest entry and reception on the day of the event. Such valuable experiences are rare, and they will undoubtedly serve as a valuable asset for you all.If you love anime, voice actors, or are simply “interested in organizing events,” why not try your hand at being on the organizing side? We sincerely look forward to welcoming enthusiastic individuals.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday (including Fridays in October) / 5:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
The Waseda Festival Organizing Staff (Matsuri Staff) is the organization that hosts and operates the Waseda Festival, one of Japan’s largest university festivals. Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Waseda Festival was an annual celebration of Waseda culture, boasting approximately 200,000 visitors and over 400 events. Even during the pandemic, we have continued to create a space where Waseda culture can flourish through online and hybrid events.Each year, we set a theme that defines the “essence of Waseda,” which serves as the guiding spirit for that year’s festival.
/
/
/
/We are a very large organization consisting of approximately 600 members.Our diverse activities span various specialties, including venue setup on the days of the Waseda Festival, support for participating groups and individuals, liaison activities with external organizations, public relations and design work for the festival, planning and execution of staff-led events, exploration of new areas, and management of internal resources and funds. Guided by the motto of student-led self-management, all members work together as one toward the annual two-day festival.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Thursday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Waseda Illumination Project Executive Committee (WIP) was established in 2005. Originally an official university project aimed at fostering exchange with international students, it is now run primarily by students. We engage in creative activities using illuminations in preparation for the Waseda Festival, and we decorate the area around the university with illuminations while interacting and collaborating with local residents.To date, we have created the “Glowing Waseda Bear” and collaborated with the J1 soccer team Kawasaki Frontale. The connections formed as students and local residents share ideas and work together are what this project values most. Moving forward, WIP will continue to create smiles among people connected by light at Waseda.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday & Friday / 6:15 PM / Main Campus, Student Union Building

活動内容: We, Wase Pro, are an officially recognized Waseda University club that plans and operates Waseda Collection (commonly known as Wase-Kore), the largest fashion event at Waseda. With the goal of dispelling the image that Waseda women are plain and unstylish, and to showcase the stylish, glamorous, and unique charm of Waseda women, we discover and feature Waseda student designers and models, holding professional fashion shows several times a year.This year marks the 10th anniversary of Waseda Collection, and over the years, the event has launched the careers of many individuals who have gone on to succeed in a wide range of fields, including modeling and broadcasting.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday / 6th & 7th periods / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are a Waseda University-recognized, intercollegiate (students from other universities welcome) “internal event planning club.”While there are many other planning clubs at Waseda University, what sets us apart is that we are “internal.” In other words, we are a planning club where “we create events for ourselves, and we enjoy them ourselves.” Guided by the slogan “Let’s do something silly we can brag about tomorrow,” we seriously plan ridiculous activities that we can boast about to our friends the next day.Walkin’ is a “dream-fulfilling” club where you can do anything you want—even things you’ve always wanted to do but couldn’t. What you couldn’t do as an “I” might be possible as a “We.” That’s the idea. Examples: Tuna dissection show, real-life escape games, “On the Run,” airsoft using mackerel, can-kicking championship, hands-free travel, and more.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: At TEDxWasedaU, we strive to contribute to TED’s vision of having “Ideas worth spreading.” TEDxWasedaU provides a platform for students from different backgrounds, nationalities, and faculties to come together and share innovative and valuable ideas. The four teams, the finance team, speaker team, design team, and marketing team, work together to make our bilingual events come to life. We mainly work towards our Student Speaker Competition and Main Event. We prep our guest speakers to go through our Student Speaker Competition and eventually to our Main Event, where they can present their speeches on a larger platform. The Main Event brings together people from various professions, backgrounds, and interests to discuss what they are passionate about and spread the word about various social issues. Past events have included participants speaking on topics such as solutions to reducing CO2 emissions, the art of Kintsugi in Japan, and the importance of preserving aging towns.

活動内容:
We are a circle working to solve the problem of litter in the rotary square in front of Takadanobaba Station! Our main activities include cleaning up the area on weekday mornings and night, collaborating with businesses and the shopping district to plan projects, displaying posters and holding exhibitions to spread awareness of the problem, and making policy proposals to Shinjuku City regarding the rotary.

In recent years, the issue of drinking on the street at the Corona Disaster has been raised and the Takadanobaba Station roundabout has been reported in news programs, bringing our Rotary club into the public eye. We are one of the most growing clubs in Waseda University, and have been featured not only on TV but also in newspaper articles and other media! Many of those who have seen the above news reports have taken it as a sign that it is Waseda University students who are polluting the rotary. Waseda University students have a close relationship with Rotary. We, the students of Waseda University, are the ones who can eliminate the garbage problem.

You don't have to be a member to participate in the cleanup, so if you want to get up early in the morning, if you have something to do nearby, or if you feel like starting something new, please feel free to visit us!
