活動内容: This club prepares for stage magic performances held three times a year. The performances are: the "Family Party" in June by second-year students, the "Magical Network" in September by first-year students, and the "Annual Performance" in November by third-year students, with all students from each grade participating. Other club members also support these events as staff, and everyone works together to create the performances.While there are rehearsals and other activities as the performance dates approach, our schedule is generally flexible. This makes it easy to balance club activities with part-time jobs or other clubs—a key feature of our group. Since most members had no prior magic experience when they joined, anyone can enjoy fulfilling and fun club activities here.
活動日時・場所: Irregular / Student Union Building E637

活動内容: We are the IT club with the longest history at Waseda University! Even if you’ve never programmed before, our senior members with specialized knowledge will teach you patiently, allowing you to improve step by step. In addition to programming, we engage in network and server setup, and recently, as part of our computer-based activities, we’ve been working on IoT, CG rendering, and DTM. Since we decide our activities every six months based on what each member wants to do, you’ll have the opportunity to learn what you’re interested in in a specialized way. Our regular activities take place in our club room located in the Student Union Building. Since computers are available there, even those without laptops can participate in programming and other activities. The room also serves as a gathering place for members to socialize during breaks between classes.
活動日時・場所: Anytime / Student Union Building E-731

活動内容: The Management Information Systems Society (MISW) is Waseda’s largest comprehensive creative club, handling a wide range of digital content including programming, CG illustration, and computer music composition. Members belong to one of three groups within the club: the Programming Research Group, which serves as the core of game development; the CG Research Group, which focuses on illustration production; or the MIDI Research Group, which handles computer music composition.After joining, members typically form game production teams called “projects” to develop various games and application software for distribution events such as the Waseda Festival and Comic Market. Beyond game production, the club engages in a wide range of activities, including distributing art books and music CDs created in-house, as well as posting music videos featuring VOCALOID tracks on external platforms like Niconico Video and YouTube.In recent years, our activities have expanded beyond the three fields mentioned earlier. New initiatives—such as 3D CG modeling, Unity development, scenario writing, and video production—are being pursued in line with members’ interests and goals. Another strength of our group is our system where experienced members provide careful guidance to beginners. Come join MISW to realize new forms of creativity!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday and Friday / 6:15 PM – 7:45 PM / Nishi-Waseda Campus, Room 52-101

活動内容: A highly prestigious Banzai-style club founded in 1971. With a mission to "rush to celebratory events across the country, make them even more festive, and have a blast ourselves in the midst of it all," the club devotes itself day and night to mastering 768 different types of Banzai (as of 2016).We have a track record of performing nationwide, primarily as entertainment at welcome/farewell parties, award ceremonies, and weddings, with the total number of annual requests easily exceeding 50. We also have extensive experience appearing in various media outlets, including television and newspapers, and are known for our surprisingly high profile despite our shrouded, mysterious nature.Their primary activities involve researching and developing "banzai" techniques in their clubroom (currently Student Union Building E709). Through annual training camps and performances at various events, members gain practical experience and develop exceptional "banzai" skills.
活動日時・場所: Celebratory venues nationwide / Student Union Building E709

活動内容: Quizzes for beginners on Mondays and for experienced players on Tuesdays. On other days, various sub-groups within the club—such as Intro Quiz—are active! Our unique members are waiting for you!

活動内容: We, the Comedy Workshop LUDO, are a comedy club that uses our monthly live shows—held primarily at Waseda—as an opportunity to showcase our material. Through weekly meetings held twice a week, we practice and perform our routines. In addition to performers, we have many staff members who support the live shows in areas such as video, lighting, and sound. All club members work together to create these live shows, which are enjoyed by many audience members.We have won the National College Comedy Championship multiple times, and some members are actively pursuing professional careers. We deliver high-quality live shows in both content and scale, so please come and see us perform. Additionally, we accept applications year-round via email for both performers and staff, so please feel free to contact us. We welcome applicants regardless of experience, university, gender, age, or nationality.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday at 6:00 PM and Saturday at 4:30 PM / Classrooms at Waseda University

活動内容: The Waseda University Drama Club (commonly known as Waseda Drama Club) is an officially recognized drama club at Waseda University, based in its own dedicated studio behind Okuma Auditorium. Its origins date back to before World War II, and it is known as the oldest drama club at Waseda.Because members not only act but also build the stages and seating areas themselves, the club has an abundance of materials and is equipped with sound and lighting systems, boasting the largest scale and most impressive track record on campus. In this privileged environment, the club has produced many notable figures in film and theater, including the currently popular Masato Sakai, playwright and director Naofumi Kogami—a leading figure in the theater world—and, in the past, film director Shohei Imai.Furthermore, unlike other theater clubs, it employs an “ensemble system” that allows members to form their own theater companies within the club. Under this system, it has produced numerous influential and popular troupes, including Daisan Butai, Yamanote Jijo-sha, Soshū Shimai, and Brazil. Most recently, at the end of last year, Tokyo Junk Z—renowned for its entertainment value—graduated from the club.Consequently, efforts to establish the next ensemble have intensified since last year. From May to June 2016, they organized a project titled “Mitsuba Planning Performance Collection,” in which three young directors staged three distinct productions in a single month. Since then, they have continued to actively organize performances and are engaged in enthusiastic activities.
活動日時・場所: Irregular

活動内容:
We accept commissions from both within Waseda University and external organizations to handle stage design and lighting for plays, musicals, and dance performances. We also hold performances organized by the Stage Design Research Society twice a year. Most members join as beginners, but under the guidance of senior members, they can acquire specialized skills.
/
/We hold a general meeting once a month, but other activities are irregular, so you can participate according to your own schedule.We accept new members at any time, regardless of age, year in school, or university.
/
/If you want to try something different, love theater, enjoy creative activities, or want to join a highly specialized club…
/
/If that sounds like you, please come visit our studio behind the Okuma Memorial Hall!
/
/Let’s have fun working together!
/
/Please view the Stage Design Research Society website in desktop layout. We ask that you submit requests via the website.
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Studio behind Okuma Memorial Hall

活動内容: We are a traditional Kabuki appreciation club with a history spanning over 70 years. Our "club creed" states: "Students must appreciate and study Kabuki strictly from the audience’s perspective, and use that perspective to voice opinions and make suggestions." True to these words, we have remained dedicated to "exclusively watching performances" since our founding, and our activities center around group viewings at venues such as the Kabukiza Theater.In recent years, we have actively engaged in exchanges with kabuki study groups at other universities. One of our attractions is our diverse membership, ranging from kabuki beginners to die-hard fans. Additionally, our clubroom houses a wide collection of valuable materials on kabuki, which individual members are free to browse, allowing them to truly “research” kabuki as our name suggests.Why not join us in watching and fully experiencing Kabuki—a performing art that Japan proudly presents to the world, embodying the appeal of both tradition and innovation? New members are welcome at any time.
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Primarily at theaters such as the Kabuki-za

活動内容:
This is a historic theater troupe with its own dedicated studio located behind Waseda University’s Okuma Auditorium. At Waseda University, only the “Kodama” Theater Troupe and the Drama Research Society have their own dedicated studios.Since it’s an atelier exclusive to “Kodama,” we can devote ourselves to theater 365 days a year! Our alumni include many prominent figures across various fields, and in recent years, we’ve been actively organizing workshops with actors from other troupes and professional actors, as well as two-city tour performances!
/
/Students from other universities and working professionals are also very welcome!
活動日時・場所: Irregular / After school / Kodama Theater Group Studio (behind Waseda University’s Okuma Auditorium)

活動内容:
Established around 1960. The character "森" is read as "Shin," but none of the troupe members know the origin of the name.
/
/It is one of the six major theater clubs at Waseda University and has the largest membership.
/
/The troupe holds three main performances a year (a spring welcome performance, a summer newcomer performance, and one additional show) as well as several special projects (held irregularly). Since the playwright and director change with each performance, the troupe does not have a unified artistic direction; however, it stages a wide variety of productions ranging from underground theater to contemporary spoken-word theater, and this diversity is a hallmark of its performances.
/
/Members can gain experience across a wide range of roles—from acting to crew work (lighting, sound, set design, stage management, and production), as well as playwriting and directing—allowing you to tailor your theater activities to your interests. Another key feature is the group’s open atmosphere, which encourages members to freely participate in external productions, propose their own projects, and get involved whenever they wish.
/
/We welcome anyone, regardless of year, university, age, or profession. If you’ve ever thought about trying theater, please come check us out!
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Student Union Building

活動内容:
In 1971, the Concerto Theater Company was founded by Professor Tatiana Nomura, who taught Russian at the University of Tokyo and Waseda University, along with her students. It began as a "cultural festival = Concerto" aimed at fostering exchange through Russian language activities such as skits, poetry recitations, and choral singing, and gradually began to take on full-scale plays.Currently based at Waseda University, the troupe brings together students studying Russian from other universities as well, and continues to hold two regular performances a year (a debut performance and a main performance).
/
/
/
/Since 1999, the group has received professional instruction in pronunciation and acting from Belarusian director Natalia Barshai. In recent years, they have staged productions such as *The Living Corpse* (Tolstoy), *Stars of the Dawn* (Garin), and *The Gift of the Wise Bee* (Sologup).
/
/
/
/Complete beginners are welcome! All of our senior members started learning both Russian and theater only after entering university. If you’re interested in Russia, the Russian language, or foreign-language theater, you’re more than welcome to join—regardless of which university you attend!
/
/
/
/You can join at any time. Feel free to start by observing a rehearsal! Please don’t hesitate to contact us!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday & Thursday / 6:00 PM / Waseda University Toyama Campus Student Union Building & Tokyo University of Foreign Studies Tama Campus

活動内容: This theater club has produced members who went on to join groups such as "Theater Group Caramel Box" and "Theater Company Rappaya." In addition to the main performance in May, the newcomer showcase in September, and the newcomer project performance in March, members can organize their own project performances at any time. A major feature of the club is that all members, not just actors, have the opportunity to gain experience as staff.
活動日時・場所: Irregular; varies by performance. Club Room: E537

活動内容: We are a Waseda University-recognized musical theater club that stages existing musicals several times a year! Omnibus is an intercollegiate club, so while Waseda students are naturally part of the group, we also have members from various other universities. We usually practice musicals together in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere.Don’t worry if you have no experience with singing or dancing! Everyone starts as a beginner. Seeing the results of our practice come to life on stage is nothing short of moving! It would be a shame to miss out on the joy of performing on stage! But of course, that’s not all. As an entertainment-focused musical theater club, Omnibus offers a packed schedule of events!! From fireworks festivals and summer training camps to Halloween parties, we have plenty of diverse events throughout the year.If you want to enjoy college life but feel like just partying isn’t enough—Omnibus is the place for you! Here, you can experience both the sense of accomplishment from creating a show together and the fun of hanging out and having a blast with everyone! Every day with Omnibus is like “a cultural festival every day”! Why not spend four dream-like years with us?
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday, Friday, and Saturday / Tuesdays & Fridays from 6:30 PM, Saturdays from 4:30 PM / Student Union Building and other locations near Waseda

活動内容: Fresh men practice and learn about theater performing in summer for three months, and act in the stage of fresh men. After finishing the stage, the members can continue to serch for the form of theater performances that they want.

活動内容:
Mime Mai☆Yume☆To is a performance group founded in 1985 by professional street performer Happy Yoshizawa.
Going beyond the scope of a typical college club, the group welcomes students from other universities and working professionals to participate in acting and performances centered around mime.
Under the unique guidance of Happy Yoshizawa, members learn the charm of pantomime—expressing stories using only their bodies—and a steady stream of distinctive performers is emerging.
Our main activities include performances at the Waseda Festival in November and our solo show, “Mime Tou Live,” in March. We also perform at various venues, such as “Nextou Live” (which features alumni) and off-campus events.
We warmly welcome anyone interested in theater or performance, those looking to try something new in college, and anyone who loves fun and creative activities!
Most of our members started mime during their time at university.
Please feel free to come try out a rehearsal. We look forward to hearing from you!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday, Friday, and Sunday / 5:00 PM (You may join or leave at any time) / Student Union Building

活動内容: Kurumeru Theater is one of the six major theater clubs at Waseda University. We cover a wide range of genres and styles, and by leveraging our large membership, we stage three main performances a year, as well as numerous special productions. There is no strict training regimen; instead, a diverse group of individuals comes together to enjoy theater in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere. Some members are active in external groups or have even started their own theater companies. There are also many active alumni theater groups.Beyond theater, we gather in our clubroom for casual chats, attend fireworks festivals, and go on retreats—allowing you to fully enjoy university life alongside your peers. Of course, it’s easy to balance these activities with your classes, and everyone participates at their own pace. It’s a club where you can enjoy yourself freely. We warmly welcome you to Kurumeru!
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Student Union Building / Waseda Small Theater "Dorama-kan"

活動内容: We assist other organizations and clubs with loading and unloading items for events. By helping out when staff shortages prevent smooth loading and unloading or when large quantities of items need to be moved, we help alleviate staffing shortages for other groups and clubs.Many of our members have experience handling items frequently used at other groups’ and clubs’ events—such as lumber, wood products, and various types of equipment—which allows us to provide smooth and safe assistance. Furthermore, since we typically have a sufficient number of active members each year, we are able to deepen our connections with other clubs and organizations while engaging in our activities.
活動日時・場所: Irregular

活動内容: We hold performances about 1 to 3 times a year. We use the Student Union Building and the Waseda Small Theater "Dorama-kan" as performance venues. Rehearsals are also held at the Student Union Building. The timing of performances is not fixed annually; we book venues and set rehearsal schedules based on when members are available to put on a show. As mentioned in the introduction, we frequently hold joint performances with other clubs.We collaborate with various groups and individuals, including staff and actors, to create the best possible performances. Specifically, we rehearse 4–6 days a week starting 2–3 months before a performance. Although we are a theater club, members are welcome to join other clubs as well, and we have a very relaxed atmosphere where each person can choose which productions they want to be involved in. Since our membership isn’t particularly large, we have a friendly and welcoming atmosphere.
活動日時・場所: 4–6 times a week (during performance periods) / 6th and 7th periods / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are a theater club that rehearses at the Student Union Building. About once a year, we collaborate with other theater groups to put on a performance at the Student Union Building. We start preparing about two months before the performance, rehearsing 5–6 times a week to create the production together. Many of our members are new to theater, so we learn and improve through trial and error as we perform. Additionally, many members belong to other clubs as well, and since they have a long period of flexibility in their schedules, each member engages in a variety of activities. For last March’s performance, we welcomed actors from other groups and staged a completely original 90-minute full-length play featuring a diverse cast, free of charge. We also took on new challenges, such as placing musical instruments on stage and holding pre-show performances. We put a lot of effort into publicity, and all five performances sold out, making it a huge success.
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Weekdays: 6th–7th periods; Saturdays & Sundays: 3rd–7th periods / Student Union Building

活動内容:
The largest musical club in the country creating the best student musicals.

Our slogan is ?Your chance to be a part of it. To achieve this, our activity guidelines are (1) The best musical students can do, (2) A place where everyone can be serious, and (3) Creating a musical culture at Waseda University. In order to achieve these goals, in addition to the main performance three times a year (August, December, and March), we also put on intra-company performances, extra-company performances, and welcome performances for new students. In addition to stage performances, we perform on the Waseda Festival stage and other venues. For the main performance, we invite professional instructors and technical staff to provide a high level of instruction. Members of the troupe are not only cast members but also staff members. In addition to the staff work for each performance, there are also departmental tasks that the troupe members perform throughout the year: props, production, public relations, administration, and costume department. The company also offers dance training, voice training, and other workshops to help beginners develop their skills.

活動内容: Theater Group 24-ku focuses on putting on three performances a year (summer performances in June–July, fall performances in November, and spring performances in February–March). Anyone is welcome to join, including theater beginners, upperclassmen, working adults, students from other universities, international students, and those busy balancing classes or part-time jobs. We especially recommend this group to those thinking of starting theater in college. There are no restrictions on joining other clubs, training schools, or agencies at the same time.You can also join solely as a staff member or volunteer. However, since we are a small troupe, members are expected to serve in both casting and staff roles. There are no annual fees, and you can participate in as few as one performance. Rehearsal days are determined for each individual performance. The script and direction change with every production, so the genre varies each time. We also hold various other events every year (such as training camps and graduation parties).
活動日時・場所: Days vary (twice on weekdays, once on weekends) / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are one of the newer theater clubs at Waseda. This year marks our 10th anniversary. While we still have a relatively low standing among theater clubs, we are not bound by tradition, and all members enjoy a relaxed and free atmosphere. Our motto is to hold regular practices that are neither too lax nor too strict, but always fun. We welcome members who belong to other clubs as well, and many of our members are active in various other groups.We aim to be a theater club where people who want to do as much as possible during their short college years—and for whom theater is one of those things—can join without hesitation, so we do not impose excessive restrictions. In return, we ask that members take responsibility and work seriously whenever they are involved in a project. Every December, we hold a joint performance with the theater troupe Teatro 50’.
活動日時・場所: Irregular / Around 6:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are the newest comedy club at Waseda University. In addition to holding regular live shows at least six times a year, we also perform at Waseda Festival and various other events. Furthermore, by participating in live show competitions against other universities and tournaments hosted by external organizations, you’ll greatly expand your social circle. We recommend this club to anyone who wants to “express themselves fully in front of an audience,” “learn to speak confidently in front of large crowds,” or “simply make friends who love comedy.”Why not join us in imitating the manzai and sketch comedians you see on TV? Of course, you can also join the staff to handle sound and lighting or create flyers. Many of our staff members are people who love comedy but are a bit shy. Furthermore, POP3 warmly welcomes students from other universities! We don’t discriminate based on year level! Our group is made up of members from diverse years and academic backgrounds!! Let’s have fun doing comedy together!!

We aim to hold performances about five times a year. Recently, we have been actively expanding our activities by holding performances at the Waseda Campus and local public facilities. Experience is not required at all, and the club’s greatest appeal is the opportunity to enjoy theater in a fun and welcoming environment.

As the first film club in the Kanto region, it attracts highly motivated and skilled filmmakers from many universities. With a wealth of filming equipment, external connections, and talented people, nothing is impossible for the Film Society, and in FY2022, we realized an international production with Inha University in South Korea. We need many support members as well as aspiring directors, producers, actors, and screenwriters. Video shooting/lighting/sound/music/editing/hair/make-up/costume/still photography/poster design/vehicle department driver, etc. All are just to mention a few. 活動内容: The Inamon Screenplay Research Society (hereinafter referred to as "Shinaken") is a club that produces independent films. Despite its formal-sounding name, Shinaken’s defining characteristic is, above all, its freedom. Club members shoot films across a wide range of genres and are free to express whatever they find interesting. We have a full range of equipment, including cameras, microphones, and lighting, so you can start making films as soon as you join.Some members have been active since their freshman year. The club includes many students from other universities and international students, and many join partway through the academic year. We accept new members year-round. Feel free to contact us via Twitter or visit our clubroom (Student Union Building, Room E619) in person. We warmly welcome anyone interested in trying their hand at directing, screenwriting, acting, or cinematography.

活動内容: We are the film production club "CineCycle Hantouno." Our activities include shooting several films a year and organizing trips to movie theaters. A distinctive feature of our club is that "the members get along very well." Not only during shoots, but even on days when we aren’t filming, we always hang out and relax together in our private clubroom, E525.While the films we produce tend to have a comedic tone, some directors also create more serious, professional-quality works. Since we’re a relatively small film club, we have access to equipment whenever we want, providing an environment where members can shoot freely whenever they feel like it. We also hold summer and winter retreats, where the filming team shoots while the rest of the members go sightseeing. We work hard when we shoot, and relax the rest of the time. That’s the kind of club we are.

活動内容: We pursue our interests at our own pace and with our own passion. We make movies, watch movies, and have lively yet relaxed discussions about them. Whether you want to make movies or just watch them, everyone is welcome! We’re a club that respects each member’s comfort level. Broadly speaking, our activities fall into three categories: “Screenings,” “Filming,” and “Events.”Screenings are our flagship event, held twice a week. Members choose the movies they want to watch, and we all enjoy them together using a projector and speakers! We also do film production, of course. Many of us are beginners, so we create our works together through trial and error! For our events, we plan outings to watch movies or go out and have fun together! We have a club room, so please come visit us sometime. We’re active on X, Instagram, and YouTube (where you can find our past works), so please search for our club name!

活動内容: Cinema Production is an officially recognized film club at Waseda University. We boast the largest membership among the many film clubs on campus and are well-equipped with filming gear. We have strong connections with upperclassmen, and members sometimes get the opportunity to work on shoots directed by professional filmmakers. Whether you want to try your hand at directing, acting, or cinematography, this is a club where you can pursue your interests freely.We frequently collaborate with other film clubs on shoots, and every winter we participate in the “Waseda Film Festival,” an open competition organized by Waseda’s film clubs. In addition to the “Waseda Film Festival,” we consistently achieve outstanding results at many renowned film festivals each year. Our regular activities include weekly meetings, and during weekends and long breaks, we engage in film production activities such as shooting and editing.
活動日時・場所: Every Thursday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are the Video Production Group "Ronin-gai." We are a club dedicated to making films. Membership is not limited to students preparing for entrance exams. Our main activities consist of regular meetings held about three times a month (on days ending in 9) and ad-hoc filming sessions. You might be curious about these "ad-hoc filming sessions." They generally take place on days off when we have free time or during long vacations.During summer and spring breaks, we might head out to shoot somewhere far away, or we might stay here and work intensively. We have everything you need to shoot a movie. I guarantee it. We have high-quality equipment. You can count on our solid technical skills. And there are probably some wonderful people here who’ll help you out. Once the script is ready, the cast and crew are assembled, and the shooting location and equipment are secured, we start shooting. And you could say the movie is basically complete once we get through the editing and screening.After that, depending on individual preferences, we submit the film to film festivals or similar competitions. Whether you want to shoot, direct, act, edit, collaborate with others to create something, leave a lasting legacy, or are just curious—everyone is welcome. It’s a great feeling to see something you’ve been a part of take shape, no matter the form. I personally recommend it. Ronin-gai.
活動日時・場所: Every day of the month ending in 9 (e.g., 4/9, 4/19, 4/29) / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building; filming takes place as needed

Our videos are available on our official YouTube channel.Our hero shows are centered around the Waseda Festival, but we also perform at local festivals, various events, and even visit kindergartens. We also occasionally make guest appearances in TV commercials and music videos. We welcome everyone—whether you love kaiju, heroes, or are simply a tokusatsu fan, as well as those interested in acting, crafting, entertaining others, or working with children! This is a club where you can do whatever you want!

名前: Waseda University Symphony Orchestra (Wase-Oke) Tokorozawa Branch
活動内容: The Waseda University Symphony Orchestra, affectionately known as "Wase-Oke," is Waseda University’s official orchestra. It is the only officially recognized orchestra composed exclusively of undergraduate students from the university, with a total membership of approximately 250.Founded in 1913 and celebrating its 100th anniversary in 2013, the orchestra held the “Waseda University Symphony Orchestra 100th Anniversary Concert Series” (five concerts in total) from April 2012 to March 2013.Its main activities include hosting 4 to 5 concerts per year and performing at Waseda University’s official events and cultural programs, such as entrance and graduation ceremonies. In addition, the orchestra performs at 20 to 30 commissioned events annually. Since winning the 5th International Youth Orchestra Competition (commonly known as the Karajan Competition) in 1978, the orchestra has performed overseas 14 times.During the “Europe Tour 2015” held from February to March 2015, the orchestra toured 13 cities in Germany, Austria, and France, receiving enthusiastic acclaim in each location. In particular, the March 8 performance in Berlin was broadcast live worldwide via the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra’s “Digital Concert Hall” internet service, following previous broadcasts in 2009 and 2012.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday / 6:15 PM / Various rehearsal venues

活動内容:
The Waseda University Symphony Orchestra, affectionately known as "Wase-Oke," is the university’s officially recognized orchestra. It is the only on-campus orchestra composed exclusively of undergraduate students, with a membership of approximately 250.In 2023, the orchestra celebrated its 110th anniversary, marking the occasion with the “Waseda University Symphony Orchestra 110th Anniversary Special Concert in Osaka” held in March of that year. Additionally, from late February 2024, the orchestra embarked on the “Europe Tour 2024,” visiting nine cities across Germany and Austria, where it was met with great acclaim.The orchestra performs four to five times a year in its own concerts, as well as at official university events, cultural programs, and external commissions.
/
/Since winning the 5th International Youth Orchestra Competition in 1978—an event that served as the catalyst for the orchestra’s overseas performance activities—the late Herbert von Karajan supported the orchestra in various ways.When Waseda University awarded him an honorary doctorate in 1979, he conducted an open rehearsal of R. Strauss’s symphonic poem “Till Eulenspiegel’s Merry Pranks” at Okuma Auditorium.
/
/In addition, we have welcomed the late Giuseppe Sinopoli, Simon Rattle, Seiji Ozawa, the late Zdeněk Košler, Leonard Slatkin, the late Hiroyuki Iwaki, Naoto Otomo, Ken Takaseki, Kazufumi Yamashita,Daisuke Soga, and Kiyotaka Teraoka. As instructors and fellow performers, we have welcomed many individuals, primarily members of the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra and the NHK Symphony Orchestra.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday / 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM / Near Waseda

活動内容: The Mandolin Club is a traditional music club with a proud 103-year history. The mandolin is an Italian string instrument characterized by its tremolo technique; it is a charming instrument both in appearance and tone. The orchestra consists of mandolins, mandolas, mandoloncelli, classical guitars, double basses, flutes, and clarinets.We hold three major concerts a year, one of which is a joint concert with Keio University’s Mandolin Club, fostering active exchange between our groups. We also host internal recitals where members freely perform their favorite pieces, as well as outreach performances (in 2016, we held a reconstruction support concert in Ofunato and Rikuzentakata). Both experienced players and beginners are welcome (we are only recruiting experienced players for the wind sections). More than half of our members are beginners. We also have a history of producing many professional musicians. Below are some of the highlights of our club: Free instrument rental. The club room is available anytime with a Waseda student ID, and it’s spacious. Members can join other clubs or participate in intercollegiate competitions. Members get along well with seniors, juniors, and peers, and often hang out together outside of club activities.Compared to other music clubs, our fees are on the lower side. You can receive instruction from professional instructors for each section. Upperclassmen provide one-on-one lessons for beginners, so even if you can’t read sheet music, you’ll be fine. Since there are many female members, the atmosphere is relatively calm; perhaps because there are few male members, the bond among them is strong. …The list goes on and on, but we always have fun during our activities. If you’re interested, please stop by Student Union Building B117 anytime!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday and Friday / 4:30 PM – 8:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are a club that performs in a big band format centered around the harmonica. Our sections are as follows: Harmonica (single, horn), Flute, Clarinet, Guitar, Bass, Keyboard, Drums & Percussion. We cover a wide range of genres, including J-Pop, Western music, and wind ensemble pieces, allowing us to play whatever songs we want. We hold concerts about twice a year (in June and December).For our June concert, we hold a joint concert with Chuo University, Meiji University, and Rikkyo University. Our December concert is a regular concert held exclusively by Waseda University. In addition to concerts, we sometimes perform at the Waseda Festival. We also hold training camps in the spring and summer, where we practice and bond through activities like fireworks, BBQs, and arrangement contests.

活動内容: We, the Latin American Association—commonly known as “Lateame”—study the cultures of Latin American countries, particularly Brazil.In our activities, we place particular emphasis on the study of musical culture. We enjoy playing and dancing to a wide range of genres—from samba batucada performed at the Rio Carnival and bossa nova often played in cafes, to Brazilian music and even folklore, the mountain music of the regions surrounding the Andes—even though we’re all beginners, we play and dance to whatever we find appealing.Of course, it’s not all about music—we also enjoy Brazilian-style barbecue (churrasco) and other aspects of food culture! If you’re even slightly interested, please come visit our club room! We’re waiting for you!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Thursday / 7:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We, the Orquesta de Tango Waseda, are the only student-run Argentine tango ensemble in Japan—and the only one at Waseda University—currently performing Argentine tango with a lineup that includes violin, piano, double bass, viola, cello, flute, and bandoneon, as well as occasional guitar and vocals.We are an officially recognized club with a history spanning over 60 years, and we have produced many alumni. We are also an intercollegiate club that welcomes students from various universities, not just Waseda, and we operate regardless of university or year of study. Almost all of us are “tango beginners” who discovered Argentine tango after entering university, and we work together every day to improve our tango skills.We hold various performances, including our annual year-end recital, as well as appearances at the Waseda Festival and our own summer live shows. We’d love for you to come visit our clubroom or attend one of our live performances!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday / 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM / Student Union Building, B1F, Room B116

活動内容:
UBC is a Waseda University-recognized club dedicated to planning live music events, founded in 1953. "UBC" stands for "University Broadcasting Company," embodying the vision to "serve as a hub for disseminating information through various broadcasting media." Having pioneered initiatives such as "UBC-FM," the first student-run mini-FM station, and "UBC-TV," the first student-run campus mini-TV station, the club now primarily focuses on planning and organizing music events.
/
/In addition to "UBC-jam," a free live concert for 5,000 people held during the Waseda Festival, we have been expanding our scope of activities by launching new music events since 2007.
/
/We are committed to music that we, as listeners, truly believe is excellent, and we actively plan events that everyone can enjoy from the bottom of their hearts.
活動日時・場所: Every Friday / 6:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The High Society Orchestra was founded in 1955 as Waseda University’s only big band jazz club. Affectionately known as “High So,” we are widely recognized as a leading figure in the student big band jazz scene, boasting a rich tradition and a proven track record. Over our long history, we have produced numerous professional musicians.Our main activities include three weekly rehearsals, as well as our own live performances, joint concerts with bands from other universities, collaborative performances with professional musicians from Japan and abroad, and performances at parties and other events. Every March, all members come together to hold a recital, and in August, we compete in a national contest featuring student big bands from across the country. In addition, we have plenty of activities typical of college life, such as summer and winter training camps.On the other hand, performing alongside professional musicians is a unique feature of the High Society Orchestra, thanks to its long tradition and proven track record. We also frequently perform at private corporate parties, which is a great advantage for job hunting! You can gain a wealth of experiences that you wouldn’t get in a typical college life. Why not spend a one-of-a-kind college life with the High Society Orchestra—a life that’s about more than just making music?
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Thursday, and Friday / 4:30 PM / Basement 1, Student Union Building

名前: Waseda University New Orleans Jazz Club
活動内容: The Waseda University New Orleans Jazz Club, commonly known as "New Oli," is the only club in Japan that performs "New Orleans Jazz," a very old form of jazz that originated in New Orleans, Louisiana—often referred to as the birthplace of jazz. We typically form a band of about seven members to perform.Our main activities include bi-monthly club recitals, an annual recital held every December, and participation in annual events such as the Waseda Festival and the Inmon Festival. We also hold summer training camps and organize winter trips to New Orleans for interested members. Additionally, New Oli accepts performance requests from outside the university and performs at various venues upon request.Examples include performances in shopping districts and at party venues, as well as appearances at jazz festivals. As such, we are characterized by our wide range of performance opportunities both on and off campus, as well as our flexibility to perform anywhere.
活動日時・場所: Daily / As needed / Student Union Building, Room B116

活動内容: We, the Music Fan Club (MFC), are a traditional "12 Major Free Band System" band club established in 1959 that performs a wide range of music, from Western genres like soul, funk, blues, and rock to Japanese music.One of our major features is that many of our bands include a horn section with instruments like trumpets, saxophones, and trombones—sometimes growing to a total of nearly 15 members! We warmly welcome anyone who was in a school band in middle or high school, or anyone looking to start playing a new instrument. Our main activities include band practice, 7–8 major live performances per year, spring and summer training camps, and weekly club meetings. There are so many other fun events that we could go on forever! Rehearsals are held mainly at a music studio in Takadanobaba, with each band organizing its own schedule based on upcoming gigs. Don’t worry if you’re a beginner—we plan to offer lessons for each section as needed! We also have a large collection of records and a record player in our clubroom, so feel free to drop by whenever you have some free time! MFC is always looking for new members. Let’s immerse ourselves in music together and become “dancing fools”!

/We have our own fully equipped clubroom where we mainly practice. As for events, we hold about six live performances a year, plus a summer camp and a winter training camp. /
/We’re looking for members across a wide range of instruments, from vocals, backing vocals, guitar, bass, keyboard, and drums to trumpet, saxophone, trombone, flute, and percussion.We especially want as many people as possible to join the horn section. This is perfect for those with experience in the wind ensemble or light music clubs who want to “try something new at university,” those who just want to play rhythm guitar, or those who want to master the one-drop rhythm. Of course, beginners and those returning after a break are also very welcome! We’re truly the happiest and most fun band club at Waseda, so please feel free to come check us out!
活動日時・場所: Irregular days / Mainly after classes / Student Union Building

活動内容:
We are a student-led classical guitar club, which gives an opportunity to experience the joy of performing with others in an ensemble.

We are a classical guitar ensemble circle which started in 1962. We perform a wide range of works like classical music, pop songs, jazz, movie soundtracks, and so on. Since we give step-by- step lessons for beginners, you do not have to worry if you have never played any musical instruments. Not only concerts, but we have many fun events so you will enjoy your university life as well. Although performing in front of audience is challenging, but it's absolutely a fulfilling experience. If you are looking for a circle which gives you experiences of playing musical instruments, performing in front of audience, and making Japanese friends, please feel free to contact us. We look forward to hearing from you!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday日（5, 6period）, Saturday日（4, 5period）/Student Center
review_note: Prefilled from English text already present in the official description.

活動内容: The Waseda Folksong Society is a Waseda University-recognized band club founded in 1963. We primarily perform cover songs, playing music from genres such as alternative, indie, post-punk, and emo—regardless of whether the songs are Japanese or Western. However, we are basically open to any genre or style! We hold live performances about once a month, operating in a freestyle format where we form bands and gather members for each show.This means you don’t have to play with the same members every time; you can play the music you love, however you want, whenever you want. We warmly welcome anyone who wants to start playing an instrument after entering university. Waseda students are, of course, welcome, and students from other universities are also welcome to join! You can join at any time, and we welcome new members mid-semester, whether it’s during the first or second semester. We have a friendly, welcoming atmosphere and enjoy our club activities. Please come check us out!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday / 6:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
We are an officially recognized club of the Waseda University School of Science and Engineering that performs jazz in small ensembles of about 3 to 6 members. Our repertoire covers a wide range of genres, centered on modern jazz but also including Latin, bossa nova, and more.
/
/We hold live performances several times a year, and any member who wishes to participate can perform. Additionally, our dedicated club room in Room B121 of the Student Union Building is equipped with an upright piano, two double basses, and a drum set. We also own several wind instruments, such as saxophones and trumpets. Many of our members are beginners; most started playing jazz or even began learning an instrument for the first time in college.We warmly welcome both experienced musicians and those with no prior musical experience. In fact, there was even a term when the club president was someone who had started playing an instrument for the first time in college.
/
/We hold jam sessions at the Student Union Building several times a month. A jam session is where members present improvise and play songs of their choice together. Non-members are welcome to participate or simply observe. Details regarding the dates, times, and locations of these sessions are posted on our blog and other platforms.
活動日時・場所: Weekdays: Student Union Building B121 (Club Room); Weekends: Student Union Building B123, etc.

活動内容: We are a club officially recognized by the School of Science and Engineering that performs classical guitar in an ensemble format. The appeal of our club lies in our wide range of repertoire, from classical pieces performed by the entire club to popular songs accompanied by percussion instruments such as drums and bass. Since most new students joining the club are beginners, beginners are very welcome. Experienced guitarists can also utilize their skills while challenging themselves with other instruments.We hold joint concerts with clubs from other universities three times a year.In December, we hold our annual concert in a rented hall as the culmination of the year’s efforts. We practice in the Student Union Building, where our club room is located. Since we use the guitars provided in the club room for practice, there’s no need to buy your own. The club room also has acoustic guitars and drums, so many members enjoy trying their hand at singing while playing or forming bands. Since we’re officially recognized by the Faculty of Science and Engineering, most of our members are from that faculty, but we also have many students from the humanities, so please feel free to join us! We’re also looking forward to welcoming students in their second year and above!!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday, 5th–6th periods; Saturday, 4th–5th periods / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Chanson Research Club operates under the motto, “You can do whatever you want!” We are not a club that focuses solely on chanson. As times have changed, we have incorporated a variety of musical tastes, and we have grown into a club that prides itself on being the most all-encompassing at Waseda. We welcome members who play guitar, bass, vocals, drums, and keyboard, as well as wind instruments, so we have many members who previously belonged to the wind ensemble.Everyone loves practicing and working with equipment, and we take our music seriously! The genres we play range from pop, rock, and progressive metal to jazz fusion, anime songs, post-rock, math rock, Russian folk songs, and even Indian progressive rock—you can play whatever music you want! If you’ve never been able to find members who share your interests, the Chanson Research Society welcomes any kind of music!We also partner with the Chanson Research Clubs at Keio University, Japan Women’s University, and Shirayuri Women’s University, holding joint practices and live performances. With nearly 200 members across all clubs, we’re a massive music club—you’re sure to find someone who shares your interests! Come join the Chanson Research Club and fill your college life with music!!!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday and Saturday / Periods 3–7 / Student Union Building

活動内容:
Hey there, are you looking for a light music club at Waseda? Hello! With so many clubs to choose from, thank you for checking us out. KONA HAWAIIANS is just your average band club. We don’t play Hawaiian music!! Here are four key points about us!
/
/
/
/First, our “fixed band system.” This means you’ll be in the same band from the moment you join until you graduate, performing at live shows about once a month!! However, you’ll quickly become friends with everyone across all bands as the circle expands beyond your own group! This is a major strength that band clubs with a “free band system” don’t have.
/
/
/
/Second, it’s so cozy it feels like home. We don’t have the kind of wild drinking parties typical of other band clubs, and we don’t pressure anyone to drink. It’s a great atmosphere where you can hang out with the people you get along with.
/
/
/
/Third, our clubroom is “fully equipped” with gear, so you can practice solo or with your band there. Saving on studio fees is a huge plus!
/
/
/
/Finally, we’re open to all genres! From fans of Japanese rock to punk to Vocaloid… we have all kinds of people. Sometimes there are even people rapping (?)
/
/
/
/By the way, we hold about four live events a year where you can play your favorite artists’ songs—using the same “open band” system as our event-based live shows! You’re welcome to join as a member of another club too. Maybe KONA is the place for you to play your instrument…?
活動日時・場所: Anytime / Student Union Building B118 (Clubroom, equipment available)

活動内容: We are a traditional club that celebrated our 50th anniversary in 2016! We hold acoustic concerts featuring singer-songwriters once or twice a week, as well as monthly band-style live performances! In recent years, our membership has grown, making us the largest club on campus!Musical skill levels range from beginners to experts. While many members love Japanese rock, we have a diverse group of people who enjoy various genres, including Western music and Vocaloid! Even those picking up an instrument for the first time or wanting to try a new one are growing rapidly through their participation and thriving both within and outside the club! Want to do singer-songwriter performances but also try playing in a band? We’re waiting for ambitious people just like you! Please feel free to come check us out!
活動日時・場所: 1–2 times a week (irregular schedule) / 4:30 PM– / Student Union Building

活動内容: Celebrating its 50th anniversary this year, this is Waseda University’s only classical guitar ensemble. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced player, we practice guitar in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere. Our clubroom is located in Room E1115 of the Student Union Building, where members gather during free periods to play guitar and enjoy each other’s company. We pride ourselves on our extensive collection of sheet music, allowing us to perform not only classical pieces but also pop songs, Western music, Disney songs, and Ghibli songs.We warmly welcome Waseda students, students from other universities, and international students alike.We hold three retreats a year—the New Member Welcome Retreat, Summer Retreat, and Fall Intensive Retreat—where you can practice guitar and build friendships across grade levels! The Summer Retreat features an ensemble competition, which is always a lot of fun. We hold concerts twice a year, in June and November, renting a hall for the events. The June concert marks the first stage performance for new members, while the November regular concert serves as the culmination of the year’s efforts. Please feel free to stop by our clubroom sometime!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday and Friday / 4:30 PM – 7:30 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
Ensemble Ridol is a university-recognized club that performs in Waseda University’s only “pop orchestra” format. We operate with a unique lineup that combines a big band with violins, flutes, and clarinets. At our concerts, we perform a wide range of genres, from pop, jazz, and fusion to classical music, as well as video game and anime soundtracks.
[Key Features of Ridol]
"No Regular Membership System"... All members can participate in concerts from the very beginning. There are no auditions.
"Arrangements"... Because of our unique lineup, we create our own sheet music for the songs we want to play. Participation is voluntary—it’s not mandatory—and we hold arrangement workshops, so even beginners can give it a try!
"Beginners and Intercollegiate Students Welcome"… About 30% of our members are beginners. We’re a truly diverse group—from those who started music in college, to those picking up a new instrument, to experienced musicians who just want to keep things casual in college. With support from upperclassmen and a focus on simply enjoying music, you can practice at your own pace. Plus, many intercollegiate students from Keio University, Japan Women’s University, Tokyo Women’s University, and other schools participate!
"Plenty of Events"... In addition to three annual retreats and two concerts a year, we have plenty of other events, including private live shows just for members, watching the Waseda-Keio rivalry game, and fireworks festivals!
There’s only one requirement: a love of music. Why not enjoy a college life filled with music alongside wonderful friends?
活動日時・場所: 3 times a week (Mon, Thu, Sat) / Mon & Thu 7:00 PM – 9:30 PM, Sat 5:00 PM – 8:30 PM / Music Practice Room, B1F, Student Union Building

活動内容: We are the Waseda Utaou-kai, a band club officially recognized by the School of Science and Engineering!! We cover a wide variety of genres, including rock, punk, jazz, metal, idol music, anime songs, and Vocaloid—and we’re a club where even beginners can feel free to join!In fact, many of our upperclassmen didn’t even start playing an instrument until they entered university! Our annual activities include three “concerts” held at live houses in Tokyo, three “classroom live” performances held in the Student Union building, and three training camps. We hold both large and small live performances frequently, so even beginners can easily participate at their own pace! We use a “free band” system where we rearrange band members for each performance, so you can quickly become friends with various upperclassmen in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere!Plus, even if you’re busy or involved in other clubs, you can participate at your own pace!! Utarou-kai is an intercollegiate club; almost all of the male members are from Waseda University’s School of Science and Engineering, while the female members come from Waseda University’s School of Science and Engineering, Gakushuin Women’s College, Tokyo Kasei University, Japan Women’s University, and other schools. Since we have seniors from various departments, you can rest assured that we’ve got your back if you ever struggle with your studies (lol). You can continue participating even after graduating, so you can stay active for a long time! We’re a close-knit group, so please definitely consider joining us!
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Student Union Building, live music venues in Tokyo

活動内容:
The Waseda University Glee Club is a men’s chorus club with a 117-year history.
/
/At our regular concerts, we get to sing in front of an audience of 2,000 people!
/
/After every practice, we all go out to eat together. Freshmen get free meals!
/
/
/
/What sets us apart from other choirs is that we have many performance opportunities beyond our regular concerts.
/
/WaseGuri has plenty of opportunities to shine, such as at the Waseda-Keio rivalry game, entrance ceremonies, and graduation ceremonies.
/
/We also go on concert tours throughout Japan and abroad, and even have the chance to appear on TV shows like the Kohaku Uta Gassen!
/
/With professional instruction from opera singers, you’re sure to improve your singing!
/
/Of course, beginners are welcome too!
/
/We actively engage in exchanges with other universities and are planning joint concerts with other choirs.
/
/Our alumni are active in all kinds of industries, and we’ve produced many announcers and singers.
/
/
/
/For those who want to lead a fulfilling life every day!
/
/For those who want to experience things you can’t do in a typical student life!
/
/And, if you love to eat a lot, you’re more than welcome!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday / 5:00 PM / Student Union Building, Waseda Hoshien, etc.

活動内容:
All the members of WMC consists of Waseda University students.

You can experience various musical activities such as singing with accompaniment of orchestra, chorus lessons by a professional conductor,and practice from the basic of chorus with voice-trainers.

Whether you are a beginner or an experienced, we welcome anyone who loves to sing!

活動内容:
Waseda University Call Flügel is a men’s chorus founded in 1949 by Shin Sekiya and others. The name “Flügel” means “wings” in German.
Our main activities center around four major events: the Welcome Concert in April, the Ikarashi Concert in August, the Tokyo Choral Competition in September, and our solo concert in December.We welcome three conductors, all of whom are alumni of our group, and we practice diligently every day in preparation for each performance.
At the Ibaraki Concert and our solo concert, we perform a diverse repertoire of music from throughout history and around the world, and we actively undertake commissioned premieres, opening up new possibilities for men’s choral music.
We have won numerous Gold Prizes at competitions sponsored by The Asahi Shimbun.Most recently, in 2025, we won the Gold Prize and the NHK Award at the 78th All-Japan Choral Competition.
In addition, our activities are wide-ranging, including appearances at the Tokyo Choral Festival, on NHK’s “Let’s Sing the Set Pieces,” and performances with orchestras as members of the Shinyukai Choir.
We are currently accepting new members.
We will hold a welcome concert on Thursday, April 2!
If you are interested, please contact us via social media or email.

Conductors: Akira Shimizu, Yosuke Mashimo
Pianist: Hiroyuki Oda
Rehearsal Pianist: Hiroki Igawa
Voice Coach: Hiroyuki Yoshida
Email Inquiries: [email protected]

活動内容:
＼Welcome to Sōai, where we play hard, laugh a lot, and sing our hearts out!／
/
/
/
/Sōai is Waseda’s largest and finest mixed-voice intercollegiate choir, celebrating its 71st anniversary.
/
/We enjoy our daily activities with a diverse group of 50 members.
/
/One of Sōai’s biggest features is that we hold over 20 events a year!
/
/The highlights among these are the Summer Concert in August and the Annual Concert in December!
/
/This year’s Summer Concert is scheduled to take place in Mishima City, Shizuoka Prefecture. We’ll be performing on a collaborative stage with local high school students, and the spectacle created by such a large group is truly breathtaking! It’s sure to be a wonderful summer memory.
/
/For our annual concert, we invite an external instructor to provide professional guidance during rehearsals. A fantastic performance awaits—one that can only be achieved with the friends you’ve worked hard with all year long!!
/
/
/
/About 60% of Hayai’s members started singing in a choir in college. We perform a variety of repertoire, including choral pieces and pop songs, so both beginners and experienced singers can enjoy singing together.
/
/And… the appeal of Hayai isn’t just about the singing.
/
/We host plenty of events to deepen the bonds between members, such as the Two-Voice Social, Summer Concert Retreat, and post-practice dinners!
/
/
/
/Whether you love choral singing or just want a free meal!
/
/We’re recruiting members 365 days a year! ◎ Check our official social media for the latest updates!
/
/
/
/Why not join us and experience the best of Hayo-gaku life?
活動日時・場所:
Every Tuesday & Thursday / 6:55 PM – 8:35 PM / Student Union Building
/
/
/
/Every Saturday / 5:00 PM – 8:35 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容:
Street Corner Symphony is one of Japan’s oldest a cappella groups, with a history spanning over 30 years. We have produced numerous alumni who have gone on to professional careers, including members of TRY-TONE, Smooth Ace, AJI, and The Gospellers.
/
/We perform a wide variety of genres—from J-pop to jazz, Latin, and world music—using only the human voice.
/
/Among the many music clubs at Waseda, we believe we are the only one that covers such a broad range of genres. You’re sure to find music that suits your taste.
/
/
/
/The club hosts a variety of events throughout the year.
/
/Among them, our club concert—entirely created from scratch by our members—is truly spectacular.
/
/From the performers themselves to the lighting and sound equipment that enhances their performances, stage decorations, and even the program booklets, everything is planned and managed by our members.
/
/With over 300 attendees at every show, it has become our club’s flagship event.
/
/
/
/Our members also actively participate in national competitions held throughout Japan, including in the Kanto and Kansai regions.
/
/Why not join us in singing a cappella at a level that can compete on a national stage?
/
/All of us in the club are looking forward to meeting you!
活動日時・場所: Anytime / Student Union Building B1, 1st, 9th, 10th, and 11th floors
First Tuesday of the month / Periods 5 & 6 / Student Union Building; Third Saturday of the month / Period 2 / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are the Whistling Club "Koto Lip," a group that focuses primarily on ensemble performances! We meet twice a week at the Student Union Building on the Toyama Campus to practice whistling and enjoy chatting, creating a warm and welcoming atmosphere. Even if you have no musical experience or aren’t very good at whistling, if you’re looking for a place to belong, please come check us out! We welcome not only students from other universities but also international students depending on the year, so you can make friends with a diverse group of whistle enthusiasts! ♪ No qualifications are required to join, and there are no membership fees—we only collect a small fee each time we perform on stage, so even those on a tight budget can join with peace of mind!We’re expanding our activities beyond Waseda Festival to include local festivals like the Waseda Earth Thanksgiving Festival, concerts where whistlers from all over Japan gather, and, in recent years, even competing in world championships.Until recently, Waseda was the only university with a student whistle club, but in the past year or two, whistle clubs have sprung up all over the country, and we’ve started interacting with them! Of course, we don’t just whistle—we also hang out and have fun together, and when it comes to a welcoming atmosphere, we’re second to none. Please feel free to contact us and come check us out!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Thursday / 5:00 PM – 8:30 PM / Student Union Building

名前: 早稲田大学女声合唱団
活動内容: We are Waseda-Daigaku-Josei-Gassyodan (a.k.a “Wasejo”)! We are regularly getting coached from a conductor and a vocal coach. Having dinner after practice is one of the best part of our activities! Moreover, mobility is our strength. There are many events throughout the year, such as our own concert, a joint concert with other universities, an open-air concert, contests, training camps, and a year-end party (“Bonenkai”). Everyone who wants to sing in a female chorus is welcome: from any universities, in any grades, and any genders!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday日, Thursday日/18:55~21:10/on Waseda campus

活動内容:
We are the Tokorozawa branch of Waseda University Mixed Chorus. In Tokorozawa, we also have a clubroom where you can practice singing anytime. We welcome international students. We are looking forward to singing together!

We are the Tokorozawa branch of Waseda Mixed Chorus(WMC)♪ All the members of WMC consists of Waseda University students, and many of us are studying at Tokorozawa campus. We usually practice at Toyama campus, but we have a clubroom in Tokorozawa where you can practice singing anytime.

You can have various valuable experiences such as singing with an orchestra, chorus lessons by a professional conductor, and practicing one-on-one with voice-trainers.

You can go to training camps, talk with your friends in the clubroom, go out to eat after practice, hang out with club members on holidays... Each member of the group is enjoying their college life in our club!

Whether you are a beginner or an experienced, we welcome anyone who loves to sing!
