活動内容: The Photography Club’s main activities consist of eight annual photo exhibitions and workshops (club activities) held on weekdays from April to July and October to December, typically starting at 7:00 PM (taking into account the end of the fifth period).During these group activities, we conduct sessions ranging from instruction on how to use cameras, computers, and printers to darkroom workshops. We also organize photo shoots and spend time in the clubroom thoroughly reading photography books—activities designed so that everyone, from beginners to experienced members, can enjoy themselves and improve their skills. Some of these activities are unique to the Photography Club, made possible precisely because we have the necessary equipment and knowledgeable members. Additionally, we hold training camps twice a year in spring and summer to foster camaraderie within the club.Furthermore, the Photography Club interacts with photography clubs from other universities, such as at the Waseda-Keio Exhibition and the Six Universities Photography Exhibition, making it an attractive club for those who want to be exposed to diverse perspectives. At these exhibitions, we create, display, and critique photographic works based on the skills honed during our group activities. The clubroom is fully equipped with various supplies, including a display for retouching, Mac computers, a color printer capable of printing up to A3+ size, and film scanners.You also have unlimited access to the black-and-white darkroom. Participation in all activities is completely voluntary; you can just drop by whenever you feel like it. We warmly welcome everyone from beginners who haven’t bought a camera yet but love taking and viewing photos on their smartphones, to experienced photographers who already own a camera or were in a photography club in high school. Since we’re an intercollegiate club, we’re not limited to current students—anyone interested in “photography” is welcome!
活動日時・場所: April–July, October–December / (Weekdays) 7:00 PM– Student Union Building, etc. / (Weekends) Photo shoots

活動内容: The Art Research and Creation Society (commonly known as "Biken") is an officially recognized club at Waseda University, and as the name suggests, it is an art-focused club! In addition to individual projects for our regularly held exhibitions, we undertake all kinds of projects under the banner of "art," including designing the interiors and exteriors of retail stores, participating in Design Festa, and live painting at the Waseda Festival!From oil and watercolor painting to CG illustrations, paper cutouts, and collages—two-dimensional works—as well as clay modeling, knitting, and other three-dimensional pieces, and even video art at times. Members create works however they please!! It’s an open-participation club with a generally laid-back atmosphere. Members engage in creative activities at their own pace.We’re a group of people interested in art and creativity—whether you “enjoy making things,” “want to create with art supplies you’ve never used before,” or “simply want to enjoy the creative process”!
活動日時・場所: Every Monday and Thursday / Around 3:00 PM – 7:30 PM / Student Union Building (W402)

活動内容: The Waseda University Textile Research Society is a fashion club centered around Waseda University, founded in 1949. Guided by the philosophy of “What kind of ideas can students from a comprehensive university convey and influence through fashion?”, the society organizes fashion shows and installations. Currently, there are approximately 80 members, and many alumni have gone on to become designers.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Waseda University Calligraphy Club is the only officially recognized calligraphy club at Waseda University, boasting a tradition of over 60 years. Our main activities consist of practice sessions held every Wednesday and Saturday at the Student Union Building in preparation for the Spring Exhibition in May and the Inashoten Exhibition in winter, which is the largest student exhibition on campus.In addition, we offer a rich variety of “other activities” (shodo), including a camp during orientation week, a summer training camp lasting just under a week, and a ski camp where calligraphy is not practiced at all. We are also a member of the Tokyo Student Calligraphy Federation, an organization comprising calligraphy clubs from nine universities in Tokyo (Atomi Gakuen Women’s, Keio, Kokugakuin, Tokyo Women’s, Japan Women’s, Hosei, Meiji, Rikkyo, and Waseda), and we engage in exchanges with students from other universities.Furthermore, we maintain strong ties with our alumni. We visit exhibitions organized by them and invite them to our practice sessions to provide guidance, which greatly contributes to improving our calligraphy skills. Members can generally participate in activities according to their own schedules—such as classes or part-time jobs—and are free to come and go as they please during practice hours, so it is not uncommon for members to belong to multiple clubs. The club has a very relaxed atmosphere.
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday and Saturday / 1:00 PM – 6:00 PM / Student Union Building W402

活動内容: Our activities center around holding 4–5 photo exhibitions per year and two annual retreats in the spring and summer. In addition, once or twice a month, we all go out together to various photo spots to take pictures. On regular days, members who have time drop by the clubroom to chat, play games, print photos, and engage in other casual activities. There’s also a darkroom in front of the clubroom, where some niche members develop photos taken with film cameras…?For our photo exhibitions, we hold two or three of them at cafes around Waseda University. The rest are held in rooms on campus. We also occasionally receive requests to provide photography support for various university events. Members participate at their own pace on a daily basis, and through events like photo exhibitions and regular photo shoots, we help each other improve our photography skills.Finally, since our club name is “Riko-sha,” we often hear people say, “I thought only students from the School of Science and Engineering could join,” but that is absolutely not the case. Compared to other photography clubs, we simply have a slightly higher proportion of students from the School of Science and Engineering; there is no overall bias regarding university or faculty among our members. We warmly welcome beginners! Many of our members started photography in college! If you have even the slightest interest in photography, please feel free to contact us!
活動日時・場所: Irregular weekends / Student Union Building Room E217 & various photo spots

活動内容: The Waseda University Ancient Art Research Society is an art club with a 60-year tradition. Our main activity is visiting art museums in Tokyo once a month. Although our name includes “Ancient Art,” the exhibitions we visit are mostly not what is typically considered “ancient art,” such as Impressionist works. Please check our club blog for details. After museum visits, we hold a dinner gathering (optional) to foster interaction among members.What sets the Ancient Art Research Society apart from other art clubs is that we specialize exclusively in art appreciation. We warmly welcome everyone, whether you can’t draw or aren’t familiar with art. Since we focus solely on visits, we allocate our budget efficiently. By joining, you’ll be able to visit museums at a great value. In other words! We confidently recommend this club to anyone with even a passing interest in art. While our monthly visits form the core of our activities, we also respond to requests like, “Since we’re all here with similar interests, I want to socialize more!”We’re a flexible group that can quickly organize events like picnics in Shinjuku Gyoen or trips to fireworks festivals. We also have a club room where members can gather to get to know each other better. With many students from other universities in our group, the atmosphere is laid-back and relaxed. It’s hard to put this vibe into words, so we encourage you to join us for a trial visit—including a museum tour—to get a better sense of who we are. We’re always accepting trial visits, so please feel free to contact us anytime.
活動日時・場所: Once a month (usually on Sundays) at art museums in Tokyo. The club room is available for use at any time.

活動内容: The Inaho Kiln Pottery Club is the only pottery club at Waseda University, where members can create their own works from scratch. We perform every step of the pottery process in our clubroom: shaping clay using electric and foot-powered pottery wheels, applying glazes we mix ourselves, and firing the pieces in a kiln.Although kerosene kilns are more difficult to handle than electric kilns, they allow for a variety of firing methods and tend to produce works with unique character. Students join for various reasons—such as “I love making things,” “I want to create tableware for my own use,” or “I want to try something different from others at university”—and many members are beginners when they join. Under the philosophy of learning basic techniques from seniors while allowing each individual to create whatever they wish, members engage in their activities freely every day.The range of works members aim to create is extremely broad, spanning from traditional tea ceremony ware to everyday tableware and art objects. Three times a year, the club holds exhibitions both on and off campus to showcase their work. During the Waseda Festival, they host a “Pottery Market” to sell the ceramics made by club members. Additionally, in September, they hold a summer training camp at a facility in Mashiko City, Tochigi Prefecture, a renowned pottery-producing region.In addition to exhibitions and retreats, the club occasionally visits galleries and museums to view and study historical masterpieces and works by leading artists. In an ideal setting just a few minutes’ walk from campus, members use their free periods, after-school hours, and holidays to leisurely devote themselves to pottery making.
活動日時・場所: Monday–Sunday / 8:00 AM–10:00 PM / Building 29-3, Waseda Campus
Every Tuesday 1:00 PM – 8:00 PM, Every Friday 1:00 PM – 6:00 PM / Student Union Building W402

活動内容: Our activities center around four annual photography exhibitions: the “June Exhibition” in June, the “Newcomers Exhibition” in October, the “Waseda Festival Exhibition” in November, and the “Graduation Project Exhibition” in February. Members work on their own or collaborate to take photographs and provide critiques, dedicating themselves to creating their works.While most exhibitions are held on campus, the February Graduation Project Exhibition is held at an external gallery. In addition, we hold workshops to learn about photography, as well as many other events such as visiting photo exhibitions together and having barbecues. We hold two retreats—one during summer break and one during winter break—and members choose the destinations they wish to visit. Furthermore, since our clubroom is located inside the Student Union Building, members often drop by during free periods to engage in casual conversation.
活動日時・場所: Irregular days/As needed/Student Union Building E224

活動内容: We are a comprehensive arts and video production club officially recognized by the Faculty of Human Sciences. Founded in 2000, we engage in a wide range of creative activities as part of our comprehensive arts practice, including video production, illustration, music composition, and game development. Our members are primarily students from the Faculty of Human Sciences, and we typically hold our activities on the Tokorozawa Campus. Our current main activities include the irregular publication of collaborative zines, CDs, and cassettes, as well as "Movie-Sons"—events where we write scripts, shoot footage, and edit videos all within a 24-hour period.We distribute our zines, CDs, and other publications at events such as Wase-ket, Sun-Cri, and Comiket. The club members get along very well, and it has a very welcoming, family-like atmosphere. Many members are knowledgeable about anime, manga, and games. As a sister club to "lomotion," a toy camera club, we hold several joint events, such as hot spring retreats.
活動日時・場所: Every day

活動内容:
GIFT is a creative club that engages in creative activities covering virtually anything that can be expressed in print media, including novels, illustrations, poetry, manga, photography, and reviews.
/
/
/
/Twice a year, we publish our club magazine, *Sky Walk*. We also collaborate on themed projects proposed by members to create special "project books," and organize club-wide special events.We distribute and sell these publications at events such as the Tokorozawa Festival, Waseda Festival, and others. We also participate in events like Comiket and Suncre.
/
/
/
/In addition, we organize various social events, including retreats, Christmas parties, baking parties, and dinner gatherings.
/
/
/
/Beginners who have never tried creative activities before are also very welcome! Why not join us and create whatever you like, whenever you like?
活動日時・場所: Irregular schedule / Tokorozawa Campus

活動内容: The Shogi Club is a group where shogi enthusiasts gather to enjoy the game. Our goal for tournaments is to win the Oza Championship, held in the winter. We most recently won the championship in 2013. To achieve this goal, we gather in the club room regularly to play matches and study strategies, aiming to improve our skills. However, not all members are strong players. We also have many members who hold kyu ranks and beginners who started playing shogi in college.Because there are many strong players in the Shogi Club, quite a few members have significantly improved their skills by actively participating in club activities and learning extensively from the more experienced players. As for our specific activities, they vary by day. On weekdays, we gather in the clubroom between classes to play games with whoever is there.On Saturdays, we hold study sessions where we play two games under the rules commonly used in university tournaments: 30 minutes per player, with 60 seconds per move after time runs out. On Sundays, there are often university tournaments, and the entire club participates. Although we are active almost every day, participation is optional, so members are free to participate as they wish.We also hold a one-week training camp during long school breaks. During this period, members play an average of about 30 games each. The camp aims to foster camaraderie among members and improve their playing skills. We also occasionally hold exchange matches with shogi clubs from other universities. Since the Shogi Club is a club dedicated to enjoying shogi, it brings together people interested in the game regardless of their skill level. If you’re interested in shogi, please feel free to stop by the clubroom sometime.
活動日時・場所: Daily / Anytime / Student Union Building Club Room

活動内容: Does the tea ceremony—a symbol of Japanese culture—feel a bit out of reach to you? The Tea Ceremony Club (commonly known as “Chaken”!) is made up mostly of beginners, and since we start by learning how to handle the utensils one step at a time, newcomers can feel at ease! During weekday practice sessions, students teach each other, while on Saturdays, we receive direct instruction from instructors of the Omotesenke and Urasenke schools.In addition to our regular practice sessions, our activities include a summer camp packed with both practice and events, tea ceremonies where we showcase our skills to guests, research projects where we handcraft traditional Japanese sweets and tea bowls, and outreach activities where we are invited to tea ceremonies at other universities. Our weekday practice sessions are always open to the public, so if you’re even slightly interested in what we do, please feel free to drop by the tea room in the Student Union Building!
活動日時・場所: Twice a week on weekdays (days vary) and once on Saturdays / 12:10 PM–6:00 PM (times vary) / Student Union Building, Kiyose and Kagurazaka

活動内容: The Waseda Go Club holds practice sessions every Wednesday and Friday from 6:00 PM to 9:00 PM at the Shinjuku Go Center. These sessions are very lively, attracting not only current Waseda students but also students from other universities, alumni, and graduate students. Additionally, you can enjoy playing games in the club room at the Student Union Building even on days when there are no scheduled practice sessions.The Waseda Go Club is not just a club where members gather at a go center to play! We offer a wide variety of events that everyone can enjoy, regardless of skill level! We field a representative team in the General Division 1 of the Kanto League, held twice a year, and also participate in the concurrently held B League (exchange matches) with multiple teams. We also organize numerous other events, including biannual training camps and welcome events for new members.One of the club’s main attractions is the opportunity to build relationships not only with members from your own university but also with Go club members from other universities through tournaments and events. Experienced players are welcome, of course, but beginners are also very welcome! Our upperclassmen will be happy to teach you, so please come check out our activities! We look forward to seeing you!
活動日時・場所: Every Wednesday and Friday / 6:00 PM – 9:00 PM / Shinjuku Go Center

活動内容: This is a club dedicated to "competitive karuta," which has surged in popularity thanks to the manga, anime, and live-action film adaptation of "Chihayafuru" released last year! We typically hold practice sessions four times a week in the Japanese-style room at the Waseda Student Union Building or at external community centers, focusing on match-style drills. We also host fun events during long breaks, such as training camps and social gatherings. Experienced players are welcome, of course, but we also warmly welcome anyone who knows the Hyakunin Isshu—or even those who don’t!Our upperclassmen will kindly teach you everything from how to memorize the Hyakunin Isshu to the rules of karuta. Many of our current members started as beginners at university, but by practicing daily alongside experienced players, they’ve grown strong enough to produce numerous tournament winners! While the number of people playing karuta is still small, it’s a deeply engaging and enjoyable sport that anyone can get hooked on! If you’re even slightly interested, please feel free to come observe a practice session!
活動日時・場所: Every Tuesday, Thursday–Saturday / 1:00 PM–6:00 PM or 5:30 PM–9:30 PM / Student Union Building or Community Activity Center

活動内容:
A modern-day group of "banka" (rough-and-tumble) men who stride across Japan clad in school uniforms, square caps, and high geta sandals, with hand towels slung around their waists. This is a dojo for men.
/
/
/
/The Waseda Spirit Uplift Society is an officially recognized club at Waseda University that promotes personal growth through a variety of activities. The Society’s activities can be broadly divided into three categories.
/
/
/
/First, "Organizing the Honjo-Waseda 100-Kilometer Hike"; second, "Striding across the nation through summer training camps"; and third, "Planning and participating in various events." Commonly known as the "100-Hike," the Honjo-Waseda 100-Kilometer Hike celebrated its 60th anniversary in 2023.Currently attracting several hundred participants, the event features everyone in their own unique costumes as they walk at full speed for two days from Honjo Waseda in Saitama toward the Okuma Auditorium. The Koyo-kai summer training camp is an 11-day, 10-night trek across Japan for men only (commonly known as “Waseda Warriors”), where members deepen their bonds with one another and interact with local residents.Each member carries 30 go of rice on their back and walks relentlessly under the scorching summer sun, with a daily food budget limited to 100 yen per person. Among our various events is the “Fuji Jukai Party,” held at Christmas exclusively for our poor, single members. We also actively participate in the Waseda Festival and the Sports Festival.
/
/
/
/We welcome all who come and let go of those who leave. Come, all, to the Waseda Shrine!
/
/
/
/Gather now, Waseda Spirit Uplift Society!
活動日時・場所: Student Union Building E719 / Okuma Auditorium

名前: Waseda University School of Science and Engineering Go Club
活動内容: The Go and Shogi Club offers not only Go, Shogi, Mahjong, and playing cards, but also a wide variety of board games. You’ll naturally pick up the rules in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere. The Go and Shogi Club is where you can play whatever game you want. We are an officially recognized club of the School of Science and Engineering, with a clubroom on the 9th floor of the Student Union Building. We are also a traditional club celebrating our 50th anniversary. If you enjoy intellectual games, please come visit us!
活動日時・場所: Every day, anytime / Student Union Building E936

活動内容:
The Coffee Research Club boasts a history of over 50 years. We warmly welcome anyone who loves coffee and cafes, or even those with just a passing interest! Don’t worry if you can’t drink coffee or aren’t an expert—you’re still welcome.
/
/
/
/During our weekly Saturday afternoon sessions, we plan various activities in advance and engage in “research.” Specifically, we might compare coffee beans from different regions, hold hand-drip workshops, or even practice making café lattes with an espresso machine.On Monday and Wednesday afternoons, we enjoy coffee while working on assignments or just chatting.
/
/
/
/Plus, we have plenty of fun events lined up, including café tours, latte art workshops, retreats, and event booths!! You’re sure to make new café friends on our café tours! In preparation for the Waseda Festival in November, we plan to create our own original blend, practice hand-drip brewing, and develop original drinks.
/
/
/
/Whether you love coffee or not, please join the Coffee Research Club! Our unique and colorful “Coffee Club members” are waiting for you!
/
/
/
/For coffee lovers! Enjoy coffee with us.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday / 3:00 PM – 6:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We, the Waseda-Keio Game Support Club, are a club dedicated to supporting the prestigious Waseda-Keio Game. On the day of the game, we guide spectators and clean the area around Jingu Stadium. While we work hard before and after the game, the rest of the time we relax and hang out in our clubroom. On game day, after finishing our duties, we get to watch the game. Singing our school song, “Konpeki no Sora,” at Jingu Stadium is sure to be a memory you’ll cherish for a lifetime!Our members join for all sorts of reasons—not just because they love watching baseball, but also because they love Waseda, or because their upperclassmen were so kind. So even if you’re not interested in sports, that’s totally fine! We also interact with other clubs and help each other out with our respective activities. We get along really well with other clubs, and some of our members even belong to multiple clubs. In the spring and fall, we hold exchange events with Keio, so you can connect with people across university boundaries! We look forward to welcoming you!
活動日時・場所: Jingu Stadium / Student Union Building, 7th Floor, Room E704

活動内容: Table-top RPGs are analog games in which multiple players gather around a table, take on the roles of characters in a story, and advance the narrative through conversation (the Cthulhu Mythos TRPG, famous on video-sharing sites, is one such example).Based on a rulebook that outlines the story’s setting and game mechanics, one person—the “Game Master (GM)”—and 3 to 5 “players” who portray the characters work together to advance the game toward a final goal (such as solving a mystery or defeating an enemy). Since it is a game, there is some element of luck involved, such as the GM guiding the scenario and rolling dice, but what actions to take and what lines to say are entirely up to the players.Whether it’s moving others with cool lines, making them laugh with funny performances, or crafting detailed descriptions of the situation, each player showcases their strengths while collaborating with others to bring the story to life. In other words, players are simultaneously actors in an improvised play, screenwriters, and the audience—and experiencing this diverse range of fun is part of the appeal of TRPGs.We usually meet once a month on Sundays to enjoy TRPGs. Whether we win a hard-fought battle in a combat-based game or reach a moving conclusion in a mystery game by stumbling upon an unexpected solution, we’re all filled with a sense of accomplishment for having “created a great story” together. Beginners are more than welcome, so please come join us!
活動日時・場所: Once a month / Sundays / 10:30 AM – 6:00 PM / Discord

活動内容:
We usually hold recreational activities at cultural centers in Tokyo! We have plenty of fun events, including quizzes that both beginners and Disney enthusiasts can enjoy, Lightning Talk (LT) sessions where you can share what you love, and seasonal special events!
Once a month, we organize park visits on weekends!
We form groups based on your favorite genres, so you can watch parades, enjoy the food, or have fun with character meet-and-greets and attractions!
We also hold research presentations twice a year! These are co-hosted with Disney clubs and seminars from other universities, and we invite professors to attend.
Since we analyze Disney from all kinds of perspectives, this is highly recommended for those who want to seriously study Disney!
The number one unique event at D-Ken is the Maihama Walk! We actually walk all the way from Waseda University to Maihama! Let’s deepen our bonds with friends while sightseeing in Tokyo!
You’re free to choose which events to join, so you can participate at your own pace!
You only get one shot at college life—why not spend it with the wonderful friends you’ll meet through Disney?
Whether you’re a Disney newbie, a show parade fan, a character meet-and-greet fan, an attraction fan, a foodie, a BGS fan, a movie fan, a Pixar fan, a Marvel fan, a Star Wars fan, or a gaming fan—we’re waiting for you at the Waseda University Disney Research Club!
活動日時・場所: Once a week (day varies) / 6:30 PM / Cultural centers in Tokyo, Toyama Campus Cafeteria, Maihama

活動内容: The Abacus Club primarily focuses on participating in approximately 10 competitions per year and practicing for them. The club was established in 2009. Although our history is short, many of our alumni have excelled in numerous national competitions, including the All-Japan Abacus Championship, the country’s premier event. We practice during free periods between classes and hold practice sessions about twice a month on weekends.We put a lot of thought into our practice routines, brainstorming ideas together and offering each other advice to make our sessions as effective as possible. Moving forward, we aim not only to continue competing in tournaments but also to actively promote abacus skills both on and off campus, hoping to help increase the number of people who use the abacus, even if only slightly. Finally, the Abacus Club is currently recruiting new members. We warmly welcome current competitive players, those who want to take up the abacus again after entering university, and anyone who simply loves the abacus. Let’s have a blast together with the spirit of “One Bead, One Soul”!
活動日時・場所: Irregular days / Free periods between classes / Student Union Building

活動内容: We are a group of people who love 20th-century retro culture (music, manga, traditional coffee shops, idols, architecture, anime, vintage clothing, etc.), with a focus on the Showa and early Heisei eras. Our main activity is a weekly meeting, and on holidays and other days off, we visit retro-themed spots such as traditional coffee shops, record stores, and shopping districts.At past Waseda Festivals, we have staged recreations of Showa-era music variety shows and held photo sessions where participants could experience having their own "promai" (idol-style) photos taken. We also interact with people outside the university, so you’re sure to gain valuable experiences!
活動日時・場所: About once a week / 5th–6th periods / Student Union Building

名前: 早稲田大学韓国人学生会
活動内容:
Hello, this is Waseda University Korean Student Association.

There are about 800 Koreans in Waseda University, and it is our role of Waseda University Korean Student Association (WUKSA) to support students' school life and represent their voices.

Waseda University Korean Student Association started in 1947 and has steadily continued its diverse activities. Through cooperation with the student association's affiliated club and Waseda University Korea Alumni Association, we will try to support the lives of many Korean students and move on to the career path that students want in the future.

I will do my best to become Waseda University Korean Student Association, which always strives for about four years of college life. Thank you.

Our circle has fun interacting with international students through various events, trips and tours held more than once a month.Also, at the ?Japanese Class? held every Wednesday, you can learn about Japanese culture and the cultures of foreign students.In addition, they support international students through such means as volunteering classes and accompanying ward offices requested by universities.WIC's characteristic is that it not only spends time with foreign students , but also deepens relationships with foreign students through close exchanges in various ways! Members always gather in the semi-underground lounge of building 15 for two to five periods on weekdays, so if you are interested in WIC, please come! For more information, please visit Twitter and Instagram!

AIESEC is a not-for-profit and youth-run organization that engages and develops youth leadership with members in 100+ countries and territories worldwide.

AIESEC is a not-for-profit and youth-run organization with 30,000+ members in 100 countries and territories worldwide. We strive to achieve Peace & Fulfillment of Humankind's Potential by developing youth leadership potential through practical experiences. Collaborating with oversea branches and our alumni, we deliver and participate in international internships, volunteering opportunities, and online cross-cultural event.

活動内容: The Rainbow Club is a long-standing international exchange club founded in 1965 and is one of the largest clubs among the many at Waseda University. As the name “International Exchange” suggests, the Rainbow Club is a group where international students and Japanese students interact through various activities. We have students from the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia, as well as from Luxembourg, a country with a population of about 500,000.Additionally, as an inter-university club, Japanese members come not only from Waseda but from various other universities as well. The club’s main activities range from academic events—such as “Japan Study,” “World Study,” and “English Study,” where members teach each other about their respective cultures and slang—to social events like Halloween and Christmas parties. We also host sports events like soccer and basketball!
活動日時・場所: Irregular (about twice a week)/Various locations

活動内容:
We are the Waseda Taiwanese Student Association (WTSA), an officially recognized circle within Waseda University. Our circle consists of Waseda students from Taiwan. Whether you are an undergraduate, graduate, or CJL student, we aim to foster friendship and provide a platform for communication among Taiwanese students studying at Waseda. We are dedicated to assisting everyone with any issues related to daily life or school in Japan.

Currently, we organize activities approximately once a month. Our events include welcoming gatherings, picnics, overnight trips, and other activities that are beneficial to career planning, such as alumni career sharing sessions. We also collaborate with other clubs, Taiwanese student associations in other universities, and external organizations to facilitate various exchanges and experiences.

We warmly welcome all Taiwanese students studying abroad to join us. By becoming a part of Waseda Taiwan Student Association, you will have the opportunity to meet fellow Taiwanese students and engage in a vibrant and supportive community during your time in Waseda, whether you are a new student or have been in Tokyo for some time.

If you have any questions or are interested in WTSA, please feel free to contact us. We look forward to creating wonderful memories together at Waseda.
活動日時・場所: at least once a month / At least once every month

名前: Waseda University Central Asia Study Group
活動内容: We travel to Kazakhstan during winter break to participate in student exchanges and homestays. Trips to Kazakhstan can be arranged based on individual interests.You can witness global welfare conditions firsthand at social welfare facilities and senior care centers. It’s not just about learning—you can challenge yourself in various ways. You can also fully enjoy winter sports like skiing and skating. Additionally, international students from Kazakhstan will welcome you there, allowing you to reunite with friends you made in Japan and foster wonderful Japan-Kazakhstan exchanges. You can expect to gain valuable learning experiences that go beyond a typical trip or study abroad program.
活動日時・場所: Every Monday / 4:00 PM / Building 101

活動内容: The Children’s Culture Research Society is a long-standing, Waseda University-recognized children’s volunteer club founded in 1945. Our main activities are “Children’s Volunteering” and “Puppet Theater.” For “Children’s Volunteering,” we assist as support staff at events held at children’s centers near Waseda. We prepare crafts and games ourselves and play with the children. For “Puppet Theater,” we primarily hold performances during long school breaks.After performances, we let the children play with the puppets and even share a meal with them. Furthermore, everything—from the puppets and scripts to the stage—is handmade. While most members are beginners in both theater and puppet-making at first, our kind upperclassmen provide gentle guidance, so please feel at ease. Both programs are aimed at children from preschool age through the early elementary grades, and interacting with them feels like receiving a boost of energy! We hold meetings once a week in a cozy, welcoming atmosphere.With a small group and a relaxed atmosphere, you’ll easily get to know the other members. Everyone is welcome, regardless of university or year! Let’s enjoy interacting with the children together!
活動日時・場所: Every other Monday and Thursday / 5:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: We have been conducting afforestation activities and community outreach in Tanohata Village, Iwate Prefecture, for over 50 years. Tanohata Village has a population of approximately 3,500. During our training camps, we live communally in Waseda University dormitories. We use firewood we’ve chopped ourselves, cook rice in a traditional pot, and light the fire for the bath using that same wood.For our afforestation activities, we perform thinning and pruning on the two mountains we own. For community engagement, we assist with primary industries such as agriculture, forestry, and ranching, and participate in local festivals. When in Tokyo, we hold weekly meetings to prepare for the next retreat and discuss various events. We also participate in the Waseda Festival, the Inmon Festival, and environmental contests. Whether in Tokyo or Iwate, this is a club where we can do what we want to do through our own efforts.
活動日時・場所: Once a week / 6:00 PM / Student Union Building

活動内容: The Himawari Children’s Club partners with four elementary schools in Meguro Ward and is a club that interacts with children attending special needs classes at each school.The program is open to students in grades 1 through 6. Every Saturday, two to three student volunteers are assigned to each child to play with them at a park. Additionally, the club organizes Sunday field trips in May, July, October, November, December, and March, taking the children to places like Kasai Rinkai Park or other parks that offer a change of scenery.In the summer, there is also a 2-night, 3-day camp. For each excursion, a student-led “Excursion Planning Committee” is formed, and preparations begin approximately two months before the event. Through activities such as making souvenirs and planning recreational games, the students also get to know each other better. The Himawari Children’s Club is a group that offers a rare and valuable opportunity to interact with many children.
活動日時・場所: Every Saturday / 1:00 PM – 6:00 PM / Parks in Meguro Ward

活動内容: Every Sunday, the Ikebukuro Children’s Club borrows a primary school in Ikebukuro to play and have fun with the children who belong to the club. We play a variety of games, such as soccer and tag. We also plan many events, including seasonal hikes and camping trips.Every Thursday, we discuss what games to play on Sundays, where to go hiking, and what activities to hold during camping trips. Since these discussions shape the club’s activities, everyone works very hard. Furthermore, we hold training camps in the spring and summer. During these camps, we brainstorm ideas on how to improve the club, borrow a gymnasium for recreational activities, and have social gatherings in the evenings—all while having a great time.
活動日時・場所: Every Sunday 9:00 AM–1:00 PM / Every Thursday 6:00 PM–9:00 PM

活動内容: Hello! The Aozora Children’s Club is a children’s volunteer group that meets at local parks. We primarily work with elementary school students living in the area surrounding the university. Our main activity is our regular Saturday meeting. During these sessions, we have fun playing games like “Tail Tag,” dodgeball, and our club’s original games at the park! In addition to our regular meetings, we hold seasonal events with the children, including field trips in spring and fall, a summer camp, and a sports day in winter!We also hold numerous events just for students, where we enjoy a friendly and lively atmosphere! Students plan and organize every event from scratch. There is nothing more rewarding than seeing the children have fun and express their joy through the events we’ve created together. Not only are we uplifted by the children’s cuteness and energy, but being able to witness their growth up close is a unique feature of our club!
活動日時・場所: Every Saturday / 1:30 PM – 4:30 PM / A park near the university

活動内容: Shinjuku Children’s Club KIDS is a volunteer group established in 1982. Every Saturday afternoon, we play with children from special education classes at a meeting room or park near Waseda University. Two student leaders plan the day’s theme and activities. There’s plenty of free time, and we’re always uplifted by these energetic and adorable kids! We also host a wide variety of events where you can play with the children, including spring field trips, summer camps (two days and one night), fall field trips, Christmas parties, and graduation ceremonies. We also have plenty of events just for students, such as orientation retreats, fireworks festivals, BBQs, and summer camps. Our biggest selling point is the club’s atmosphere. Everyone is welcome, regardless of university or year! Please come and try it out!
活動日時・場所: Every Saturday / 12:00 PM – 7:00 PM / Toyama Park

活動内容: Short for Human-Volunteer, we’re man-vo.! We conduct welfare-related volunteer work in the Tokorozawa area with the goal of “interacting with people”! Through our volunteer work, we deepen our daily connections by cooking and playing sports with people with intellectual disabilities, as well as studying and playing with children and the elderly. We also collaborate with the Tokorozawa City Board of Education and local volunteer groups to support the operation of community events.Volunteering is never mandatory. You can participate at your own pace whenever you have time. In addition to volunteering, we hold events like class reunions and training camps, so you’ll quickly become friends with upperclassmen and students from other universities. Even if you’re unsure how to interact with people with disabilities or have never volunteered before, don’t worry! Experienced upperclassmen will kindly support you. Why not take this opportunity to get involved in the world of social welfare? Please feel free to contact us!
活動日時・場所: Varies by activity (mainly Saturdays and Sundays)

活動内容: Kankyo Rodriguez is Waseda University’s largest officially recognized environmental volunteer club, founded in 1997. Hearing the name might make you think, “Do I need to be an environmental expert to join?” but that’s not the case at all. Our members are diverse, ranging from those with a strong interest in the environment to those who first became interested after entering university. What we value most is “finding what you can do while having fun.” Our activities are divided into six projects: “Satoyama,” “Ocean,”“Community Revitalization,” “Education,” “Product Development,” and “Plastic.” We organize nature experiences, workshops, and the creation of recycled products. Each project group meets about once a week, and all groups have a warm, welcoming atmosphere. One of the group’s attractions is the opportunity to make friends across different departments and grades. Even if you aren’t an expert on the environment, you’re more than welcome if you think it sounds interesting! Whether you want to try something new or find like-minded friends, you’re sure to find a comfortable place here.

活動内容: BBS is one of the organizations cooperating with the Probation and Parole Service (Ministry of Justice), engaged in activities related to rehabilitation and juvenile delinquency prevention. Our club is the largest BBS group in the Kanto region and, unusually for a regional chapter, is an inter-university club consisting solely of students! We volunteer at child guidance centers and child welfare facilities, acting as older siblings to children facing various challenges—listening to their stories and helping them with their studies.Currently, we have students from various universities, primarily Waseda University and Toyo University! While students majoring in law, psychology, and education are prominent, we also have students in STEM fields as well as those majoring in politics and economics. Our members range from freshmen to graduate students! Having overcome the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, we have recently expanded our activities to include support for students who are not attending school. We are always looking for motivated students interested in rehabilitation and child welfare! Why not join us?

活動内容: Wase Neko is a club engaged in volunteer activities focused on community cat care. Our goal is to reduce the inconvenience caused to local residents by stray cats—such as feces, urine, and mating season vocalizations—and we carry out our activities with the understanding and cooperation of university staff, Shinjuku Ward Public Health Center staff, and local residents.Our daily activities primarily involve feeding the cats. Every day during the fifth class period, we feed the community cats that appear along a designated route on the main campus.We also keep daily records of our activities in a notebook and hold monthly meetings to exchange information and review our progress. Additionally, although on an irregular basis, we strive to raise awareness of our community cat activities by cooperating with interviews from newspapers and TV stations, and we participate in discussions aimed at improving our activities through presentations at symposiums. We welcome inquiries about our activities or requests to observe our work.
活動日時・場所: Daily / 4:30 PM – 6:00 PM / Student Union Building, Main Campus

活動内容:
We engage in “Waseda community development” by interacting with local shop owners and children through the planning and operation of events!
We participate in many events every month, such as local festivals and events at elementary schools.
We also take part in Waseda’s three major festivals: “Waseda Festival,” “Earth Appreciation Festival,” and “Inmon Festival.”
In addition, we publish “Waseda Town Magazine,” a print media outlet that showcases the charm of Waseda, and distribute it in racks at Waseda Station on the Tozai Line and at various shops throughout Waseda.
Our regular meeting every Wednesday during 5th period has a cozy, welcoming atmosphere, so you’ll make friends right away! We also have plenty of social activities among members.
Anyone is welcome—whether you’re even slightly interested in volunteering, love working with children, want to help others, or simply want to learn more about the Waseda neighborhood!

活動内容: “Why is there no rice paddy at Waseda, even though the name includes ‘Wase’ (rice)?” This simple question led to the founding of our Nōraku Juku, and we have been actively engaged in a wide range of activities centered around “Waseden” in Okuma Garden. Nearly 20 years have passed since our founding, and today, in addition to rice cultivation at Waseden, we engage in various other activities.Our main activity is managing the rice paddies and vegetable fields in Okuma Garden. We do this during our weekday lunch breaks, and after we finish, members who have no classes in the third period often go out for “Waseda-meshi” (Waseda-style meals) together. We also have exchanges with Waseda Kindergarten and the Step Class in Sumida Ward, where we volunteer to provide children with opportunities to experience nature. We sometimes plant and harvest rice together, or go crayfish fishing.On weekends, we regularly interact with local farmers. When we visit farms in Tokorozawa City or Kasumigaura City, we not only get to experience farming firsthand but also enjoy delicious meals. We also organize a variety of events—ranging from those with little agricultural focus to more intensive ones—so you can enjoy our activities all year round! We will continue our activities under the motto: “Enjoy farming and reflect on farming.”
活動日時・場所: Weekdays at noon / Irregular holidays / Okuma Garden, etc.

活動内容: Hello. We are the DOORS Japan-Vietnam Exchange Project. Our activities are centered on two main pillars: providing scholarship support for children in Vietnam and organizing exchange events. We travel to Vietnam twice a year, for two weeks each time, during the spring and summer long vacations.In Japan, to raise funds for scholarships, we participate in events like the Waseda Festival to sell Vietnamese goods. We also hold monthly events for foreign residents, primarily Vietnamese people. We’re a close-knit club where not only peers but also seniors and juniors get along very well! Many members join in their second or third year, so we welcome anyone interested in overseas volunteering, Southeast Asia, cross-cultural exchange, or event planning! Please come to one of our meetings.

活動内容: Student NGO EST is a hands-on volunteer group that provides educational support and cultural exchange to children in the Philippines, guided by the motto, “Providing the maximum support that only students can offer.” Every year during the summer break, we travel to the Philippines to engage directly with children through homestays, local games, and simple lessons, fostering hope and possibilities for their future.In our classes, we provide a space for children to think and learn together on themes such as hygiene, history, and local traditional culture, creating opportunities for them to realize their dreams. Furthermore, by taking the lead in everything from planning to implementation, students cultivate an international perspective, leadership skills, and problem-solving abilities, making this an excellent opportunity to gain experience that will be useful in the real world. In addition, we offer a variety of events throughout the year, including training camps, ensuring that our activities are not only meaningful but also fun.To all motivated students: Why not join EST and support the Philippines as we work together to shape the future?

名前: Waseda University Disaster Prevention Education Support Association WASEND
活動内容: The Waseda University Disaster Prevention Education Support Group (WASEND) was established in response to the 2004 earthquake off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia.Currently, approximately 80 members conduct disaster prevention education activities not only within Japan but also for children in Indonesia and the Philippines. Based on thorough on-site surveys conducted with local university students and experts, we implement lessons tailored to each region. By incorporating hands-on activities using experimental equipment, we aim to raise children’s awareness of disaster prevention.In addition, we actively participate in local disaster prevention festivals. WASEND also produces disaster prevention picture books; to date, we have published two titles: “The Story of Yoshihama’s Dislike” and “I Am Not Alone: Wahyu and the Great Tsunami That Struck Aceh.” We offer both Japanese/English and Indonesian versions and distribute them to elementary school students in Japan and abroad.

活動内容: The Matsudai region of Tokamachi City, Niigata Prefecture, is surrounded by abundant nature and is one of Japan’s heaviest snowfall areas, sometimes recording 3–4 meters of snow in winter. In recent years, population decline has led to serious issues of depopulation and an aging population, and there are many “marginal villages” in this region. We conduct our activities primarily in the Gamo settlement within the Matsudai region.Our main activities include weekly meetings, monthly on-site activities, the Matsudai Juku Jr. educational support program, and the Snow Country Experience Program. Through on-site activities such as participating in local events and maintaining the environment, we interact with local residents while striving to preserve the region’s rich natural environment, beautiful terraced rice fields, and local cultural traditions like village festivals.Matsushiro Juku Jr. is a project that provides educational support during summer vacation for elementary and junior high school students living in the Matsushiro region, alongside general participants. The Snow Country Experience Project is a program that recruits general participants to experience life in a snowy region through activities such as snow shoveling and homestays. Both projects aim to introduce general participants to the charms of Matsushiro, and we actively participate in university events and other occasions to promote Matsushiro’s appeal to a wider audience.We engage in various activities with the goal of sharing joy through interaction with local residents and contributing to regional revitalization by leveraging our status as university students.
活動日時・場所: Every Friday / 6:30 PM / WAVOC

名前: 日本コリア未来プロジェクト
活動内容:
Japan & Korea Future Project?, also known as ?Nikkori?, is a student club whose aim is to contribute to a brighter future for Japanese-Korean relationships. Our motto is: ?Realize an individual’s abilities, think deep, and make actions?. We mainly organize four types of activities.

Through presentations and group discussions on topics regarding Korea (e.g. territorial disputes, comfort women issues, and nuclear issues), we try to deepen our understandings on the Korean Peninsula.

We regularly visit Korea University, located in the city of Kodaira, where we join their meetings and events. Also, we organize various kinds of activities and with the involvement of Korea University's students. Through this, we can acquire a better insight of North Korea.

We frequently hold fun events including collaborations with other organizations such as the Waseda Korean Students Association, where you are able to meet new people and have memorable experiences.

During the summer, we make a short trip to a village in the DMZ (Demilitarized Zone) Area, and we volunteer to help local farmers.//////

?NIkkori? believes that having better and deep communication and understanding between Japanese and Korean people in our generation is the key to overcome existing negative images that we have on each other’s countries.

Nikkori is the future for better relations between Japan and the two Koreas. We offer great opportunities for you to find your strengths and meet awesome people.

Doing residential construction volunteering activity overseas! Largest volunteer circle in Waseda University with a variety of experiences!

We are the Waseda University student branch of the international NGO Habitat for Humanity. Our main activity is volunteer work for building houses in developing countries during long vacations. In addition to overseas activities, we also organize teams to volunteer in various areas in Japan during long vacations, and regularly support agriculture and pick up trash in the suburbs of Tokyo. We also hold weekly meetings to discuss social issues and provide opportunities to raise volunteer awareness through presentations by hosts and discussions among participating members. We are also able to interact with other universities that share the same parent organization as our circle listed above, and we are able to exchange ideas and opinions with many people. Not limited to volunteer activities, we also regularly hold events such as a Christmas party, BBQ, and other recreational activities, and camps, so you can enjoy the fun that only university students can have! The atmosphere of the circle as a whole is very friendly and fun, regardless of grade or gender. The main feature of the circle is that everyone is kind and cozy, welcoming everyone with a smile no matter who and when they come. Because we can give our all in both learning and playing, we are able to meet the needs of those who want to try something new! Join WHABITAT and let's make your college life more fulfilling!

名前: Laos School Construction and Educational Support Project ~Soon~
活動内容: Guided by our philosophy of “thinking and feeling together,” we conduct educational support activities for two weeks during winter break in the villages of Non Vien and Non Sa in Champasak District, southern Laos.Due to the impact of the coronavirus, we were unable to travel for two years, but last year we traveled to the site for the first time in three years to carry out our activities. The Activities Group planned a sports day centered on the theme of “teamwork,” while the Lower Grade Group addressed environmental issues. Additionally, the Upper Grade Group conducted education on World Heritage sites. In addition to classes, we engaged in teacher exchanges and home visits, allowing us to experience Laotian culture firsthand.Within Japan, we host exchange events with international students from Laos, teach classes at junior high and high schools, and participate in the Waseda Festival. With no barriers between upperclassmen and underclassmen and a warm, welcoming atmosphere, this is a club where new members’ ideas are welcomed and where you can become deeply involved from your very first year. We look forward to welcoming you! ♪

活動内容:
We were founded based on the connection between Waseda University and Kesennuma City, Miyagi Prefecture, immediately following the Great East Japan Earthquake, and have been continuously engaged in reconstruction support activities ever since. Currently, we visit the area once every two months to conduct study tours, provide academic support, and assist with events. The “Kesennuma Minato Festival” held in August is a major event where we help with operations while also participating as dancers to liven up the festival.Thirteen years after the disaster, local conditions and needs have changed, and our activities—which began with debris removal—continue to evolve. We are actively working in Tokyo to help Kesennuma become a more vibrant and energetic city by sharing not only what Kesennuma was like at the time of the disaster but also its current charms. Additionally, since 2020, we have been disseminating information about Kesennuma through blogs and the distribution of free newspapers, creating opportunities for more people than ever to learn about the city.As time has passed since the disaster and memories begin to fade, the number of volunteers working on the ground has also decreased. This may be inevitable. However, there are still many people in the area who need us and who find joy in our activities. We will continue to respond to the voices of these people. Anyone who is even slightly interested in volunteering, wants to visit Tohoku, or would like to learn more about the disaster is more than welcome to join us.

活動内容:
"I'm interested in volunteering, but I don't know exactly what I want to do..." "I want to try out all kinds of volunteer work!" If you're thinking along these lines, we highly recommend Waseda University POST! POST is an officially recognized volunteer club characterized by its all-encompassing approach—you can do any kind of volunteer work here. Our main activities include social gatherings with the elderly, support activities at after-school programs, litter cleanup, agricultural experience camps during long school breaks, and various one-time volunteer events such as event management.Through volunteering, you can interact with people of all ages, from children to the elderly. Our members get along very well, making this a very welcoming club!
Now, more than ever, as the global pandemic has weakened human connections, we have come to realize the importance of these bonds and ways of connecting that were previously unseen. Waseda University POST offers the opportunity to experience this firsthand through volunteering—not only by cherishing the connections in our daily lives, but also by reaching out to others and truly feeling the warmth of human connection.
Volunteering is never a one-way street; it is a two-way connection with others. Through this, we can accept others and find joy in simply being together in the same space. We value the connections that arise specifically from working as a group, and that is why we volunteer.

名前: 早稲田大学いちご大福研究会
活動内容:
We are the first circle in Japan that specializes in strawberry Daifuku. Founded in 2016, it was launched with the aim of spreading the charm of strawberry Daifuku to the world. People have different reasons for joining the club, such as liking strawberry Daifuku, liking strawberries, liking sweets, liking cooking, wanting to develop products, and the circle name is interesting. One of our members said, “I don't like strawberries, but I joined the club because it sounded interesting”. Since it is an intercollegiate circle, there are many students from other universities, and everyone is engaged in activities in a friendly atmosphere. The main activities are trial production of Daifuku for the sale of the circle's original products and comparison of Daifuku, especially strawberry Daifuku. We also have summer camps, stalls at the Waseda Festival, and day trips.

Since 2022, our activities have focused on product development. After many prototypes, in April 2023, we finally decided to sell a product in collaboration with “Chacha Kobo” located in Nishi-waseda. The “Unwrapped Strawberry Daifuku” was developed to match the tea of Chacha Kobo, and pink and white mochi (rice cake) was made into the shape of cherry blossoms in time for the spring selling season. The mochi is topped with fresh cream, anko (red bean paste) cream, and strawberries to make it look pretty. It was so well received that we sold take-out at our Asakusa store in May.

If you are interested in product development, like strawberry Daifuku, or want to learn more about Daifuku, any reason is welcome.

活動内容: Any Waseda student from outside Tokyo can join our events anytime! The Regional Student Clubs (○○ Student Inmonkai) are officially recognized clubs established to bring together Waseda students with ties to specific prefectures (hometowns, high schools, etc.) and foster camaraderie. There are no rules other than strengthening the bonds of our shared hometowns!Each Student Inmonkai conducts unique activities, such as going out for drinks together, participating in local festivals, or holding training camps. With nearly 30 Student Inmonkai chapters nationwide—from Hokkaido to Okinawa—many Waseda students from regions outside Tokyo, Kanagawa, and Saitama belong to these groups.The National Federation of Waseda Student Associations (Zensoren), as the umbrella organization for the Student Inmon-kai, engages in a wide range of activities. These include planning and organizing joint social gatherings and events for the Student Inmon-kai, as well as managing official Waseda University Sports Festival events like the “Tokyo Hike,” the spring “New Student Welcome Party,” and the fall “Inmon Hometown Party.”This is a club where you can meet many friends from different faculties and grades! Furthermore, even with people you’re meeting for the first time, you already share the irreplaceable bond of being from the same hometown. Please feel free to join us for a Student Inmonkai or Zensoren activity sometime. *Please note that not all Student Inmonkai are listed in this club introduction. If you’re wondering, “Is there a Student Inmonkai for my hometown?” please contact Zensoren.

活動内容:
The Yamanashi Student Inmonkai works daily to create a welcoming space for Waseda students from Yamanashi Prefecture. We usually gather at "Printan," a café near the Waseda campus, to enjoy lunch together, occasionally hold drinking parties, organize retreats during long breaks, or meet up in Kofu... all while keeping things laid-back.
/
/We also have strong ties with student Inmonkai chapters from other prefectures and alumni, and with our long-standing traditions, there are plenty of opportunities to expand your network and social circle. We participate in the Waseda University Regional Exchange Forum, held annually in Yamanashi Prefecture, as well as the Alumni Association branch general meetings.
/
/I’m sure you’ve all left Yamanashi behind and made many new friends at Waseda. But why not get together and have a lively chat about Yamanashi Prefecture, the home of your hearts?Just being from the same hometown creates a sense of closeness and solidarity, regardless of your major, year, or hobbies—it’s a really warm and welcoming club. Many members are also active in other clubs.
/
/We’re always looking for new members, no matter your year! First-years are a given, but we also welcome fourth- and fifth-years, as well as graduate students! So, please come check us out—even just once! Let’s hang out. We’re always waiting for you.
